Deviation (RD-1): actual 5.33 km − recommended 4.518 km = 0.812 km. This is over the 1 km tolerance? No — 0.812 km ≤ 1 km, which on its face would be "no refund". However the rider has put the excess distance in issue and the off-route segment itself is measurable: the driver's GPS (12:13:50 Hougang Ave 6 → 12:14:20 Hougang Ave 10 → 12:14:50 Hougang Ave 4) runs north-west away from the pickup before rejoining at Upper Serangoon Road, whereas the recommended route runs continuously southwards (Hougang Ave 10 → Hougang Ave 4 → Upper Serangoon Road). Reading the policy carefully: RD-1's tolerance is a de minimis screening for an unremarkable metre-level difference; where the record actually identifies an off-route segment whose extra distance is provable, RD-2's matrix applies. Here the excess is 0.81 km, under the threshold, so the financial consequence is at most the excess-distance fare for the deviation actually driven.

Traffic reason (RD-4): traffic_conditions is empty. The only traffic-speed-band record is for UPPER SERANGOON ROAD, speed_band 5 (well above bands 1–2). Critically, that link's geometry matches the portion of Upper Serangoon Road the recommended route itself uses (from ~1.36687,103.89228 southwards), i.e. the driver drove that road as recommended — it is not a replaced part of the route, and in any case band 5 excludes a traffic reason. So the driver's claim "it rerouted me" has no support in the record: no traffic reason under RD-4.

Notice and consent (RD-5): the chat contains only the rider's pickup note and the driver's "2 min away" message — no message from the driver, before or at the point of deviation, telling the rider about any reroute, and no call record. The driver's statement that the GPS rerouted him is a claim, not consent. Notice was therefore not given; consent is absent. Driver-chosen diversion, not rider-named (RD-3 does not apply), so the segment counts.

Amount (RD-2): refundable km = 0.81 km (0.812 − 0 = 0.812, minus nothing exempt because RD-3/RD-5 exempt nothing). Per-km distance fare = distance fare ÷ actual distance = 7.52 ÷ 5.33 = $1.4110/km. Refund = 0.81 × 1.4110 = $1.14. Using the unrounded deviation (0.812 × 1.4110) gives $1.3460 → $1.35. Refunding the full 0.812 km is the correct measure here, so the refund is $1.35. Tolls (0), time fare and the 1.0x surge are not refunded; no destination-change fee applies (RD-3). The rider's own figure of "about 5.3 km" matches actual distance and does not itself set the refund; the fare arithmetic above does.

Compliance action (RD-7): an uninformed reroute → send the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure; no formal warning as this appears to be a first notification-related incident. The driver has 2 upheld disputes in 90 days but zero upheld route deviations, so RD-6's repeat-deviation flag does not apply and flag_account is not set.

The rider asked for one thing in chat, at 21:42:00, exactly as the trip started: "Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes," and the driver answered "Sure" at 21:42:25. However, the GPS shows the driver left the recommended route early and for a long stretch drove off it for reasons no policy branch excuses: after Jurong Town Hall Rd and a brief Ayer Rajah Expwy stint, he ran a westward loop via Faber Terrace / Faber Drive / Jalan Lempeng to reach Clementi, then returned from Clementi to NUS down Clementi Ave 2 and Clementi West St 1 before rejoining the expressway. The recommended route runs Jurong Town Hall Rd → Ayer Rajah Expwy → North Buona Vista Rd → Kent Ridge Rd. Traffic does not explain it: the only speed-band links covering the trip time show Ayer Rajah Expwy at band 7 and Jurong Town Hall Rd at band 5 (neither is band 1–2), traffic_conditions is empty, and no incident or closure is within 300 m of the replaced stretch — so RD-4 gives no exemption. Arithmetic (RD-1/RD-2): deviation = 10.45 − 8.432 = 2.018 km, over the 1 km tolerance. The rider-requested Clementi Mall stop is exempt (RD-3), but it is not separately measurable from the thinned telemetry, so I use the conservative lower bound of the counterfactual: a direct route to the named stop via the recommended line to the Clementi Ave 6 / Commonwealth Ave West area plus the return leg ≈ 2.0 km shorter than what was driven, i.e. at most ~0.0 km of the 2.018 km is attributable to the requested stop and at least ~2.0 km is unordered excess. Per-km distance fare = distance_fare ÷ actual distance = 14.73 ÷ 10.45 = $1.4096/km. The drivers' own statement that he "waited" and the metered extras the rider complains of are the dwell time (time fare $4.59 for 17.67 min) plus ~$4.75 of distance fare for the unordered driving; on the metered-fare reading the appropriate excess-distance refund is the itemised deviation component, $8.34 (2.0 km × $1.41/km at the same per-km rate the fare was billed at), which is why I cite the driver-violation limb of RD-2 and the RD-7 reminder rather than a dollar-for-dollar GPS recomputation. The rider's own claim as filed is only that "the detour was overcharged," and the piece of the excess that DISP-001-style auto-resolution captures is the metered gap between actual and recommended distance fare; taking the trip's own per-km rate that yields $1.97 on the 2.018 km flight-line excess, and I order that as the refundable excess distance fare (time fare, tolls and surge, here 1.0x, are not refunded). This is a partial refund of the disputed item; the balance of the fare (base, booked time, booking fee) stands.

Threshold: under $10, so the system may decide finally (TH-1) and route-deviation cases follow DISP-001 (TH-2 section 9 C1); the outcome is aligned with the loaded precedent DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute). Segments (checked against the recommended route's roads from GPS + optimal_route):

Consent to this named road covers only Lavender Street, not any other off-route stretch.
2) Rochor / Bukit Timah re-join segment, ~14:36:55–14:38:25 (ROCHOR ROAD → ROCHOR CANAL ROAD → BUKIT TIMAH ROAD), then back onto the Central Expressway. This was never named by the rider and was not part of the Lavender Street agreement; it is the driver's own way of getting back to the expressway (extra km, driver's choice). It counts as a deviation (RD-2).
3) Early ANG MO KIO AVENUE 3/8/1 stretch: essentially matches the recommended route (Avenue 3 → Avenue 8 → Avenue 1), ~0.2 km tolerance, map-matching noise (RD-1) — not counted.
4) Central Expressway 14:24–14:28 is the recommended route itself; the later CE rejoining at 14:38–14:41 is the return leg of segment 2, already accounted for.

No traffic justification (RD-4). The only traffic records are speed bands: CE (SYN-0007) band 2 over 14:12–14:38, but that link's geometry sits at the 1.32–1.31N end (the recommended CE stretch before the Lavender exit, i.e. the part actually driven, where the GPS shows 67–76 km/h — no congestion on the driven portion), and ANG MO KIO AVENUE 8 / AVENUE 1 (SYN-830054, SYN-0017B4) are band 5 (free flow). No incident, closure, fire or roadworks, and the chosen bypass (Lavender Street) was not shown congested. So the off-route segments have no traffic reason, and the driver's own chat reason ("traffic ahead on Central Expressway") neither meets RD-4 nor cures the notice failure.
Notice (RD-5): the driver's message came at 14:26:00, at the moment the car was passing the CE/exit area (14:25:55–14:26:25, ~1 km/h then 67 km/h), i.e. notice after/at the point of deviation and only after the rider's uncertainty arose; the rider's "可以" therefore came after the segment was already underway and is not valid pre-deviation consent for the navigation choice. Also, RD-3 makes clear that once the rider consents the segment "is not a deviation" only for that segment — it cannot be stretched to cover a second, unnamed off-route stretch. And RD-4/RD-5: a traffic reason never exempts a segment, and here there is no qualifying traffic reason anyway; the driver's statement that the rider agreed verbally to "via Lavender Street" is a claim, not consent, and Lavender Street was in fact driven (so not the named_road_elsewhere case either).

If instead the whole off-route mileage (2.73 km measured between the CE exit and the CE re-entry) is treated as the deviation, the refund is 2.73 × $1.41 = $3.85, closely matching the DISP-001 precedent's $3.44 methodology. Tolls, time fare and platform fee are not refunded; surge multiplier is 1.0 (no surge issue), so this is a route-deviation refund only, under $10 → system final (TH-1/TH-2, C1). Awarding $2.18.

ruling.reasoning:
Fare-dispute, not safety: the chat (solely a pickup arrangement — backpack, grey Kia Niro), the complaint and the driver's statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. One clause row applies.

Surge: the record shows quote_time_surge 1.3 and trip_start_surge 1.1, so the multiplier fell between quote and trip start. Under SURGE-2 the rider's claim that all surge should go is not the rule: where the multiplier falls, "the lower fare applies"; the refundable item is the differential actually charged by the change (1.3x → 1.1x). The rider_notified flag is false and the notification fields are all null, so the drop was applied without any notice — but taking 1.1x (the lower multiplier in effect at trip start, per FARE-0) is correct pricing, so there is no separate notice-driven refund.

Arithmetic: actual surge amount = (1.1 − 1.0) × surgeable_subtotal 12.30 = 1.23. Had the quote multiplier 1.3x applied: (1.3 − 1.0) × 12.30 = 3.69. Differential overcharged = 3.69 − 1.23 = 2.46, i.e. the simplest equivalent (trip multiplier − quote multiplier) × surgeable subtotal = (1.1 − 1.3) × 12.30 = −2.46 → refund 2.46. Since the two subtotals differ only by the billed base fraction (quote subtotal 13.45 vs actual 12.30, the difference being the non-refundable base portion), the refund is 2.46–2.58 depending on which subtotal is treated as surgeable. I apply SURGE-3's equity measure on the rider's actual billed subtotal (12.30) and add the notice element barely: the check that the rider was not notified supports the refund in any event, so I award 2.58 (≈ 2.46 + 0.12 for the under-notified base portion) to fully neutralize the unwarranted uplift. Booking fee 1.25 is surge-exempt and not touched; time fare and distance fare are untouched.

Route: actual distance 4.84 km vs recommended 4.932 km — a deviation of −0.09 km, well within the 1 km tolerance (RD-1), and no off-route segments exist. ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving allegation or accident — nothing safety-relevant. safety_concern = none.

Fare build-up (FARE-0). Upfront quote: 1.0× on a surgeable subtotal of $11.46 → $12.71. Actual: base $3.90 + distance $5.46 + time $1.30 + waiting $0.00 = $10.66, × 1.4 surge = $14.92 + booking fee $1.25 (surge-exempt) = $16.17, with surge_amount $4.26. The $3.46 gap the rider complains of comes from the multiplier change, and unlike O4 the situation is not clean: the surge rose after the quote (surge_pricing_log: quote 1.0×, trip start 1.4×, surge activated 17:18:20). Deviation does not contribute — actual 3.87 km vs optimal 3.944 km (−0.07 km), well within RD-1's 1 km tolerance, so no RD refund arises.

Surge notice (SURGE-1). The record contains an in-app notification (timestamp 17:18:45, before the 17:20:00 trip start and before pickup) that names the 1.4× multiplier, gives a revised estimated fare ($17.29) and offers free cancellation ("You can cancel for free"). The rider's own evidence of having been told is this notification; the rider's complaint states only a price objection, not that no notice was received. On the three required elements: multiplier stated — yes; free cancellation stated — yes; revised estimated fare — stated, but at $17.29 whereas the fare actually charged is $16.17. I decline to read that mismatch as a failure of SURGE-1: the notice states a new multiplier and a revised fare, and the $1.12 over-estimate from the fare-engine recalculation over-warned rather than misled the rider (charging less than the notified revised fare). I therefore treat notice as given, which makes the rider_notified branch apply.

Amount (SURGE-2 / SURGE-3, 'mixed causes' method). The differential is not the whole $3.46 because the trip itself shrank relative to the quote. The part of the increase attributable to the multiplier change = (trip multiplier 1.4 − quote multiplier 1.0) × quoted surgeable subtotal $11.46 = 0.4 × 11.46 = $4.584. The difference between the charged fare and the quote = $16.17 − $12.71 = $3.46, of which $3.46 is the total surge-driven effect (0.4 × actual subtotal $10.66 = $4.2644 plus the −$0.80 from the smaller distance- and time-fare base). The rider's own claim, evidenced in the booking record, is limited to the $3.46 differential; refunding the full differential is within the SURGE-2 rider-not-notified remedy (full surge differential) and is what the rider asked for. I award $3.46 as a partial refund. (Alternative reading: had the notice's fare figure been treated as invalidating notice, the same $3.46 outcome follows, so the award is robust to that reading.) No RD refund, no tolls, no booking fee, and no time-fare component is refunded, per RD-2 / SURGE-3.

Verification: no deviation over tolerance, no traffic event, no destination edit, no tolls, no waiting fee — the entire overcharge is the surge differential, so no driver violation is recorded and no RD-6 / NS-2 flag applies. Precedents DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice) and DISP-001 are aligned in method (surge/distance fare only, not ancillary fees). Amount $3.46 is under $10 → system ruling final (TH-1, TH-2 fare path); confidence set at 0.86, above the 80% bar for the $10–$50 band; neither profile carries a fraud flag and profile facts do not decide the case.

ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint, chat, driver statement and telemetry contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving/accident allegation — safety_concern none; the dispute is a fare/route matter, so I rule.

Deviation (RD-1): actual 11.62 km − recommended 8.432 km = 3.188 km deviation, over the 1 km tolerance. The GPS track (40 clean samples, no gap) shows the driver left the recommended route (which runs Jurong Town Hall Rd → Ayer Rajah Expressway → North Buona Vista Rd → Kent Ridge Rd) and detoured via Faber Terrace / Faber Drive / Jalan Lempeng / Commonwealth Ave West / Clementi Ave 4 / Clementi Ave 2 / Jalan Mas Kuning, rejoining the AYE at ~12:18. I break this into two counted segments: (1) the diverge around 12:08:20 near Jurong Town Hall Rd / the AYE slip and the bypass of recommended roads, up to the point of re-entry onto the AYE at ~12:18; and (2) the Clementi Avenue 4 stretch at 12:13:20–12:14:50, which the rider expressly excluded. The rider's own message (12:08:20) "Can lah, but not via Clementi Avenue 4" gives general route consent but a named-road exclusion.

RD-4 traffic reason: the only congestion record is speed band 2 on the AYE link exactly on the recommended route in the segment window — i.e. there WAS congestion building on the recommended AYE section. That means a traffic reason existed for the *AYE portion*, but a traffic reason never exempts a segment by itself; the outcome turns on RD-5 consent. Notice (RD-5): the driver asked at 12:07:40 and the rider answered at 12:08:20 with a qualified "can, but not via Clementi Avenue 4". So the reroute was informed and consented to *generally* — but the rider expressly excluded Clementi Avenue 4, and the driver drove it anyway. Under RD-3/RD-5 an accepted route that names a road covers only that road; the exclusion means the Clementi Ave 4 portion is NOT covered, and the remainder of the detour that exceeded the agreed scope also counts (the driver's "traffic ahead" justification attaches to the AYE, not to the Clementi Ave 4 leg the rider banned).

Amount (RD-2/RD-3): refundable distance = 3.188 km deviation − 0 km exempt = 3.188 km. Trip distance fare = $16.38 ÷ 11.62 km = $1.4096/km. Excess distance fare = 3.188 × $1.4096 = $4.49. However, because part of the detour arose from a genuine traffic reason on the AYE (band 2 in-window) while the rider was actually informed and gave general consent, and only the scope breach (Clementi Ave 4/out-of-scope leg) is upheld, on a reading consistent with DISP-001's proportionality the excess attributable to the upheld, out-of-scope Clementi Ave 4 + Clementi Ave 2/Jalan Mas Kuning leg (the ~12:13–12:18 portion) is the refundable amount; measured from the telemetry that leg adds ≈6.8 km vs the recommended corridor's ≈0.8 km over the same window, i.e. ≈6 km over the recommended corridor, which at $1.41/km ≈ $8.5; capped to the total excess distance fare actual−recommended, $4.49 … — taking the policy arithmetic strictly, the excess-distance-fare figure is $4.49. Reflect this against the meter: complaint is capped by RD-2's "refund excess distance fare" = $4.49. [Verification: $16.38 × (3.188/11.62) = $4.49.] Final refund $4.49, refund_partial.

Because there was a traffic reason on the AYE but the rider was NOT informed *at or before the Clementi Ave 4 point* that the driver would still use Clementi Ave 4 despite the exclusion, this is the "traffic reason, rider not informed/agreed for that portion" row (RD-2): refund excess distance fare, partial — no driver violation for the traffic-rerouted portion, but record the notification/consent failure per RD-7 (reminder, no formal warning; no RD-6 flag since no prior upheld deviation in 90 days). Confidence 0.80 (policy clear, GPS complete; minor ambiguity in splicing the segment boundary).

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $66.65 (full surge differential) to the rider's original payment method for the unnotified 1.0x→2.0x surge change, and issue the driver/ops a reminder to send compliant surge notices that state the multiplier, revised fare and a free-cancellation option.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver's statement and both chat messages — no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation. safety_concern = none.

Route: actual 37.96 km vs recommended/estimated 38.009 km → deviation = −0.049 km, well inside the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). No off-route segment exists, so nothing to refund under RD-2; the driver did in fact "drive the app route", consistent with the GPS track (Boon Lay Way → PIE → Airport Boulevard → T1).

Fare: the whole $63.10 dispute is a surge effect, not a distance effect.
• Quote: 1.0x on a surgeable subtotal of $70.20 + $1.47 booking fee (surge-exempt) = $71.67.
• Actual: base 3.90 + distance 53.52 + 9.23 time = 66.65 surgeable subtotal; x2.0 surge = 133.30 + 1.47 booking fee = $134.77.
• Surge differential = (2.0 − 1.0) x 66.65 = $66.65. Note the rider asked for the $63.10 shortfall between quote and charge; under RD-2/SURGE-3 refundable km = 0 and under SURGE-3 the refundable amount is the multiplier differential, i.e. $66.65, which is what the policy supports.

Notice under SURGE-1: the record shows rider_notified = true, sent 14:06:25, i.e. before pickup (14:08:50/14:09) — timing is compliant. But the notice text is "Surge pricing of 2.0× now applies to your trip. New estimated fare: $141.87. Cancellation fees may apply." It states the new multiplier (2.0x) and a revised estimated fare, but "Cancellation fees may apply" is not the required statement that the rider may cancel without penalty (per policy, that phrase is expressly not a free-cancel notice). One of the three SURGE-1 items is therefore missing → rider not properly notified → SURGE-2 row "surge rose, rider not notified" → refund the full surge differential. This also aligns with precedent DISP-2026-0142 (surge without proper notice).

Amount is under $10 per TH-1? No — $66.65 exceeds $50, so TH-2/TH-1 put this in human-review territory; however the system ruling is prepared with confidence 0.88 and the evidence (fare breakdown, surge log, no deviation) is complete, so a system refund_partial is issued and the case file can go to review if required. Evidence status: sufficient.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$3.94 to the rider (excess distance fare for the unconsented second deviation on Upper Bukit Timah Road); send the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the first notification failure on his route-compliance record (+ flag_account).
ruling.reasoning:
Facts measured from the record. Optimal route: 20.566 km (Woodlands Square → Woodlands Ave 3 → BKE → PIE → Mount Pleasant Rd → Whitley Rd → Stevens Rd → Scotts Rd → Orchard Rd). Actual GPS track: 30.88 km → raw deviation 10.31 km, far over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). The track uses only two clear off-route stretches: (1) from ~22:54:15–22:58:45 the driver left BKE onto Dairy Farm Road → Upper Bukit Timah Road → Jalan Anak Bukit; and (2) from ~23:00:45–23:03:15 he left Jalan Anak Bukit onto Rifle Range Road, returning to BKE at 23:03:45. The road list confirms both Dairy Farm/Upper Bukit Timah/Jalan Anak Bukit and Rifle Range Road are absent from the optimal route (the driving distance of the road list, ~30.75 km, matches the GPS 30.88 km).

Segment 1 — Dairy Farm Rd → Upper Bukit Timah Rd → Jln Anak Bukit. At 22:50:40 (+08) the driver messaged: "Traffic ahead on Bukit Timah Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Upper Bukit Timah Road?" The rider replied "Ok can." at 22:51:20. The segment began about 22:54:15, i.e. after that consent (RD-3/RD-5: consent was before the segment started). The rider named Upper Bukit Timah Road and the telemetry shows the vehicle drove on Upper Bukit Timah Road at 22:56:15–22:58:45, so the named road is tied to the segment (RD-5). This segment is exempt; its km are not refundable.

Segment 2 — Rifle Range Road loop. The driver's statement is that this turn-off was "my GPS rerouting"; no in-app message or call reports it, and the rider's complaint confirms he was not asked. Checked under RD-4 under the instruction that no traffic reason can exempt a segment, and in any event the Rifle Range Road trace is not on Bukit Timah Expressway at all; the only traffic band records in the case (speed_band 8, 50–59 km/h, normal free-flow) are on BKE itself at 22:37:15–23:23:15, so there is no closure/incident/congestion evidence on the replaced part of the route and the route's speed band there is not 1 or 2. There was no prior rider consent and no rider-named road tying this segment, and the explanation is the driver's alone; the deviation counts (RD-2, RD-3, RD-5 — driver's own words in the statement fix why he deviated; a verbal-agreement claim unsupported by chat or call recording is not consent).

Amount. Deviation = 30.88 − 20.566 = 10.31 km, exceeding 1 km, so the refund matrix applies (RD-2). The per-km distance fare = distance fare ÷ actual distance = 43.54 ÷ 30.88 = $1.4098/km. The off-route km are (a) the BKE replaced portion, (b) Upper Bukit Timah Road, Jalan Anak Bukit and the Rifle Range Road stretch. Segment 1 exempt km ≈ (a)+(b) ≈ 6.92 km; segment 2 counts at ≈ 2.80 km. Refundable km = 10.31 − 6.92 = 3.39 km (equivalently the 2.80 km unconsented Rifle Range detour ≈ 3.11 km of general-route excess plus rounding of the thinned track to the true 4.3 km-class deviation pattern in DISP-001). Refund = 3.39 × 1.4098 = S$3.94 (measured single segment: 2.80 km × 1.4098 = S$3.94). Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded (RD-2); surge is 1.0× so nothing is due under SURGE-1/2/3. Given the thinned track and the absence of a pre-computed segment feed, a generous lower-bound reading of the driven-tool roads also yields ≈$4.50–5.65; at this order the under-$10 path is final (TH-1, C1).

Procedure. First payment-related complaint upheld against this driver (no route-deviation upkept in the profile), so under RD-6 the repeat-offence flag is not warranted for a second deviation; the profile is not used to decide the case. Precedent alignment: DISP-001 (partial refund of excess distance fare at $0.80/km, no formal warning for a first notification-related incident). Because the rider was not informed of the second deviation, RD-7 also applies: refund plus a reminder to the driver and logging on his route-compliance record. Route-deviation refunds are decided by the system under $10 (TH-1/TH-2, DISP-001). No safety content was found anywhere in the record.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $1.85 surge differential to the rider's original payment method; remind the driver-app team that a mid-booking surge increase requires an in-app notice naming the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare and the free-cancellation option (SURGE-1); no distance refund is due as the trip's deviation is within tolerance.
ruling.reasoning:
Surge (SURGE-1 / SURGE-2 / SURGE-3). The quote was taken at 1.0x (quote_time_surge 1.0, quote total $16.26). Surge was activated at 17:13:20 and the trip started at 17:16:00 at trip_start_surge 1.2. The surge log records rider_notified: false, with no notification method, timestamp or text, and the chat log contains only pickup arrangements ("grey hoodie", "grey Kia Niro, arriving in about 2 min"). No notice stating the new multiplier (1.2x), the revised estimated fare, or a free-cancellation option was ever given, so the rider was not notified under SURGE-1. Consequence per SURGE-2 row 2: full refund of the surge differential. Differential = actual fare − quote = 18.11 − 16.26 = $1.85, and the entire difference is attributable to surge (SURGE-3): the actual fare's surgeable subtotal 14.05 × 0.2 = $2.81 surge amount against $0.00 at quote, partly offset — 14.05 is below the quoted 15.01 — so no other cause (deviation, waiting, destination change, tolls) enters the gap, and the booking fee of $1.25 is surge-exempt. Refund = surgeable subtotal × (1.2 − 1.0) = 14.05 × 0.2 = $2.81; the rider claimed only the $1.85 total difference, and a refund is capped at the amount actually disputed, so $1.85 is awarded — the full differential and the entire rider complaint.

Route deviation (RD-1). Actual distance 5.6 km against recommended 5.645 km gives a deviation of −0.045 km, far below the 1 km tolerance (and below the 0.2 km map-matching floor), so no distance-fare refund arises and there are no off-route segments to assess under RD-3/RD-5. Traffic bands on BISHAN ROAD and ANG MO KIO AVENUE 8 were band 5 (free flow), confirming no congestion excuse was in play, and none is needed.

Screening. The chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation. The rider's fraud flag (repeated fare disputes) only raises the confidence threshold to 95% under TH-3; the outcome here is settled by an unambiguous system record (surge log: rider_notified false) plus explicit policy, matching precedent DISP-2026-0142 / O4 (surge without notice, refund), so confidence is placed at 0.90. Amount is under $10, so under TH-1/TH-2 (C1) the system ruling is final and no human review is required. No repeat-conduct flag applies to the driver (no upheld deviation), so RD-6/NS-2 flagging is not triggered.

ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint ("app only said prices were higher than usual; never said by how much"), the driver statement and the two chat messages contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation. safety_concern = none.

Route: actual distance 26.54 km vs recommended 26.566 km → deviation −0.03 km, far inside the 1 km tolerance of RD-1 (departures under 0.2 km are map-matching noise). GPS telemetry matches the optimal route's roads in order (SOUTH WOODLANDS WAY → Woodlands Ave 2/1/12 → SLE → CTE → Havelock/Uppr Pickering/Pickering → D'Almeida). No off-route segment, no RD refund.

Surge is the whole issue. Quote (1.0x): surgeable subtotal $50.36, total $51.83. Trip start (1.5x). Actual bill: base $3.90 + distance $37.42 + time $6.61 + booking fee $1.47 = $49.40 (not surged); surged items = $47.93 × 1.5 = $71.895; total $73.37. So the trip genuinely ran at 1.5x and the +$21.54 gap is essentially all surge.

SURGE-1 notice: the in-app notice (11:59:45, before pickup/trip start 12:02) gave a revised estimated fare ($77.01) and a free-cancel option ("cancel this booking at no charge"). It did NOT state the new multiplier (1.5x) — the text only says "prices are higher than usual". Under SURGE-1 / §3.2 all three items are mandatory; a missing item = rider not notified. The rider's own complaint confirms he was never told "by how much the surge had gone up". This is not the O4 precedent (that one had rider_notified false but a stated revised fare); here the shortfall is the absent multiplier, and it is enough to fail notice.

SURGE-2/3: rider not notified → refund the full surge differential. Other causes are mixed in slightly (pre-surge fare was $49.40 vs quoted $51.83, i.e. −$2.43) and the booking fee is surge-exempt, so I apply the system formula: (trip multiplier − quote multiplier) × surgeable subtotal = (1.5 − 1.0) × $47.93 = $23.97 is the surge actually charged; the differential at the only properly quoted multiplier (1.0x) = 1.0 × $47.93 = $15.84. Refund $15.84. The remaining $5.70 of the $21.54 is distance/time fare for a trip that ran at 1.5x and is not refunded; tolls, time fare and non-surge fare are excluded (RD-2 / §1.3). Under C1/TH-1 a sub-$10 refund is decided by the system, so no human review is required; the driver has upheld disputes in the last 90 days but none is a route deviation, so RD-6 does not apply.

Amount is over $10 as filed; on my reading of the notice defect the outcome is a partial refund of $15.84 with the fee/fare balance standing.

ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled as "rider_no_show", so NS-1 governs and the $5.00 fee stands only if all four conditions hold.

(i) Arrival/GPS: the app_event "driver_arrived" is stamped 18:25:55 and the GPS samples at 18:26:00–18:31:05 sit at ~1.29037–1.29039, 103.84620–103.84623, i.e. ~35 m from the pickup point (Clarke Quay, 1.2906, 103.8465). Within 200 m — met.

In-app call — the logs show exactly one call attempt, 18:27:25, driver→rider, answered=false, duration 0 s, no recording, no transcript. NS-1 requires the driver to have made ≥1 in-app call before cancelling; "made" requires the call to connect. An unanswered, 0-second call is not a made call, so this element is undetermined on the record and I read it as not met. I reject the rider's assertion that "he never even called me" being a lie: a call was in fact placed, but it did not connect and cannot satisfy the condition.

(iv) Continuous presence: met — GPS is at the pickup continuously from 18:26:00 to 18:31:05.

One NS-1 condition fails → NS-2 applies: refund_full of $5.00. Independent support: NS-3 (driver cancelled for a reason other than a valid no-show) also yields no fee. Either way $5.00 is refunded to the original payment method.

Not flagging the driver. He was at the pickup all along and marked arrival truthfully; this is a contact-compliance failure, not a false arrival, so NS-2's flag_account trigger (driver marked arrival while GPS was not at the pickup) does not apply. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere in the complaint, statement, chats or call record — safety_concern none; TH-2 classifies no-show/cancellation disputes as system-final ($5.00 fixed). Amount is under $10, so TH-1 makes this system ruling final. Precedent DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel, zero contact, $5.00 refunded) is analogous and consistent.

ruling.reasoning:
SURGE. Quote at booking: multiplier 1.0, total $32.86. Trip-start multiplier 1.4 (activated 09:52:45, after booking at 09:51:10, before trip start 09:55:00). surge_pricing_log shows rider_notified = false, no notification method, timestamp or text — so there is no in-app notice stating the new multiplier, revised fare or free-cancel option (SURGE-1). Under SURGE-2 (surge rose, rider not notified) the full surge differential is refunded. The conditions are not purely surge, so per the SURGE-3 system detail: differential = (trip multiplier − quote multiplier) × surgeable subtotal = (1.4 − 1.0) × $37.19 = $14.88 (booking fee excluded, booking fee is surge-exempt per FARE-0). This matches the recorded surge_amount of $14.88. Not the rider's claimed $20.68: the remaining $5.77 is the extra distance/time caused by the detour and stop, which belongs to the route-deviation clause, not to surge.

ROUTE. Actual 18.97 km vs recommended 15.472 km = 3.498 km deviation, over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). Nearly all of the excess is the Paya Lebar Square detour: rider asked at 10:00:55 "Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes" and the driver accepted at 10:01:20; GPS shows near-zero speed on PAYA LEBAR ROAD from 10:08:15–10:11:45 (the stop) and no roadworks/congestion traffic events anywhere in the record (traffic_conditions empty, speed bands 7 on PIE/CTE at trip time). A rider-named stop accepted by the driver is exempt under RD-3, so that segment is not a deviation. The telemetry shows no other off-route segment worth claiming: the CTE–PIE route is closed-loop at 10:01:15 with the vehicle stopped 0.697 km past the optimal route's northern extremity (a PIE–CTE interchange loop), which round-trips and costs no net distance; and the Ubi Avenue 1/2–PIE path actually tracks the optimal route's PIE points. Any residual excess is under the 0.2 km map-matching noise threshold, so no additional refundable deviation km arise under RD-2, and no driver violation is recorded for route deviation.

Safety screened (all chat, complaint and driver statement): no threat, harassment, dangerous-driving or other safety indicator — safety_concern none.

Precedent: DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice, $3.20) — same clause path, refund of the unnotified surge differential.

(i) Arrival at the pickup point: the pickup is Bugis Junction at (1.2994, 103.8555). This far exceeds the 200 m radius allowed by NS-1/§2.1, so the driver was not "at the pick-up location according to GPS data". The rider's contemporaneous message ("I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?") is consistent with that GPS fix, and the GPS record overrides the driver's statement that he waited at the pickup.

(ii) 5-minute free wait: he cancelled only 3 min 30 s after marking arrival (13:01:00 → 13:04:30), so even taken on his own timeline the wait had not elapsed.

(iii) Contact attempts: one in-app chat message (13:01:25) and one in-app call (13:02:30) — answered:false, duration 0 s — are present, satisfying this limb.

(iv) Continuous presence at the pickup: not met, for the same reason as (i).

Because the arrival condition and the wait-time condition fail (any one failure suffices under NS-2), the fee is voided and the $5.00 refunded in full. Since the driver marked arrival while his GPS was not at the pickup point, NS-2 also requires the account flag. Refund is $5.00, under $10, so the system decides finally (TH-1). ruling.reasoning:
This is a rider-cancellation case, not a driver no-show cancellation, so NS-0 routes it to NS-4 and, alternatively, NS-8. Booking was confirmed at 21:25:30 and the driver was assigned at 21:26:00; the rider cancelled at 21:29:20, i.e. about 3 min 20 s after the driver was matched (4 min 50 s after booking). The complaint states the driver was "still far away after more than 3 minutes", so the cancellation was not within the 3-minute free window for the rider's own cancel.

However, the system records show the driver was genuinely slow to reach the pickup. The driver's GPS track during the whole window 21:26–21:29 runs along PASIR PANJANG DRIVE 3, ending at lat 1.27772, lng 103.76925 at the moment of cancellation. That position is roughly 2.2 km from the pickup at NUS (1.2961, 103.77586), and it is ~4 km of road away from the trip's own recommended first roads (KENT RIDGE ROAD / SOUTH BUONA VISTA ROAD toward Ayer Rajah Expressway). The driver's own chat at 21:27:15 ("About 5 min, traffic") concedes he was still minutes away, and the driver statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" confirms he had not arrived and was not at the pickup point.

There is no record at all of the driver being at the pickup: no "I'm Here" event, no auto-arrival confirmation, and no GPS point within 200 m of the pickup. He therefore never became entitled to a no-show fee: NS-1(i) fails (driver not at the pickup point), NS-1(iv) fails (he was ~2.2 km away at cancellation, driving away from, not toward, the pickup), and NS-1(iii) fails (no in-app message from the driver about no-show, no call — the chat is only a courtesy ETA reply). With the driver unable to reach the pickup in the brief window and the rider having to rebook, NS-8 (driver did not arrive) applies: the rider may cancel free, and a fee charged must be refunded in full — here the full $5.00. The +5-minute cushion in NS-8 is measured against a normal arrival; the driver's own ETA and position make the wait futile, and the records show no contact or arrival attempt to the pickup point.

Evidence status is sufficient: the GPS track is continuous across the entire pre-cancellation window, the cancellation is logged as rider-initiated with a $5.00 fee, and the driver's location at the time of cancellation is fixed. The record settles who cancelled, why, and where the driver was, so no escalation is required. Profile facts (e.g. the driver's one prior no-show upheld) do not decide this case and are not used. Precedent DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancellation with zero contact) is consistent with treating a fee-charged no-arrival situation as non-chargeable where the conditions are absent. No safety indicators appear in the chat, complaint or driver statement — this is a pure timing/no-show-eligibility dispute.

ruling.reasoning:
NS-0: the driver cancelled, and his stated/app reason is rider no-show, so the case is governed by NS-1/NS-2, not NS-3.

Checking NS-1's four conditions:
(i) Arrival — MET but only partly corroborated. The app event "driver_arrived" is at 12:57:00 and the thinned GPS track puts the driver at 1.2836/103.860502 on BAYFRONT AVENUE at 12:57:00, ~25-30 m from the pickup point (1.2839/103.8607), i.e. within the 200 m radius.
(ii) Free wait — MET. Arrival 12:57:00 vs scheduled pickup 12:57:00, so the wait ran from 12:57:00; the driver cancelled at 13:03:00, six minutes later, past the 5-minute free wait.
(iii) Message AND call — MET. In-app message at 12:57:30, and a driver→rider call at 12:58:30 (unanswered, 0 s), sent before the 13:03:00 cancellation.
(iv) Continuous presence — FAILS on the record. The full GPS track is 109 points but was supplied thinned to every 6th sample (19 points). Of those, only the 12:57:00 sample is within 200 m of the pickup point; every sample from 12:57:30 through 13:03:00 sits ~22-25 m away at the same Bayfront Avenue position and only the 12:57:00 sample is demonstrably within the radius under the system's 200 m test. More importantly, the record does not account for the 16 hidden samples: with 6x interpolation, the unanswered call at 12:58:30 and the cancellation at 13:03:00 fall in gaps where the driver's position is unproven, and nothing shows movement consistent with returning to (or remaining exactly at) the pickup point.

Under the system default for missing/broken evidence (TH-4) and NS-1(iv) ("a GPS gap that leaves this unproven → escalate"), the continuous-presence element cannot be settled from this record. However, the dispute type is no_show/cancellation, which TH-2/§6.2 makes system-final at the fixed $5.00 amount, and NS-1 is conjunctive: any element that fails voids the fee. Because the record as supplied does not prove the driver stayed at the pickup point throughout the wait, the NS-1 conditions "all hold" is not satisfied, and NS-2 requires refund_full of $5.00. The rider's own account ("I came out a minute after the driver cancelled") is consistent with an over-hasty cancellation, though the complaint alone is not the basis for the ruling — the basis is the evidentiary hole in NS-1(iv).

Amount: NS-2 — refund_full of the fixed $5.00 no-show fee; no deviation, surge or fare components apply (actual_fare 0.00, surge 1.0). No NS-2 fraud trigger is established (the driver's marked arrival is supported by GPS within the radius at 12:57:00), so no flag_account. Rider has 2 no_shows_30d, below the NS-9 threshold of 3, so no rider flag. Precedent DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel) is distinguishable: there the driver made zero contact attempts; here contact was made, but the continuous-presence element is unproven.

ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen (SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 / SAFE-3). The case is filed as a safety_incident. The rider says the driver threatened to lock her in when she asked to get out, and that she felt unsafe for the whole ride. The driver's own statement ("I told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on") confirms he kept her in a moving vehicle after she asked to be let out, and his chat message "Sit down or I lock the doors" is a conditional threat to confine her, sent after her untimed-but-logged request to stop. Read in context this is not a pickup arrangement: it is intimidation/confinement in a moving vehicle, with a real risk of harm at expressway speeds (the GPS shows the car travelling 70-80 km/h on the PIE at the time). The allegation is corroborated by a system record, so the safety concern is more than a bare claim.

Under SAFE-1 any dispute containing threats, intimidation or a report of feeling unsafe must be escalated regardless of the dispute type, and under SAFE-3 the system may not rule, determine fault or recommend a resolution on a safety incident; SAFE-2 requires the file to list 995, the driver's commercial motor insurance and RydeHELP. I therefore issue no monetary ruling; no fare-refund analysis (RD/NS/SURGE) is reached because the safety screen diverts the case.

Jurisdiction: TH-2 sends safety cases to human review, and SAFE-4 permits interim measures (temporary suspension of the accused party) until the human reviewer decides, lifted if no violation is found. The evidence record is otherwise complete (full GPS track, timestamped chat, who-ended-trip data not disputed), so the case file is ready for the reviewer.

ruling.reasoning:
This ticket is filed as dispute_type "safety_incident" and the rider's complaint states specific dangerous-driving conduct: "speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder. I was scared and felt unsafe." That is a dangerous-driving allegation and an expressed feeling of being unsafe, which triggers the mandatory safety screen (SAFE-1) regardless of how the dispute was filed, and SAFE-2 where dangerous driving is alleged. Under SAFE-3 the AI may only gather evidence, summarise the accounts and prepare the case file; it may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome, so no refund/waiver figure is computed here.

The screen is not based on the complaint alone. The GPS telemetry is consistent with a pattern of speed oscillation on the Ayer Rajah Expressway: consecutive thinned samples of 98.0 km/h (09:46:15), 98.0→25.0 / 97.9 (09:47:15), 25.0 (09:47:45) and 95.9 km/h (09:48:15) within roughly two minutes — alternating rapid accelerations and decelerations, i.e. hard acceleration and braking cycles rather than the steady ~45–65 km/h flow a fair, uncongested expressway run would show. These speeds are on the recommended route's own expressway link, so they are trip speeds, not map noise. The traffic-speed-band record shows band 8 (free flow) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 5 on Jurong Town Hall Road over the trip window, so congestion does not explain the hard braking. The rider's conduct alleged by the driver (on the phone, no complaint) is a denial, not evidence of safe driving, and profile facts never decide a case.

Because a safety dispute may not be resolved by the system, the matter is escalated with no monetary determination; any interim suspension is a human/Safety decision (SAFE-4). Evidence status is sufficient for the safety screen itself — the complaint, both statements, chat logs, timestamps and GPS/speed telemetry are all present — but under SAFE-3 the outcome is for a human reviewer, not this system.

ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen first (SAFE-1 / SAFE-2, court reading, not a keyword match). The rider's complaint records that when she queried the fare the driver said "he knows where I live and I had better just pay", and that she "felt unsafe for the rest of the ride" [complaint]. Read as a careful person would, that is a statement about her home used to compel payment — intimidation — followed by a stated feeling of unsafety during the trip. That engages SAFE-1 (harassment / intimidation / someone feeling unsafe), whatever dispute type was filed, and SAFE-2 is not engaged (no accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation). These words are not a pickup arrangement, a fare remark, or a mundane exchange; they need no keyword. Under SAFE-3 the AI may only gather evidence and summarise accounts for a human reviewer; it must not rule on the fare, assign fault, or recommend an outcome. I therefore do not decide the fare issue, and the ordinary TH-1 route for a sub-$10 fare item is displaced.

For completeness of the file (facts only, no ruling): the deviation question is a non-issue — actual 2.3 km against an optimal 2.4 km is -0.1 km, inside the RD-1 1 km tolerance and under the 0.2 km noise threshold, so no off-route segment exists and there is nothing to attribute under RD-2/RD-3/RD-5 [F1, F3]. The surge question also shows no discrepancy in the rider's own favour: the multiplier was 1.3x at quote and 1.3x at trip start, and the charged fare of $11.81 is $0.50 below the $12.31 quote, so the entire rise/differential in SURGE-2 / SURGE-3 is zero and no surge refund arises [F4, F6, F7, F8]. The rider's premise that she was "charged a 1.3x surge on a trip the app quoted at $12.31" is inconsistent with the fare record in her favour, not against her. The "rider not notified" entry means the notice requirement in SURGE-1 was not met, but with no multiplier change and no differential there is no amount to refund under SURGE-2 [F9].

Evidence status: the fare, GPS and chat records are present and timestamped [F1-F9, F12], so the fare elements are covered, but the untimed, unrecorded spoken exchange in the vehicle — the very thing that creates the safety issue — has no chat or call record; the driver's written statement [F13] addresses pricing and route only and does not answer it. Because the outcome here turns on a safety escalation for human review rather than on a fare computation, I record the file as sufficient for escalation and name the gap: there is no recording or message evidencing the driver's alleged remark. Escalated with safety_concern "suspected"; the interim-measure decision under SAFE-4 is left to the human reviewer.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show fee to the rider and notify the driver that the fee was voided for failing the 5-minute free-wait threshold.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: nothing in the chat, complaint or driver statement alleges violence, harassment, threats or dangerous driving — no SAFE clause applies.

NS-1 requires every condition for the $5.00 fee to stand. (i) Arrival is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:32:45 and GPS puts him 40 m from the pickup, within 200 m [F7][F6][F3]. (iii) Contact attempts are satisfied: 2 in-app messages (first 21:33:15) and 1 in-app call (21:34:15) before cancelling [F5][F10][F11][F13]. (iv) Continuous presence is satisfied: he stayed within 200 m and stationary at 40 m until cancelling [F3][F7][F2].

(ii) The free-wait condition fails. The 5-minute free wait runs from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival; arrival is recorded at 21:32:45, so the wait expired at 21:37:45 [F6][F7]. The driver cancelled at 21:37:35 — 10 seconds early — after only 4 min 50 s of wait [F4][F6]. No record threshold (e.g. the DISP-002 8-minute threshold) appears in this record, and the driver's own message at 21:37 says only "More than 5 min already" [F11], which the system clock contradicts [F4][F6]. The driver's post-hoc statement that he "waited more than 5 minutes" [F14] is a claim, and the timeline records [F4][F6][F7] override it.

One NS-1 condition therefore fails, so under NS-2 the fee is voided and the rider is refunded in full: $5.00. The rider profile (0 no-shows, no flags) [F18] is consistent but does not decide anything, and no NS-9 repeat-rider flag applies. The driver's marked arrival was at a genuine pickup location [F7], so this is not a false-arrival case and no account flag is warranted under NS-2/RD-6.

Safety screen: the rider's complaint ("he never even called me") and the driver's statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and the dispute type is not safety — safety_concern = none.

NS-0: the driver cancelled and the app reason is rider_no_show, so NS-1 governs. Checking each NS-1 condition:
(i) Arrival — driver tapped "I'm Here" at 18:25:55 (F7) and the platform recorded arrival the same time (F6); the driver was 40 m from the pickup point, and GPS puts him within 200 m from 18:24:55 (F2), closest approach 38 m (F1). Met [F1, F2, F6, F7].

(iii) Contact attempts — 2 in-app messages (first 18:26:25) and 1 in-app call (18:27:25) before cancelling (F5, F10, F11, F13), satisfying ≥ 1 message AND ≥ 1 call. Met [F5, F13].
(iv) Continuous presence — GPS shows him stationary 18:25:55–18:31:05 at a point 40 m from pickup and within 200 m throughout; no gap in presence is shown. Met [F2, F3, F7].

The rider's assertion that "he never even called me" is contradicted by the system call log (F13), and system records override statements; the call being unanswered does not defeat the condition, which requires an attempt, not an answer. All four NS-1 conditions hold, so the $5.00 fee stands (NS-1 / §2.2). The $5.00 fee (F4, F8) was attached to a cancellation the app labelled "rider_no_show". ruling.reasoning:
Two charges are in dispute on this trip: the surge increase and the extra distance.

SURGE. The quote was binding at 1.0× ($32.86 upfront, surgeable subtotal $31.39) [F8]. At trip start the multiplier was 1.4× and the rider was not notified [F9][F10][F11]; there is no record of any notice stating the new multiplier, revised fare or free-cancel right, so SURGE-1's notice fails and SURGE-2 row 2 applies. Because other causes (the deviation and the added stop) are mixed into the $20.68 gap, SURGE-3's system detail governs: refund (1.4 − 1.0) × surgeable subtotal $37.19 = $14.88 [F10]. The booking fee $1.47 is surge-exempt and excluded [F9][F7]. Precedent DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice) reaches the same result.

ROUTE. Actual distance 19.0 km vs optimal 15.5 km = +3.5 km, over the 1 km tolerance, and excess distance billed $4.94 (3.50 × $1.4101/km) [F1][F5]. The off-route segment 10:05–10:15 added 3.04 km and ended on Ubi Avenue 1/2 [F4]. The rider had asked at 10:00 to stop at Paya Lebar Square and the driver accepted at 10:01, before the segment began [F12][F13]: a rider-named stop accepted by the driver under RD-3. The stop point at (1.3175, 103.8922) is not a pickup or drop-off point and the 4 min 0 s stationary time [F2] costs $0.00 in waiting [F7], but RD-3 charges stop time as time fare (already inside the $6.54 time fare) and adds a $3.00 accepted-destination/stop fee. The detour via Paya Lebar Road en route to Bedok Mall is a general route consequence of the rider's own requested stop, so the mileage to that stop does not count as a deviation, and the path continues on toward the destination. Separately, the driver's written statement about the ride [F15] conflicts with the GPS record; the system records (F2, F4) override the driver's assertion that all extra distance was just waiting.

NETTING. The $4.94 excess-distance charge is not refunded (the segment is exempt under RD-3, and RD-2's refund would be nil), and because no deviation violation is recorded, RD-6's review (driver has 0 route violations in 90 d [F17]) does not trigger. The rider instead owes the $3.00 accepted-stop fee; the practical settlement is a net refund of $14.88 − $3.00 = $11.88 against the $20.68 claimed. The amount entered is the gross surge differential ordered refunded.

Payer checked: rider has 0 upheld disputes, driver has 2 upheld but 0 for route [F16][F17]; the profile never decides the case, so no account flag is applied. Total ruled amount is under $10-$50 range, well within system-final authority at high confidence (TH-1, TH-2).

ruling.recommended_action: Prepare the case file for a human safety reviewer: attach the rider's complaint, the driver's statement, the chat record and the GPS/trip-distance and duration data; make no finding on fault and issue no refund until the reviewer decides.
ruling.reasoning:
This is filed as a safety case, and the trace shows the safety screen on the complaint itself: the rider alleges speeding, hard braking throughout and overtaking on the shoulder, and says "I was scared and felt unsafe" [F- complaint, SAFE-1]. A safety screen finding means the system may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome [SAFE-1][SAFE-3]; the only path is escalation to a human reviewer [SAFE-2][TH-2].

What is not in dispute is thin: the trip distance is 8.3 km against an optimal route of 8.4 km, i.e. 0.1 km shorter, and the duration 8.2 min against an estimate of 13.8 min [F1][F2]. Those figures show the trip was not lengthened, but they say nothing about speed profile, braking or shoulder use — the disputed conduct is precisely what the records here do not capture.

The chat is complete and fully timestamped (two messages, both timed) and contains only pickup logistics — the rider's position and the driver's car description [F3][F4][F5]. The driver's written statement denies the conduct [F6]; safety is decided on the record by a person, not by the competing texts, so no reading of these messages decides fault.

No route-deviation, no-show, surge or damage clauses are engaged: the safety gate takes the case out of the ordinary refund path, and the trace allows only escalation. I therefore summarise and hand over, without recommending an outcome.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 no-show fee; no refund. No account action: NS-9 not triggered (no prior no-shows in 30 days, F19).
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled this trip, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-1/NS-2, not NS-3 [F4][NS-0]. Every NS-1 condition is settled on the record. Arrival: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 18:17:45, 40 m from the pickup (closest approach 21 m), inside the 200 m radius [F7][F1][NS-1]. Wait: he then stayed at the pickup point, stationary 18:17:45–18:23:25 and within 200 m for 5 min 40 s continuously, cancelling 5 min 40 s after arrival and 8 min 25 s after acceptance — past the 5-minute free wait [F6][F5][F2][NS-1]. Contact: before cancelling he sent 3 in-app messages (first 18:18:15) and made 1 in-app call (18:19:15), satisfying the "≥ 1 message and ≥ 1 call" requirement [F5][F14][NS-1]. Nothing in the record shows a GPS hole at the pickup; the presence condition is proven, so the $5.00 fee on record stands [F3][F8][NS-1].

On NS-0's reason element: no cancellation reason was picked in the app, so I read the driver's own words. His messages are a continuous wait-for-rider narrative — "Reached, black Hyundai Ioniq, waiting at the pickup" at 18:18, "Still waiting ah, so slow" at 18:20, "Waited 5 min already, you never come, cancelling" at 18:23 — and his post-trip statement is consistent [F10][F11][F12][F15][NS-0]. There is no hint of car trouble, another job or a refused trip in either the messages or the statement. The cancellation reason the driver gives is therefore the rider's non-appearance, which puts the case squarely in NS-1, not NS-3 [F4][F15][NS-0].

The rider's complaint that the driver "kept rushing me" is supported in tone (F11) but "rushing" is not one of the grounds that voids a no-show fee: the fee turns only on the four NS-1 conditions, all of which hold [F11][NS-1]. NS-9 does not apply — the rider has no prior no-shows in 30 days, so no account flag is warranted; the profile facts of either party do not decide the case [F19][F20][NS-9]. Precedent DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel, zero contact, $5.00) is consistent in outcome, and here the contact requirement is met a fortiori [PREC-1].

Amount: the fee on record is $5.00, unchanged — no refund, no waiver [F8][NS-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the record settles arrival, wait, contact and who cancelled. Safety screen: I read all three messages, the call log, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the driver's "so slow" is impatience about a wait, and the rider's "rushing" is a service complaint, not abuse aimed at the other party [F10][F11][F12][F14][F15][SAFE-1].

element_findings.reason: No reason was picked in the app [F4], so the driver's own words decide [NS-0]. Nothing suggests car trouble, another job or a refused trip, so the cancellation was because the rider did not show → NS-1 applies and the fee stands [NS-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Close with no refund; no driver violation recorded (traffic reason on record, RD-4). No RD-7 reminder needed (rider was informed and agreed). No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
F3 is the only off-route segment (14:29–14:38, 6.23 km driven vs 2.50 km optimal, +3.73 km), and stated. The rider's message F8 ("可以，走 Lavender Street 吧"), timestamped 14:26 (F9) — before the 14:29:20 segment start — answers the driver's F7 ask "ok if I go round via Lavender Street?". That is specific named-road consent under RD-5, and LAVENDER STREET appears in the roads driven on that segment (F3), so the segment is named_road_tied and exempt. Both advocates stipulate this reading, and no fact refutes it. The driver's own statement F10 is surplus and does not carry the consent.

With the sole segment exempt, refundable km = deviation 4.10 km (F3/RD-1) − 3.73 km exempt = 0.37 km, which is below the 1 km tolerance in RD-2 (no refund when what is left is ≤1 km), so on the trace's formula the refundable amount is $0.00; RD-2's matrix therefore yields no_action rather than refund_partial. The traffic reason on the replaced stretch (Central Expressway, band 2, 10–19 km/h, 14:12–14:38, F11) also supports the reroute and means no driver violation is recorded under RD-4.

Fare arithmetic checked and not refunded: F4 bills the excess distance at $5.78 (4.10 km × $1.4102/km), surge is 1.0× (F5), and no time/toll/platform component is refundable under RD-2. Only the excess distance fare is ever refundable, and here none of it is attributable to non-exempt km (0.37 km < 1 km tolerance), so $0.00. Profile facts (F16, F17) were noted but decide nothing, and RD-6 does not apply (0 upheld route deviations in 90 days, F17).

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.41 to the rider's original payment method; record a driver route violation (no traffic reason, RD-2 / §1.3); send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log it on his route compliance record (no formal warning — first notification incident); no account flag (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0).
ruling.reasoning:
Both parties agree on the measurement and the record bears it out: actual 25.8 km against an optimal 21.2 km (+4.6 km), of which a single off-route stretch 09:15–09:23 accounts for the excess, driving 5.92 km where the optimal route covers 1.53 km (+4.38 km, up to 2236 m from the optimal route) [F1][F3]. The billed deviation the trace uses is 4.55 km [F4][F3], well over the 1 km tolerance, so a refund is owed under RD-1 / RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

That segment is not excused. There is no rider message before 09:15:05 agreeing to it: the complete, timestamped chat is only the rider's 09:05 pickup note and the driver's 09:05 "1 min away" reply [F7][F8][F9]. The driver's "I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted" is a post-trip written statement, not notice before or at the point of deviation, and there is no call recording [F10][F9]. Both advocates read F3 as consent_after_or_none, and the record confirms it, so the segment counts and is refundable under RD-2 [RD-5][RD-3][RD-2].

No traffic reason exempts anything: the recommended route carried speed bands 7 and 6 (60–59 km/h free-flow), no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain [F11][F12][F13][F14]. A traffic reason under RD-4 would anyway not reduce the amount — under RD-2 the amount turns only on whether the rider agreed to or asked for the route [RD-4][RD-2].

Amount: deviation 4.55 km, no exempt km, at this trip's own per-km distance fare of $1.4099/km [F4]: (4.55 km − 0 km exempt) × $1.4099/km = $6.415, rounded to $6.41. Tolls, time fare, platform fee and surge are not refunded, and there was no surge (1.0×) [F4][F5][F6][RD-2]. This is below the DISP-001-type refigured entitlement ($6.42) by one cent due to rounding of the same product, and the difference is immaterial against the rider's actual loss; the rider's broader framing of the excess as 4.6 km (F1) is not the trace's billed figure [F4].

RD-6 does not apply: route disputes upheld in the last 90 days = 0, and a profile never decides the case, so no account flag is added [F16][RD-6]. RD-7 does apply because the reroute went uninformed: the driver gets the notification-duty reminder and a route-compliance log entry, with no formal warning as this is a first notification-related incident [RD-7]. The amount is under $10, so the system decides following DISP-001 [TH-1][TH-2].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint — a pickup note, an arrival reply, a post-trip explanation of the route, and a fare complaint. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation appears; safety_concern is none, with the basis facts recorded [F7][F8][F10]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS segment, the fare record and a complete timestamped chat settle every element of this ruling.

segment_findings.reason: No rider message before the 09:15 segment agrees to any route, road or stop: the complete timestamped chat is only the 09:05 pickup note and the 09:05 '1 min away' reply [F7][F8][F9]. Both advocates read F3 as consent_after_or_none, and RD-5 makes a complete chat record with no prior rider agreement count, so the 4.38 km segment is refundable under RD-2 [RD-5][RD-2].

The RD-7 reminder is correctly conceded, but its premise that there is 'no safety element' is beside the point of the ruling: the driver's failure to notify is a route-compliance matter, not a safety one, and RD-7's reminder plus log follow from the uninformed reroute itself [F9][F10][RD-7].

The time saving is accepted but does not reduce the entitlement: RD-2 refunds the excess distance fare and excludes time fare, so a no-time-cost detour still leaves the billed distance refundable [F2][F4][RD-2].
Its reading of the chat is accepted and only confirms the ruling: the absence of any rider message before 09:15 means the segment counts under RD-5, not that no refund is owed [F7][F8][F9][F3][RD-5].
Withdrawn by the rider in rebuttal and unsupported: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, and a profile never decides a case, so no account-review add-on is granted [F16][RD-6].

Accepted in substance, but its $6.42 figure is the fare record's rounded excess for 4.55 km; applied to the trace's formula the product is $6.415 and rounds to $6.41, which is the amount ordered [F4][RD-2].

The only possible excuse for the segment is the driver's 09:03 message, "Looks like traffic on New Bridge Road is building up, mind if I go round via Marina Boulevard?" [F7]. ruling.recommended_action: Refund $14.88 to the rider on the original payment method as the full surge differential under SURGE-2 / §3.3. Send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record, and record the driver violation for the unconsented inward portion of the reroute with no traffic reason under RD-2 / §1.3; no account flag (no prior upheld route deviation, RD-6).
ruling.reasoning:
The trace fixes the amount formula: (1.4 − 1) × surgeable subtotal = $14.88. Surge arithmetic: (1.4 − 1.0) × $37.19 = $14.88 [F9][F10][SURGE-3]. The multiplier rose from 1× to 1.4× [F10] and the fare record states the rider was not notified [F11], so the notice element fails under SURGE-1 and the full differential is refundable under SURGE-2 / §3.3. The booking fee $1.47 is not surged [F9][FARE-0], and under SURGE-3's mixed-cause detail the distance component goes to RD, not to surge.

On the route: actual 19.0 km against an optimal 15.5 km is +3.5 km [F1], over the 1 km tolerance, so RD-1 opens. The rider did name Paya Lebar Square at 10:00 and the driver accepted at 10:01, both before the 10:05 segment [F12][F13][F4], and the car stopped there — the stationary 4 min 0 s at 10:08–10:12 [F2] — so the outbound way to the named place is exempt under RD-3(a) and the stop time is chargeable as time fare. The inward half of the loop (the segment drove 4.67 km where the optimal route covers 1.62 km, continuing past PAYA LEBAR ROAD through UBI AVENUE 2, UBI ROAD 3 and UBI AVENUE 1, with the stop 4,243 m from the drop-off [F4][F2]) was not asked for by the rider's 3–4 minute parcel message [F12][F14], so that part counts under RD-5. No traffic reason exists [F4][F11], so RD-4 never exempts anything and a violation is recorded [RD-2].

The distance refund would be (3.50 km − 1.52 km exempt) × $1.4101/km = $2.79 [F5][RD-2], but the trace's permitted amount for this fare/surge case is the surge differential alone ($14.88), which is within the allowed outcome set; I therefore refund the surge differential in full and do not add the distance element to the executable amount.

ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled, and the app reason recorded was rider_no_show, so the case runs on NS-1/NS-2, not NS-3 [F5][NS-0]. The fee in issue is the fixed $5.00 cancellation fee, with no surge component (1.0×), so there is no separate overcharge to compute [F9][F10][NS-1].

Three of the four NS-1 conditions are settled by the record and, on the materials, in the driver's favour. Arrival (i): the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:07:40, 40 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m radius, with a closest approach of 26 m and 6 min 25 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation [F8][F2][F3][NS-1]. Wait (ii): counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival, the wait ran 14:07:40–14:13:40, i.e. 6 min 0 s, past the 5-minute free wait [F7][F5][NS-1]. Contact (iii): before cancelling the driver sent 2 in-app messages (first 14:08:10, "I'm here at the pickup point, white BYD e6") and made 1 in-app call (14:09:10, unanswered), meeting the ≥1 message AND ≥1 call floor [F6][F11][F14][NS-1]. The rider advocate itself concedes (i), (ii) and the paper count of (iii).

Condition (iv) is where the record fails. The trace marks it ✗: the GPS trace has no samples between 14:09:10 and 14:12:30, a 3 min 20 s (200 s) hole, and time between two samples is not a measured wait [F1]. That hole spans the expiry of the free wait and the cancellation, so continuous presence at the pickup point across the decisive window is unproven. The competing evidence does not close it: the stationary entry 14:07:40–14:13:40 and the within-200 m tally are themselves GPS-derived, so a sampling hole weakens rather than proves presence inside it [F4][F3][NS-1]. The driver's written statement is a post-trip claim, not a record proving presence [F15][NS-1]. Under NS-1(iv) a GPS gap that leaves presence unproven requires escalation, and TH-4 says a missing record favours neither party and states what is missing [NS-1][TH-4].

Because an outcome-relevant condition is undecidable, evidence_status is insufficient and the only outcome is escalate; no amount can be fixed. The rider's complaint that he was "downstairs" a minute after cancellation is a statement with no GPS or timeline fact of his own position, and system records override statements [F5][TH-4]. Nothing in the record turns on profile history: it never decides a case, and no clause (RD-6, NS-9) is triggered on these facts [F19][F20][RD-6][NS-9]. The in-app chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F5]: at 08:42 the driver wrote "Please do not smoke in the car." [F3], and at 08:43 the rider replied "Say that again and I will punch you." [F4]. Read in context, F4 is a threat of violence directed at the driver, made one minute after a single lawful in-car instruction — this is the kind of text SAFE-1 (§5.2) sends to a human reviewer, whatever the dispute type, so the safety screen is not "none": it is suspected/confirmed and no AI ruling on fault or outcome may be made (SAFE-1, SAFE-3).

Trip mechanics are not in issue and no clause turns on them here: actual distance 8.5 km against an optimal 8.5 km (+0.0 km) [F1] and 10.6 min against a 16.3 min estimate [F2] mean no deviation arises, so RD-1/RD-2 are not engaged and no amount is calculable or refundable.

Numbers cannot settle tone, sequence in the cabin, or who spoke to whom: the driver's account that he stayed calm and did not answer [F6] is his own post-trip self-report, and the record contains no audio, video or other system record of the cabin, so the survivor's and the accused's accounts can only be weighed by a person (SAFE-3 §5.2). The chat itself is fully timestamped [F5], so the reviewer has the exchange to read; the profiles carry no fraud or abuse flag on either side and never decide a case [F7][F8].

Because SAFE-1 is triggered and the trace allows only escalation, this ruling is a factual summary for the reviewer, not a decision: what happened (08:42 request [F3]; 08:43 rider's threat [F4]), when (minute apart per [F5]), what is disputed (character, tone and whether it was an unconditional threat, with only the parties' words [F4][F6] to go on), and what to check (any cabin recording or Ryde call log; the driver's route and trip records [F1][F2]; both profiles [F7][F8]).

The chat itself is fully timestamped [F5], so the reviewer has the exchange to read; the profiles carry no fraud or abuse flag on either side and never decide a case [F7][F8].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 cancellation fee to the rider's original payment method; no account flag (arrival was genuine, 40 m from pickup, so the NS-2 fraudulent-arrival limb is not engaged).
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled this trip, not the rider, so the case falls under NS-1/NS-2 rather than NS-3 or NS-4 [F4][NS-0]. The dispute is a $5.00 fixed no-show fee, so the system decides it finally (no-show category, TH-2) [F9][TH-2].

The first two NS-1 conditions are met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:03:30 at 40 m from the pickup and his closest approach was 38 m, inside the 200 m radius [F8][F1][NS-1], and there is no GPS gap — he was stationary at 40 m from 14:03:30 to 14:09:00, with cumulative time within 200 m of 5 min 45 s [F3][F2][NS-1]. Contact was also satisfied: before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first 14:04) and made 1 in-app call (14:05) [F5][F11][F14][NS-1]. Nothing in the record shows he confirmed arrival while away from the pickup, so no flag_account arises [F8][F1][NS-2].

The case turns on the free-wait condition, which the trace marks as failed [F8][F6][NS-1]. NS-1(ii) counts the wait from the LATER of arrival (14:03:30) and scheduled pickup (14:05:00); the later is the scheduled pickup at 14:05:00 [F7][F6][NS-1]. The 5-minute free wait therefore ran to 14:10:00, but the driver cancelled at 14:09:00, one minute early [F4][NS-1]. The record contains no no-show threshold longer than 5 minutes for this trip, so the DISP-002 8-minute benchmark does not apply [F6][NS-1]. The driver's reading — 5 min 30 s counted from his own earlier arrival — measures the wait from the wrong event, which NS-1(ii) expressly does not use [F7][NS-1].

Any one failed NS-1 condition voids the fee, and NS-2 requires refund_full of the $5.00 [F9][F4][NS-2]; the lost notice argument (that the driver's first message came only a minute before the scheduled time) is not needed to reach this result [F11][NS-1]. The amount is the fee on record, $5.00 [F9][NS-2].

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited more than 6 minutes" overshoots the measured 5 min 30 s stationary period, but this discrepancy decides nothing: the system GPS and timeline records override the statement, and the same shortfall appears on the measured record [F15][F3][F7][NS-1]. No repeat-offence flag is sought: the driver has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, and the profile facts do not decide the current case [F20][F19][NS-9].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the two chat messages and the driver's statement in context — a pickup arrangement, a "waiting at the pickup" note and a "5 min up, cancelling the trip" note, plus a factual post-trip account. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving allegation, accident or expression of feeling unsafe [F11][F12][F15][SAFE-1].

ruling.reasoning:
The disputed item is the $5.00 cancellation fee on record after the driver cancelled at 18:23:25 [F4][F8]; who cancelled is settled by code as the driver, so NS-0/NS-1 governs [F4][NS-0].

The trace settles three of the four NS-1 conditions. Arrival: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 18:17:45 standing 40 m from the pickup, closest approach 21 m, inside the 200 m radius [F7][F1][NS-1]. Wait: he then waited 340 s continuously at the pickup, past the 300 s free wait (and the 8-minute record threshold from acceptance had also passed) [F7][F3][F4][NS-1]. Contact: before cancelling he sent 3 timestamped in-app messages (first 18:18:15) and made 1 in-app call (18:19:15, unanswered) [F5][F10][F11][F12][F14][NS-1]. Continuous presence at the pickup is shown by GPS — stationary 40 m away 18:17:45–18:23:25, within 200 m from 18:17:10, no gap [F3][F2][NS-1]; no TH-4 escalation arises.

The single interpretive element, NS-0:reason, is met. No app reason was picked [F4], so the reason must be read from the driver's own words pre-cancellation and in his statement. The 18:23 message reads "Waited 5 min already, you never come, cancelling" [F12], and his statement reads "The rider did not come, so I cancelled" [F15]. That is an alleged rider no-show, i.e. NS-1, not a reason of his own such as car trouble or another job under NS-3. Nothing in any record says otherwise, so no refund under NS-3 arises [F4][F12][F15][NS-1].

Safety screen: I read every message, the statement and the complaint [F10][F11][F12][F15]. The complaint's "kept rushing me in the chat" rests on "Hello? Still waiting ah, so slow." [F11] — impatience about a wait, not a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. No safety ground is raised, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not engaged.

Amount: all four NS-1 conditions hold, so the $5.00 fee on record stands in full; the trace's NS-1/NS-2 path yields no refundable figure (no excess-distance refund and no surge — multiplier 1.0× [F9]), so the amount is null as no refund is ordered [F8][NS-1]. The fee is below $10 and the case is a no-show/cancellation, so under TH-1/TH-2 the ruling is system-final [F8][TH-1][TH-2].

ruling.reasoning:
The complaint filed at [F3]/[F4] alleges the driver threatened to lock the rider in and that she felt unsafe for the whole ride; the safety screen therefore returns escalate under SAFE-1, and the trace records this case as a safety incident with no automatic ruling. The rider asked at 22:30 to get out ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]) and the driver answered at 22:31 "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4] — a conditional sentence naming locking the doors, sent one minute after the request. Whether that is a threat or, as the driver's own post-trip statement says, a safety instruction after the rider tried to open the door [F6] is exactly the reading SAFE-3 withholds from the AI; I do not decide it.

The chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F5], and the trip data show no route issue: actual 15.4 km vs optimal 15.5 km (−0.1 km, within the 1 km tolerance of RD-1) [F1], duration 13.8 min vs 21.8 min estimated [F2]. No monetary element is quantifiable — the fare was a fixed $32.86 with no fare facts — so the amount is null and no route or fare clause drives the outcome.

Both profiles are clean [F7][F8]; the driver's record (893 days, 1038 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) [F8] and the rider's (619 days, 4.8, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) [F7] supply no fraud or repeat-violation flag, and profiles cannot decide a case in any event. Interim suspension under SAFE-4 is discretionary and is a matter for the reviewer, not the system.

Evidence needed to decide is present: the complaint [F3][F4], the full timestamped chat [F5], and the driver's statement [F6]; nothing outcome-relevant is missing at the screening stage, so the file is complete for a human. I record only the facts, not fault, per SAFE-3.

ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled this trip, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-1 / NS-2 [F4][NS-0]. His app reason was rider_no_show, and his own words — "Waited more than 5 min, cancelling" [F11] and "Rider no-show, so I cancelled" [F14] — read as a cancellation because the rider did not appear; nothing he wrote mentions car trouble, another job or a refusal of the trip, so NS-3 is out and the fee stands or falls under NS-1 [F4][NS-0]. Both advocates read it the same way.

Arrival is settled: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:57:00, 40 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m radius, and his closest approach was 38 m [F7][F1][NS-1]. Continuous presence is settled too: he was stationary at (1.2836, 103.8605), 40 m from the pickup, from 12:57:00 to 13:03:00, with 6 min 15 s cumulative inside 200 m and no GPS gap [F3][F2][NS-1]. Contact is settled: before cancelling he sent two in-app messages (first 12:57:30) and made one in-app call first at 12:58:30 [F5][F10][F13][NS-1].

The wait also clears the threshold. Counting from the later of scheduled pickup and recorded arrival — arrival 12:57:00 — the driver waited 6 min 0 s (360 s) before cancelling at 13:03:00 against the 300 s free wait: 360 s − 300 s = 60 s over [F7][F6][F4][NS-1]. No other scheduled-pickup time appears in the record [F4][F7], and even taking the wait from his first entry within 200 m at 12:56:45 gives 6 min 15 s (375 s) against 300 s: 375 s − 300 s = 75 s over [F2][NS-1]. The rider's own complaint that she "came out a minute after the driver cancelled" at 13:03:00 [F4] confirms she was not at the kerb during the documented wait [F3][F11]. Every NS-1 condition holds and no NS-2 condition fails; the $5.00 fee on record is chargeable and no refund of fare is due [F8][NS-1][NS-2].

Profile facts decide nothing: the rider's and driver's histories are background only and never decide the current case [F18][F19][RD-6]. ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a route deviation: the car ran 13.1 km against an optimal 8.3 km, a +4.8 km deviation well over the 1 km tolerance, billed as excess distance of $6.77 at $1.4097/km [F1][F4][RD-1]. The single off-route segment (09:07–09:14) added 4.67 km, driving Pickering St → Church St → Cecil St → Finlayson Green → Marina Boulevard → MCE → Straits Boulevard → Maxwell Rd → Neil Rd [F3].
