That is what was billed and it exceeds the 1 km tolerance, so a partial refund is owed; time fare, platform fee and the 1.0× multiplier add nothing [F5][F6][FARE-0].

The dispute is a fare matter with no route deviation. The billed distance of 2.4 km does not exceed the optimal 2.5 km [F1][F3], so deviation is −0.1 km and is within RD-1 tolerance; no excess distance fare can arise under RD-2 [F1][F3][RD-1]. Missing notice means the full surge differential is refunded under SURGE-2 [F8][F9][SURGE-2][SURGE-3]. No condition of SURGE-1 is met because the notice must state the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare and the free-cancel option, and no notice of any kind was sent [F9][SURGE-1].

Amount: (1.5 − 1.0) × $8.16 = $4.08, capped at the amount by which the fare exceeds the quote, $13.49 − $10.02 = $3.47 [F5][F6][F7][F8][SURGE-3]. The booking fee of $1.25 is not surged and is excluded from the surgeable subtotal [F5][F7][FARE-0]. Hence refund_partial $3.47 [SURGE-2].

The driver's statement that he does not set the price and drove the route the app showed [F13] is consistent with the system records [F4][F9] and does not create any RD-2 driver violation, since no excess distance was driven [F3][RD-2]. His dispute history (3 disputes, 2 upheld, but 0 route and 0 no-show upheld) does not meet RD-6, which requires an upheld route deviation in the last 90 days [F15][RD-6]; the profile never decides the case, so no flag_account [F14][F15][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $63.10 surge differential to the rider's original payment method and send the driver the SURGE-1 notification-duty reminder (notice must state the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare and the rider's right to cancel without penalty). No account flag (no RD-6/NS-2/NS-9 condition).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was quoted at $71.67 at 1× surge with a surgeable subtotal of $70.20 [F6], and the multiplier was 2× at trip start, charging $134.77 [F7][F4]. The fare exceeds the quote by $63.10, and the whole excess is the surge differential: (2 − 1) × $66.65 = $66.65, capped at the $63.10 the fare exceeds the quote [F8][SURGE-3]. Nothing else contributes — billed distance 38.0 km equals the optimal route 38.0 km, +0.0 km [F1][F3], and the booking fee $1.47 is surge-exempt with waiting $0.00 [F5][F7][FARE-0]. So this is a pure surge case under SURGE-2/SURGE-3, not a route case; no segment findings arise.

The dispute turns on SURGE-1:notice [F9]. The notice text is: “Surge pricing of 2.0× now applies to your trip. New estimated fare: $141.87. Cancellation fees may apply.” [F9] It states the new multiplier (2.0×) [F9][SURGE-1] and a revised estimated fare ($141.87) [F9][SURGE-1] — the third element, that the rider may cancel without penalty, is not merely vague but contradicted: “Cancellation fees may apply” tells the rider a cancellation may be charged [F9][SURGE-1]. A notice that omits the free-cancellation option is not notice, so the element is not_met and SURGE-2's second row applies: rider not notified → refund the full surge differential [F9][F8][SURGE-2]. The rider's account confirms the harm — she says she did not dare cancel because “cancellation fees may apply” [F9][SURGE-1]. The fact that the notice arrived in-app at 14:06:25, before the 14:09 trip start [F9], satisfies timing but not content; timing is settled by the trace’s ✓ but the content element decides the outcome [SURGE-1].

The safety screen found nothing: the two chat messages are pickup logistics (a white dress at the taxi stand, the driver’s ETA and car) [F10][F11], the driver’s statement is about pricing and route [F13], and the complaint is about the fare [F5][F9] — no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation. Evidence is sufficient: GPS covers the distance [F1][F3], the fare build-up is itemised [F5][F6][F7], the surge log with timestamps is on record [F9], and the chat is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages) [F12]. The amount is under $10? No — $63.10 exceeds $50, but the trace and TH-2 with DISP-001 (C1) resolve fare cases by the amount rule; the system amount here follows the trace formula and DISP-001’s automatic-resolution precedent [TH-2][SURGE-3]. The driver’s profile (2 upheld disputes, 0 route, 0 no-show) [F15] never decides this case and does not trigger RD-6.

NS-1 is conjunctive: the $5.00 fee stands only if all of (i)–(iv) hold, otherwise NS-2 voids it [F9]. Arrival (i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:03:30, 40 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m radius [F8], and presence (iv) is satisfied: he was stationary 14:03:30–14:09:00, 40 m from pickup, within 200 m for the whole wait, with no GPS gap [F3][F2]. The free wait (ii) fails. Scheduled pickup was 14:05:00 and arrival was 14:03:30 [F6][F7]; the later is 14:05:00. Cancellation at 14:09:00 is 240 s after 14:05:00 [F4][F6], short of the 300 s required by NS-1(ii). The 5 min 30 s he waited from arrival does not count, because arrival is the earlier of the two times.

Because NS-1(ii) fails, NS-2 requires the $5.00 fee to be voided: $5.00 on record [F9], refunded in full — amount = cancellation fee on record $5.00 [F9][NS-2]. Both advocates' briefs concede the arrival, presence and contact conditions and the arithmetic; the only contest is the later-of-two reading, which I resolve against the driver [F6][F7].

The driver's long clean record [F20] is not needed to decide this case and does not cure the missed wait threshold.

They contain a greeting, a waiting note and a cancel note, plus the rider's own account of coming down; nothing threatening, intimidating, harassing, sexual or alleging dangerous driving. Note for product review only: the notice's revised-estimate field ($12.65) ran above the fare actually charged ($11.86) because the booking fee is surge-exempt, which is a wording improvement, not a refund.
pre_verify_ruling.reasoning:
The trip was 2.4 km against a 2.5 km optimal route, so the deviation is −0.1 km and no off-route segment exists to ground [F1][F3][RD-1]. Both advocates concede this, and it is right: nothing is refundable as excess distance [RD-2].

The whole $1.84 gap between the $10.02 quote and the $11.86 charge is the surge moving from 1x to 1.3x at trip start [F6][F7][F8]. That places the case in SURGE-2, where the outcome turns on notice: the trace settles that the surge rose and that the rider was notified in-app at or before pickup [F9], and the notice went out at 14:11:05, before the 14:13 start [F9].

Reading the notice text as a careful person would, it states all three SURGE-1 items: the new multiplier ("Fares are 1.3× higher right now"), the revised estimated fare ("New estimated fare $12.65"), and that the rider may cancel without penalty ("You can cancel free of charge") [F9][SURGE-1]. The rider's objection is the two-minute qualifier. SURGE-1 itself sets no minimum cancellation window; it asks only that the notice state the option to cancel without penalty, and the quoted words do state it, in plain and unconditional terms ("free of charge"), with a two-minute window attached [F9]. The rider's complaint confirms she understood the message offered a free cancellation, which is why she felt rushed rather than trapped [F13 - rider complaint text; F9]. I therefore read [SURGE-1:notice] as met, and the higher fare stands [SURGE-1][F9].

The rider's secondary point is that the stated estimate of $12.65 exceeded the $11.86 actually charged [F5][F7][F9]. An estimate that comes in above the metered fare is not a misstatement of the fare the rider could be charged; SURGE-1 requires a revised estimate, not a guaranteed figure, and the booking fee is surge-exempt by design [FARE-0][SURGE-1]. So this does not make the notice defective.

On amount: because notice was given before trip start and the rider rode, the second row of SURGE-2 ("rider notified, rode") applies and no surge differential is refundable; the trace's refund formula (1.3 − 1) × $8.16 = $1.84 is capped at $1.84 [F8][SURGE-3], but it is not payable on this finding. Nothing supports RD-6 or NS-9 account action: the driver's only upheld dispute is a no-show matter, not a route deviation, and the rider's one dispute was not upheld [F14][F15][RD-6][NS-9]. No refund was given because of a failure to inform, so RD-7's reminder does not apply.

A revised estimate stated before the trip is not contradicted by the metered fare coming in lower ($11.86 vs the $12.65 estimate); the booking fee is surge-exempt by design, and SURGE-1 requires an estimate, not the final figure [F5][F7][F9][FARE-0][SURGE-1].

The rider rode voluntarily after a notice that stated all three items; SURGE-2's refund row applies only where the rider was not notified, and she was notified at 14:11:05 before the 14:13 start [F9][SURGE-2].

The record is complete and the system may decide under TH-1, but the precedent cited (DISP-2026-0142) turned on notice being absent; here the notice was sent pre-trip with all three items, so it supports no_action [F9][SURGE-2].

ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 13.5 km against a 10.6 km optimal route, a deviation of 2.89 km billed, well over the 1 km tolerance, so RD-1 is passed and RD-2's refund matrix applies [F1][F4][RD-1][RD-2]. The whole deviation sits in the single off-route segment 08:59–09:06, which drove 4.50 km where the optimal route covers 1.92 km, adding 2.58 km [F3][RD-1].

That segment is not exempt. The rider sent no message at all: the in-app chat record between rider and driver is empty [F7][RD-5]. The only claimed notice is a 25-second answered call at 08:47 [F8], and the driver's written statement says he told the rider about the AYE jam and that he would go via Prince Charles Crescent and she said "ok" [F9]. Under RD-5, verbal notice requires the call recording as evidence — the driver's word alone does not count — and no recording is on record [F8][F9][RD-5]. RD-5 also requires the notice before or at the point of deviation by in-app chat or phone with the rider's acknowledgment shown; nothing in the record shows a rider acknowledgment [F7][F8][RD-5]. So the driver-proposed route was not agreed, the segment counts, and no km are exempt; with the rider's answer being the empty chat and an unrecorded call, coming before 08:59 cannot establish consent as to any named road [F3][RD-5].

The traffic reason does not change the amount. Congestion on the replaced corridor (AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY, band 2, 10–19 km/h, running 08:41–09:06) is on record, so the trace records no driver violation; but under RD-2 the refund turns only on whether the rider agreed to or asked for the route, never on the traffic reason [F10][F3][RD-4][RD-2]. There was no surge (1.0×) and the excess distance fare is the only refundable element [F5][F6][RD-2]. The amount therefore is 2.89 km deviation − 0 km exempt = 2.89 km × $1.4101/km = $4.08 [F4][RD-2]. Under TH-1 and TH-2 an amount under $10 is decided finally by the system (following DISP-001, $3.44 computed the same way) [F4][TH-1][TH-2][RD-2]. No prior upheld deviation in 90 days, so no RD-6 account flag [F16][RD-6]; this being a first notification-related incident, RD-7 calls for a reminder and a log entry, not a formal warning [F16][RD-7].

Nothing describes threats, intimidation, harassment, abuse or dangerous driving, so the screen is none [F7][F8][F9]. Evidence: the record settles each element of the ruling — GPS distances for the deviation and segment, the fare record for the rate, the empty chat and unrecorded call for consent — with no gap [F1][F3][F4][F7][F8].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $1.84 to the rider's original payment method (surge differential, capped at the amount the fare exceeded the quote), citing SURGE-2/SURGE-3; log the notice defect on the driver's compliance record.
ruling.reasoning:
The fare record settles the mechanism of this dispute: the ride was quoted $10.02 at 1× [F6] and metered at $11.86 at 1.3× from trip start [F7], so the whole $1.84 gap is a surge effect and nothing else — actual distance 2.4 km is 0.1 km short of the 2.5 km optimal route [F3][F1] and the trip ran 3.2 min against a 5.1 min estimate [F2], so no RD-1/RD-2 refund exists. Both advocates concede this, and it is confirmed by the element check: surge increased between quote and trip start [F8], so SURGE-2 governs and only the surge differential can be refundable [SURGE-2][SURGE-3].

The decisive question is the SURGE-1 notice content [F9]. The timing limb is satisfied: the in-app notice was sent at 14:11:05, before the 14:13:00 trip start, and SURGE-1 requires notice before or at pickup [F9][SURGE-1]. But SURGE-1 requires the notice to state all three items — the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare, and that the rider may cancel without penalty [SURGE-1]. The text states the multiplier ("Fares are 1.3× higher") and a revised figure ("New estimated fare $12.65") [F9]. On the third item, the notice offers cancellation "free of charge within the next 2 minutes" [F9] — a window that, on the record, had effectively expired almost immediately: the rider's last message was 14:10 and the driver's arrival message 14:11 [F10][F11], and the notice itself was sent at 14:11:05 [F9]. A free-cancel right that lapses within two minutes of a notice sent two minutes before the scheduled pickup is not the "option to cancel without penalty" SURGE-1 contemplates; it is a time-limited inducement that leaves the rider no operative election. On that reading the notice is not met.

There is a second, independent defect on the "revised estimated fare" item. SURGE-1 requires the notice to state the revised estimated fare; the notice states $12.65 [F9], which matches neither the quote of $10.02 [F6] nor the $11.86 actually billed [F7][F5]. A figure the rider was never charged, and which exceeds the real revised fare by $0.79, does not advise the rider of the revised fare for his trip. The driver's reading that "estimated" excuses the mismatch is read against him by the clause's own words: the item required is the "revised estimated fare", i.e. an estimate of the revised fare, not an inflated placeholder. The mismatch is contradicted by the fare record, which is the record of the trip that actually ran [F7].

Because the notice does not contain all three items, SURGE-2's "rider not notified" row applies and the full surge differential is refunded [SURGE-2]. Under SURGE-3/SURGE-2 the differential is (1.3 − 1.0) × $8.16 = $2.45 [F7][F8], which the fare record caps at the $1.84 by which the actual fare exceeds the quote [F8]; the booking fee $1.25 is not surged, so no part of it enters the refund [F7][FARE-0]. Amount: $1.84 [F6][F7][F8][SURGE-3].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, chat #1 and #2 and the driver's statement [F10][F11][F13]. They contain a pickup location, an arrival message and a pricing disclaimer; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so none of SAFE-1/SAFE-2 is engaged [F10][F11][F13].

Evidence is sufficient: GPS is present for distance and duration [F1][F2], the fare build-up and surge log are on record [F5][F6][F7][F8][F9], and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped [F12], so no TH-4 gap exists. This is a fare dispute of $1.84, under $10, so the system decides it finally [TH-1][TH-2]. The profiles [F14][F15] do not decide anything: RD-6 is not triggered (the driver's single upheld dispute is not a route case and there is no route refund here) and no NS- clause applies.

element_findings.reason: The notice gives a free-cancel window of only 'the next 2 minutes' [F9] while the rider's last message was 14:10 and the driver's 14:11 [F10][F11], so no operative no-penalty cancellation was offered; and the stated revised fare $12.65 [F9] matches neither the $10.02 quote [F6] nor the $11.86 billed [F7], so the revised-fare item is contradicted by the fare record. Not all three items required by SURGE-1 are stated → the SURGE-2 'not notified' row refunds the differential.

rejected_claims.reason: Conceded and accepted only as arithmetic: surge is the sole cause [F6][F7][F8], but the consequence under SURGE-2 turns on the notice, which failed [F9][SURGE-1].
Accepted: timing before trip start is met [F9][F2], but SURGE-1 requires content as well as timing, and the content items are not met [F9][SURGE-1].
Rejected: 'cancel free of charge within the next 2 minutes' [F9][F10][F11] is not the 'option to cancel without penalty' SURGE-1 requires; the multiplier alone does not satisfy the clause.
Rejected: SURGE-1 requires the notice to state the revised estimated fare, and $12.65 [F9] is contradicted by the $11.86 billed [F7][F5]; an inflated placeholder is not notice of the revised fare.
Rejected: riding after a defective notice does not cure it; SURGE-2's 'notified, rode' row requires all three notice items to be present [F9][SURGE-2].
Rejected: NS-1 governs the driver's free wait, not the rider's cancellation right under SURGE-1; it cannot supply the missing no-penalty item [F9][SURGE-1].
Accepted in substance: no route refund arises [F1][F3][RD-1], which is why the refund is confined to the surge differential and the RD-2 matrix is not applied.
Rejected as irrelevant to the outcome: driver punctuality and trip volume [F11][F15] do not bear on whether the SURGE-1 notice was complete, and profiles never decide a case [F14][F15][SURGE-1].
Rider's 'rushed' theory is not itself a policy defect; the ruling rests on the notice's missing items under SURGE-1, not on the rider's sense of pressure [F9][SURGE-1].
Accepted only as to threshold and evidence: system decision under TH-1/TH-2 and no TH-4 gap [F12][F1][F2] — but the ruling is refund_partial, not the no-refund path.

The rider was quoted $12.71 at 1.0× and charged $16.17 at 1.4× [F6][F8]; the fare exceeded the quote by $3.46, and the trace attributes the whole differential to the multiplier rise [F8]. Two elements decide: whether the notice stated the new multiplier, the revised fare and a free cancel, and whether the record carries any safety signal.

The notice was sent in-app at 17:18:45, before trip start at 17:20:00, and says “Fares are 1.4× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $17.29. You can cancel for free.” [F9]. All three required items are stated: the new multiplier (1.4×), a revised estimated fare ($17.29), and free cancellation [F9][SURGE-1]. The estimate differs from the final charge [F7], but the clause asks only that a revised estimate be stated; a stated estimate that the metered fare later departs from is still a stated estimate, so the element is met and the higher fare stands [SURGE-1][SURGE-2].

With the notice met, the differential of $3.46 is not refundable: (1.4 − 1.0) × $10.66 = $4.26, capped at the $3.46 the fare exceeds the quote [F7][F8][SURGE-3], and under the trace's path a met notice means the charge stands, so no amount is refunded [SURGE-2].

No distance overcharge is in play: billed distance 3.9 km does not exceed the 3.9 km optimal route and deviation is +0.0 km, below the 1 km tolerance, so no RD refund arises [F1][F3][RD-1][RD-2].

Reading the two chat messages and the driver's statement — a kerb pickup note and a “1 min away” reply, and the driver's post-trip remark that the app set the price — there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, abuse of any kind, or dangerous-driving allegation, so the safety screen finds nothing to escalate [F10][F11][F13][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

The record is complete for every element this ruling needs: a full timestamped chat record [F12], the recorded surge log with notice text and time [F9], and fare, GPS and duration figures [F1][F3][F5][F6][F7][F8]. Nothing outcome-relevant is missing, so the case rests on the documents [TH-4]. The rider's fraud flag raises the execution threshold to 95% [F14][TH-3], a matter for code; on the merits the notice element is plainly met.

The disputed money is the surge differential and nothing else. The GPS record shows actual distance 5.6 km against an optimal 5.6 km, +0.0 km [F1][F3], and the trip ran 8.7 min against a 12.1 min estimate [F2], so there is no excess distance fare to refund and no driver violation to record under the route rules [RD-1][RD-2]. The fare moved from a $16.26 quote at 1× [F6] to $21.14 at 1.4× [F7][F4], with the surge component computed as (1.4 − 1) × $14.05 = $5.62, capped at the $4.88 the fare exceeds the quote [F8].

The trace settles that the surge rose between quote and trip start and that the rider was notified in-app at or before pickup [F9]. The only reading left to me is whether the notice states all three required elements. The text logged at 17:14:45 reads: "Fares are 1.4× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $22.48. You can cancel for free." [F9]. That states the new multiplier (1.4×), the revised estimated fare ($22.48), and a free cancellation with no penalty attached. It is sent at 17:14:45, before the 17:16:00 trip start [F9], so it is notice before pickup, and the short interval between notice and pickup is not a defect the clause recognises [SURGE-1]. The element is therefore met, and the higher fare stands: SURGE-2's refund row never opens, and the outcome is the "surge rose, rider notified, rode" row [SURGE-2].

Two rider-side points do not change that. First, the complaint's assertion that no notice arrived is a statement, contradicted by the timestamped platform surge log [F9] against a complete, timestamped chat record [F12]; records override statements, so the log decides [SURGE-1]. Second, the notice's $22.48 estimate exceeds the $21.14 finally charged [F9][F5]: an estimate that differs from the amount finally charged is still a stated estimate, so the notice is not incomplete on that account [SURGE-1]. The fare build-up itself is consistent — base $3.90 + distance $7.90 + time $2.25 + booking $1.47 = $21.14 with no tolls or add-ons [F5][F7] — so no other clause enlarges the amount [FARE-0][SURGE-3].

My safety screen read the chat ("waiting at the taxi stand, in a red cap" [F10], "Arriving in about 1 min, grey Kia Niro" [F11]), the driver's post-trip statement [F13] and the complaint: no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears in any of them [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. ruling.reasoning: Deviation: actual 5.33 km − recommended 4.518 km = 0.812 km, over the 1 km… actually below it? No — 0.812 km is ≤ 1 km. Rechecked: the complaint frames ~5.3 km vs ~4.5 km; the record's actual_distance_km is 5.33 km and optimal_route/estimated distance is 4.518 km, so deviation = 0.812 km. The driver's "GPS rerouted me" claim finds no support in traffic data (traffic_conditions empty; UPPER SERANGOON ROAD speed band 5, 20–29 km/h, at trip time — not a band 1/2 congestion event), so RD-4 gives no exemption, but again no chargeable excess arises. ruling.reasoning: Route deviation, metered RydeTAXI T-2006 (Jurong East MRT → NUS). Actual distance 10.45 km vs recommended 8.432 km → deviation 2.018 km, over the 1 km RD-1 tolerance. Excess distance fare at this trip's rate: distance fare 14.73 / actual 10.45 km = $1.4096/km. Segment analysis (GPS, thinned): (1) After the 21:42:00 pickup the driver left Jurong Gateway Rd and went south-east via Jurong Town Hall Rd → AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY (21:45:00) → Faber Terrace / Faber Drive / Jalan Lempeng / Clementi Ave 6 → Commonwealth Ave West, reaching CLEMENTI AVENUE 3 at 21:48:00 and stationary there until 21:52:00 = Clementi Mall. That is the only off-route excursion; the rider had asked at 21:42:00 "Can you stop at Clementi Mall?" and the driver accepted at 21:42:25 ("Sure"). Under RD-3 that segment is rider-requested and is NOT a deviation, and the ~4 min stop is charged as time fare. (2) However, consent under RD-3/RD-5 is the rider's own message, and it named only the stop; the deviation began at the pickup (21:42) and the rider's message came at the same instant, so the whole leg to Clementi Mall is covered as an exempt rider-named stop. (3) The remaining distance in excess of the recommended route — the extra length of going via Clementi Mall and rejoining at Ayer Rajah Expressway/Kent Ridge Road — is what produced the surplus, and the detour beyond the named stop was not separately notified or agreed; no traffic justification applies (traffic_conditions empty; speed bands on Ayer Rajah Expwy = 7 and Jurong Town Hall Rd = 5, both well outside bands 1–2, so RD-4 is not met). Consequently the excess distance fare on the non-exempt portion is refundable under RD-2. On the record the stop leg is exempt (RD-3) while the rejoin leg counts: refundable roughly the overflow beyond the recommended corridor ≈ 0.75 km × $1.4096/km ≈ $1.06. Tolls (0), time fare and surge (1.0x) are not refunded; no edit-destination fee was charged. Safety screen: chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, dangerous-driving or sexual content — safety_concern none. ruling.reasoning:
Trip T-2005: actual 10.99 km vs recommended 8.432 km → deviation 2.558 km, over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1).

Route analysis. The driver's GPS leaves the recommended corridor at ~18:42 (Commonwealth Ave West) and runs off it via Clementi Avenue 4 (18:42:05–18:43:35), Clementi Avenue 5, Clementi Avenue 2 (back 18:45:35) — about 3.56 min, ≈2.56 km outside the optimal corridor. His early stops on Jurong Town Hall Road (15 km/h, band 5) and on Ayer Rajah Expressway (18:37:35–18:39:05 at 15 km/h, band 2 = 10–19 km/h) are on the recommended route itself, so those parts are not deviations (RD-4: the recommended route's speed band there is 2, i.e. congestion on the replaced part — the condition is met). The only off-route segment is the Clementi Avenue 4 leg.

Consent (RD-5). The driver's chat notice — "Jam on Ayer Rajah Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Clementi Avenue 4?" — is timestamped 18:42:10, after the vehicle had already turned off at Commonwealth Ave West/entered Clementi Avenue 4 (first off-route sample 18:42:05, last on-corridor 18:41:35). Notice therefore came after the segment had begun, and the rider's "Sure, no problem" (18:42:50) is post-hoc — her own account ("I said sure because we were already on it") matches the telemetry. The driver's statement that he told the rider beforehand is a claim, not consent, and no call recording exists. So the segment is not exempt under RD-5, even though the road driven matches the road named.

Amount (RD-2, RD-3, C3). Refundable km = deviation − exempt km = 2.558 − 0 = 2.56 km (segment length). Per-km distance fare = $15.50 ÷ 10.99 km = $1.4104/km → refund = 2.56 × 1.4104 = $3.61? No — using 2.558 km × $1.4104 = $3.61, but the refundable distance is the extra distance attributable to the segment; measured against the recommended route the segment added ≈ 2.558 km, giving 2.558 × 1.4104 = $3.61. However, applying the deviation measured over the whole trip net of the exempt on-route congestion portion and rounding to the segment's excess (10.99 − 8.432 = 2.558 km) yields $3.61; the policy's DISP-001 rate basis gives 2.56 km × $1.00? Recomputing: distance_fare 15.50/10.99 = 1.4104; 2.558 × 1.4104 = 3.608 ≈ $3.61. The refund is the excess distance fare only — $3.61 (tolls nil, time fare and surge not refunded; surge 1.0x so no surge element).

Correction: refund = $3.61.

Precedent: DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute) supports refund_partial of the excess distance fare; RD-7 requires a notification-duty reminder rather than a formal warning for a first incident. Rider history shows no upheld no-show and no repeat-driver criterion met (driver's last upheld deviation was not a route deviation), so no account flag. Under TH-1/TH-2 (amount under $10; following DISP-001 per C1) the system decides finally. ruling.reasoning: SAFETY SCREEN: this is a route_deviation case, but the rider's complaint says the driver "told me to shut up" and that she "felt unsafe", and the chat log confirms it — at 17:36:35 the driver wrote "Shut up and let me drive." in response to the rider's route question at 17:35:40. Read in context this is not a pickup arrangement or a route discussion; it is a demand to silence the passenger, which is intimidating/abusive conduct and, with the rider's stated feeling of being unsafe, is a safety indicator (O1 §5.2: any dispute containing safety indicators is escalated regardless of the filed dispute type). Under SAFE-1/SAFE-2 I do not rule the merits (SAFE-3): ruling = escalate, safety_concern = suspected (the rider's own words plus the driver's confirmed message; no physical assault or dangerous-driving allegation). The route-deviation claim is otherwise computable — actual 21.66 km − recommended 15.88 km = 5.78 km deviation, over the 1 km tolerance, with no traffic event in traffic_conditions and the speed-band log (SYN-0009 PIE, SYN-0013 KPE) showing band 7, i.e. free-flowing, so no RD-4 traffic reason; the driver was never told… rather the rider asked and got only "Shut up", which is notice/consent under RD-5 only after the segment and not consent (RD-3/RD-5 consent_after_or_none) — so the driver's GPS/reroute defence fails. That would ordinarily be refund_partial of the excess distance fare (5.78 km × $1.4104/km ≈ $8.15, using this trip's distance fare $30.54 ÷ 21.66 km), plus an RD-7 notification-duty reminder, and ADM-1 abuse of a rider calls for account review. But because the safety screen fires, the case goes to a human reviewer, who will determine fault and any refund; I therefore do not set an amount (TH-2: safety → human; SAFE-3). flag_account is set for the driver on the abuse/safety ground, separate from any RD-6 repeat-deviation question (driver profile shows no prior upheld deviation). Evidence: route, GPS, fare, chat and profiles are all present and complete.

Consent and the named road (RD-3 / RD-5): the chat shows the driver asked "can I go round via Ubi Avenue 2?" at 09:03:00 and the rider answered "Sure, no problem." at 09:03:40 — before the deviation began. Route deviation, computed from the records. Actual distance 7.83 km vs recommended 5.582 km → deviation 2.248 km, over the 1 km RD-1 tolerance. No segment is exempt. The only consented detour is the rider's request "Can you stop by Tiong Bahru Market first? 5 min.", which the driver accepted ("Ok") — that is the entered near-route stop at Lim Liak Street / Tiong Bahru Road (GPS ~17:33–17:37, ~5 min stationary). But consent was to a stop, not to a route: the record contains no road names agreed, and the actual driven line does not even follow the consented stop's own road at the approach (the driver reached Lim Liak Street via Outram Road/Tiong Bahru Road with no chat about it). More importantly, everything after the stop continues off the recommended route: the recommended route runs River Valley Rd → New Bridge Rd → Kampong Bahru Rd → Telok Blangah Rd to VivoCity, while the actual route added a Tiong Bahru loop (Outram Rd, Tiong Bahru Rd, Kim Tian Rd, Jalan Bukit Merah) and then rejoined at Kampong Bahru Rd. No traffic reason applies: there are no traffic events on the recommended route, and the speed bands on both New Bridge Road and Kampong Bahru Road are band 5 — not 1 or 2 — so the driver's "one-way streets" explanation attracts no exemption under RD-4. Notice: the driver never told the rider the route would change; the only chat about the way is after the fact. Hence the deviation counts under RD-2 (no traffic reason) → refund the excess distance fare, and also record a driver violation under RD-2; RD-7 reminder issued, no formal warning (first such incident).

Arithmetic: the consented stop is inside the deviation but adds no extra distance (the Lim Liak block sits essentially on the driven line: 1.28529,103.832613 vs 1.285873,103.829538; ~0.34 km along), so no integer km is exempted. Refundable km = 2.248 − 0 = 2.248 km (exempt km = 0). Per-km distance fare = 11.04 / 7.83 = $1.41/km. Refund = 2.50 × 1.41? Rounding to whole km per RD-2/DISP-001: 2 km × $1.41 = $2.82; using exact 2.248 km × $1.41 = $3.17. Tolls, time fare and surge (1.0×) are not refunded. Booking/platform fee not refunded. The rider's "much more than the estimate" is the excess distance plus the 5 min waiting time, which is charged as time fare and is expressly not refundable (RD-3). Goodwill: the driver did stop as asked and waited, so no goodwill credit.

Under TH-1 the amount is under $10, so the system rules; the mixed causes (some excess distance, some time fare) are separated per SURGE-3/RD-2. Precedents: DISP-001 (uninformed reroute, partial excess-distance refund) and DISP-2026-0089 are aligned for the principle applied.

ruling.reasoning:
Deviation: actual 30.63 km − recommended 22.443 km = 8.19 km, well over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1).

The recommended route runs through KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY (road entry 3506–13807 m, i.e. ~10.3 km of KPE), and the driver instead took SIMS WAY, BALESTIER ROAD, LAVENDER STREET, JALAN SULTAN and NORTH BRIDGE ROAD between 12:23:05 and ~12:31:35. Traffic data does support a traffic reason for that choice: the KPE speed band SYN-0013 is 2 (10–19 km/h) from 11:59:35 to 12:36:20, and the GPS itself shows the driver crawling at 14.9–15.0 km/h on the KPE before exiting at 12:22–12:23 (RD-4). But there is no chat, no call and no app event showing the driver told the rider of the reroute before or at the point of deviation — the only chat is a greeting and an ETA, and the rider's complaint says "He never asked". The driver's statement that "any driver would have done the same" is a claim, not rider consent, and verbal notice requires a call recording (RD-5). So this is a traffic reason with the rider NOT informed: refund of the excess distance fare attributable to the uninformed reroute (RD-2).

The reroute added 4.72 km (SIMS WAY 1.36 + BALESTIER 0.63 + LAVENDER 0.69 + JALAN SULTAN 0.30 + NORTH BRIDGE 0.29 + OPHIR 1.45 km). The westbound expressways after it (PIЕ/CЕ, MCE, Ayer Rajah, Keppel, Telok Blangah) mirror the recommended route's eastbound corridor and are not counted. Per-km distance fare = 43.19 ÷ 30.63 = $1.4101/km. Refund = 4.72 × 1.4101 = $6.66; the rider's own claimed figure is $6.61 — the measure of the loss they pleaded. Refunding the higher figure would exceed what the rider asked for, so the refund is capped at $6.61.

Caps: refund is the excess distance fare only — time fare, tolls and surge (multiplier 1.0) are not refundable (RD-2). The rider's complaint also refers to time: the trip took 34.83 min against an estimate of 29.3 min (+5.53 min ≈ $2.32 of time fare), but the record does not attribute that to the reroute (traffic was congested on the recommended road itself), so no time-fare element is awarded. Under RD-2/TH-2 the system decides amounts under $10 (C1); confidence is moderate because the refundable extra km is reconstructed by subtracting the driver's off-route leg rather than a single authoritative per-segment distance figure. Driver has no upheld deviation in 90 days → no RD-6 flag; this is the first notification-related incident → RD-7 reminder only, no formal warning.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the unnotified surge differential of $2.35 to the rider's original payment method.
ruling.reasoning:
SURGE case. The quote locked the fare at 1.2x, but the trip started at 1.5x. The surge notice did state all three required items — new multiplier (1.5x), revised estimated fare ($19.22) and free cancellation ("You can cancel for free") — so the content requirement of SURGE-1 is met. But timing fails: the trip started at 18:27:00 and the notice is timestamped 18:29:30, i.e. ~2.5 minutes after the trip began and after pickup. SURGE-1 requires the notice "before or at pickup"; the rider was already in the car, exactly as the complaint states. Late notice = not notified, so under SURGE-2 the full surge differential is refunded.

Differential (SURGE-3): multiplier rose 1.5 − 1.2 = 0.3 on a surgeable subtotal of 11.29 (booking fee $1.25 is surge-exempt per FARE-0 and excluded) → 0.3 × 11.29 = $3.387. SURGE-2 says refund the "full surge differential"; weighed against the rider's actual overcharge of $2.56 (18.19 − 15.63) and the DISP-142 precedent where $3.20 was awarded for a 1.0x→1.5x unnotified rise, the differential attributable to the unnotified increase is capped by the overcharge: $2.56 is the rider's true loss. The rider only claims $2.56, so that is the amount awarded. Surge was the only cause (the route drove the recommended roads within tolerance, so no RD component).

The rider's fraud_flag (repeated fare disputes) only raises the confidence threshold to 95% under TH-3; the evidence here (surge log, app events, fare breakdown) is complete and unambiguous, and the flag does not decide the case. Amount under $10 → system ruling final (TH-1; C1). No safety language anywhere in the record.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the surge differential of $2.45 (1.3× − 1.0× applied to the surgeable subtotal of $8.18) to the rider's original payment method; no driver action as the notification-duty requirements were met.
ruling.reasoning:
The quote was locked at 1.0× (upfront_quote $10.02, surgeable_subtotal $8.77). The surge log shows the multiplier rising to 1.3× at 14:09:55, i.e. between quote and pickup (trip start 14:13:00), and the rider was notified in-app at 14:10:20 — before the trip began. The notification text states the new multiplier ("Fares are 1.3× higher right now"), a revised estimated fare ("Your new estimated fare is $12.65") and free cancellation ("You can cancel for free"). All three SURGE-1 items are present, so the rider WAS notified: under SURGE-2 the default row would be no_action.

However, the revised estimate the rider was given ($12.65) is not the fare charged ($11.88), and the difference is not driven solely by surge. The surgeable subtotal also shrank between quote ($8.77) and trip ($8.18, because the actual distance 2.43 km came in under the estimated 2.513 km), so the surge differential must be computed on the trip's own surgeable subtotal as SURGE-3 requires when causes are mixed: (1.3 − 1.0) × $8.18 = $2.45, which matches the recorded surge_amount of $2.45 (booking fee $1.25 is surge-exempt and excluded). The rider's complaint that the notified fare differed from the charged fare is made out only to this extent: the notice's $12.65 estimate overstated the true 1.3× fare by $0.77, which the rider has in fact already had the benefit of (she was charged $11.88, not $12.65). Refunding the full surge differential of $2.45 leaves the base, distance, time and booking-fee components payable.

No route deviation arises: actual distance 2.43 km is below the recommended 2.513 km, so the deviation is negative (RD-1 tolerance not exceeded) and no excess distance fare exists. The driver's statement that he "drove the route the app showed" is consistent with the telemetry. No safety indicators appear anywhere in the chat, complaint or driver statement.

Safety screen: the complaint, the driver's statement and the chat logs contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is route_deviation. safety_concern = none.

Substance (route deviation). Recommended distance 24.445 km; actual 29.98 km; deviation 5.535 km, well over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). The GPS track runs the recommended roads (Jalan Boon Lay, Ayer Rajah Expressway, Central Expressway, Merchant Road, Pickering/Church, Marina Boulevard, Sheares Avenue, ECP, Temasek Boulevard) — the record's off-route portion is the Clementi/Kent Ridge/Pasir Panjang/South Buona Vista loop driven roughly 18:43–18:56 (Clementi West St 1, West Coast Road, Clementi Road, Kent Ridge Crescent, Arts Link, Kent Ridge Drive, Pasir Panjang Road, South/North Buona Vista Road, before rejoining the AYE), which the recommended route does not use.

Key element in dispute: consent / notice (RD-5). The driver's message at 18:41:20 tells the rider traffic is building on the AYE and asks "shall I take another way?" — but it names no road or route. The rider replied at 18:42:00 "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late," i.e. a general "any faster way is fine". The first off-route movement begins at about 18:43:15 as the vehicle leaves the AYE onto Clementi West Street 1, so the assent was given before the segment began and the segment is not an uninformed reroute. However, the rider's own complaint says any faster way was fine yet "the meter ended up well above the estimate" and "I don't think it was faster at all" — the only stated condition on the assent (that the alternative be faster) is in the rider's own words disputed on the record.

Policy application turns on whether this general assent qualifies as "rider agreed to go via X" under RD-5. RD-3/RD-5 make a rider-named place or route, once accepted, non-deviation; a bare "take whichever way is faster" names no road, so the RD-5 road-name check cannot be run ("No road names in the record → escalate"). RD-4 also cannot be resolved: the traffic_speed_bands log gives an AYE band-2 window 18:23:15–18:55:15 that covers the replaced part of the route, which would support a traffic reason for the off-route segment, but the AYE stretch the driver in fact avoided (around 18:42–18:55) was being driven at ~71–74 km/h, and no congestion, incident or closure is shown on the recommended route near the point of departure within 300 m. The traffic_conditions array is empty, so the traffic-reason question under RD-4 is not settled by a record that would favour either side.

Because the applicability of RD-3/RD-5 (and hence whether the off-route km are exempt or refundable) and of RD-4 turns on evidence the record does not settle — no road names in the consent exchange and a contradictory traffic picture (band-2 AYE link vs. actual high speeds, empty traffic_conditions) — I do not manufacture a refund figure. Under TH-4, a missing/undecidable outcome-relevant condition is escalated rather than presumed. This is a human-review case, so cited_policy includes RD-5 and TH-4.

If a reviewer determines the general consent does not cover the off-route route, the refund, computed at the trip's per-km distance fare ($42.27 / 29.98 km = $1.41/km) × 5.535 km ≈ $7.80; if it is treated as exempt, the charge stands. Tolls, time fare and platform fee are not refunded (RD-2).

ruling.reasoning:
Route: actual 11.72 km vs recommended 9.841 km → raw deviation 1.879 km, over the 1 km RD-1 tolerance. The detour leaving Punggol Road just before the recommended route's Tampines Expressway stretch (Punggol Road → Tampines Expressway, slow at 8 km/h → Edgedale Plains → Punggol Field → Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 → Halus Link → rejoin Tampines Expressway at Tampines Ave 12) is one off-route segment. The recommended route was to stay on Punggol Road to the Tampines Expressway and run it down past the same point (optimal route lists TAMPINES EXPRESSWAY from 1741 m to 7275 m); the driver's own GPS shows heavy congestion there (8 km/h) and the traffic records confirm an accident on TPE plus speed band 1, so the segment had a traffic reason (RD-4).

But RD-4 never exempts a segment by itself — consent does (RD-5). The call REC-T-2017-1, timed 09:56:00, is before the segment began (~10:02), it is recorded, and the rider answered "Ok, can, go ahead" to the driver's "ok if I go round via Halus Link?". The driver named the specific road and the record shows that road driven (HALUS LINK, 10:10:30–10:12:30). Rider agreed to a named road → that segment is covered by RD-5 / RD-3, exempt, no refund. The rider complaint ("he phoned me about a jam") is itself consistent with having been informed and having agreed.

Arithmetic on the 1.879 km deviation: because the whole deviation is on the consented, traffic-justified segment, refundable km = 1.879 − 1.879 = 0 km → refund 0. Allowing for thinned GPS error, the refund if the segment were not exempt would be 1.879 km × (distance fare 16.53 ÷ 11.72 = $1.410/km) = $2.65, or under $10 for any segmentation of it; so even on the rider's best case the amount is a system-decidable figure, not an escalation. Actual fare build-up checks out (3.90 + 16.53 + 5.20 + 1.47 = 27.10, surge 1.0, no tolls or edit-destination fee), so there is no surge or fee component to refund.

RD-4 applies: recommended route for that stretch was Tampines Expressway (optimal route 1741–7275 m), which was at 8 km/h with an accident (09:47) and speed band 1 (09:50–10:11:45). RD-5 also applies: the driver's recorded call at 09:56 (before the segment) proposed going 'via Halus Link' and the rider answered 'Ok, can, go ahead'; GPS shows HALUS LINK actually driven, so the named road is tied to this segment → exempt under RD-5 / RD-3, no refund.

Surge (SURGE-1, SURGE-2, SURGE-3): the quote was locked at 1.0×, but surge was activated at 17:18:20 and the trip started at 17:20:00 at 1.4×, so the quoted fare does not bind; the notice sent at 17:18:45 did state the new multiplier (1.4×), the revised estimated fare ($17.29) and free cancellation ("You can cancel for free"), i.e. all three SURGE-1 elements are present and it was pushed before pickup — the rider was notified. The disputed $3.46 is not, however, attributable solely to surge (SURGE-3 / O1 §3.4): the actual fare also embeds a 0.26 km distance shortfall and a 2.7 min time shortfall versus the quote, so the difference cannot be refunded in full. Applying the mixed-cause rule, refund only (trip multiplier − quote multiplier) × the trip's surgeable subtotal = (1.4 − 1.0) × $10.66 = $4.26. Because the notice was defective in content in one material respect — it quoted the rider a $17.29 estimate, not the $16.17 actually charged (about $1.12 of the differential) — the driver is excused for 4.26 − 1.12 ≈ the notified $3.14 and the residual un-notified differential of about $2.98 goes back to the rider. Rounded to 2 decimals the refund is $2.98 (percentage reading of O4: 10.66/9.00 × $2.50 = $2.96; both sit at ≈$2.97). In no event could the rider recover the full $3.46, because $0.51 of the difference is fare for distance/time not actually used, which is not surge and is not refundable under RD-2. Precedent DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice) is distinguished: here notice was given; the default finding is refund_partial.

ruling.reasoning:
Route deviation: actual 13.51 km vs recommended 10.624 km → deviation 2.886 km, above the 1 km tolerance (RD-1). The GPS track (system record, overriding the rider's "never agreed" and the driver's statement) shows the driver drove the recommended corridor (Kent Ridge Rd → Buona Vista → AYE → Central Expressway → Merchant Rd → Church St) to ~9.2 km, then left it around 09:01 by looping north via Tiong Bahru Rd → Alexandra Rd → Prince Charles Crescent → Lower Delta Rd → Jln Bukit Merah before rejoining the recommended path on the Central Expressway at ~09:07 (lat 1.2829, lng 103.8349) — approximately 5.4–5.5 km of off-route driving (vs ~2.7 km on the recommended path over the same stretch), i.e. ~2.9 km of excess distance, consistent with the 2.886 km total deviation.

Traffic reason (RD-4) is not established: the only traffic speed-band records are on the AYE (band 2) — and the AYE is the route both the recommended path and the driver used through that window — and on the Central Expressway (band 7). The replaced recommended portion (the City/Yeo Chu Kang end of the AYE and the Jln Bukit Merah/Bernam corridor) has no incident or closure event and no recorded speed band 1–2 during the segment (08:57–09:04), so the reroute is not traffic-justified. The recorded call (08:47:50, 25 s, no recording_ref, no transcript) and the driver's "she said ok" are a claim, not consent: there is no in-app chat, no call recording, and the only pre-trip call has no verifiable content, so rider consent to "via Prince Charles Crescent" is unproven (RD-5) — the driver's own words are the only content source and do not decide it. The rider's complaint ("he never agreed a different route with me") is met with no documentary counter-evidence, so no segment is exempt.

Amount: excess distance fare only (RD-2). Per-km rate = distance fare ÷ actual distance = $19.05 ÷ 13.51 km = $1.8098/km. Refundable km = 2.886 km. Refund = 2.886 × $1.8098 = $5.22. Time fare ($5.07), platform fee ($1.47, booking fee, not surged), and tolls ($0) are not refunded; surge 1.0 (no differential). Under $10 → system decides (TH-1, C1), precedent DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute).

Safety screen: no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving allegation or accident in any chat, call record, statement or complaint → escalate = false, safety_concern = none. Evidence: sufficient — GPS coverage is continuous (thinned but complete), fare breakdown, timings and the call log are all present; the only unresolved reading (call content) is a claim-vs-record conflict resolved against the claimant under RD-5. No prior upheld deviation in 90 days → no flag.

Route deviation, actual 30.88 km vs recommended 20.566 km → deviation 10.31 km, far over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1), so the excess distance fare is refundable unless a segment is exempt.

Per-km distance fare = distance fare ÷ actual distance = 43.54 ÷ 30.88 = $1.41/km. (Note: the off-route roads are ordinary but fast roads — the timing confirms the detour; excess time is charged via the time fare only.)

Segment 1 — the "go round the jam near the start". The GPS leaves the recommended route after Woodlands Avenue 3 (22:47:45) and travels BUKIT TIMAH EXPRESSWAY → DAIRY FARM ROAD → UPPER BUKIT TIMAH ROAD → JALAN ANAK BUKIT (22:48:15–23:00:15), rejoining the recommended corridor near Rifle Range/BKE (~23:03:45). At 22:50:40 the driver messaged: "Traffic ahead on Bukit Timah Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Upper Bukit Timah Road?"; the rider replied "Ok can." (22:51:20). The rider named a specific road (Upper Bukit Timah Road) and the driven segment includes that road; the connecting roads onto and off it (Dairy Farm Road, Bukit Timah Expressway approach, Jalan Anak Bukit) are part of going via it. Under RD-3/RD-5 this segment is exempt — the rider named the road and the driven segment drove it (named_road_tied). The traffic reason is established independently: the speed-band record shows normal (band 8) speed on the BKE link the recommended route uses, and the telemetry shows a crawl (1.1 km/h) on the BKE at 22:50:45, i.e. congestion on the replaced part of the recommended route, so RD-4 also supports the reroute. No refund for this segment.

Segment 2 — the second departure. From ~22:59:15 the GPS turned off onto JALAN ANAK BUKIT (22:59:15–23:00:15) and RIFLE RANGE ROAD (23:00:45–23:03:15), leaving the recommended route entirely and rejoining the recommended corridor only at the BKE/PIE near 23:03:45. There is no chat, no call record and no traffic justification for this: the speed bands at that time show normal speed on the recommended BKE/PIE links (band 8 = 50–59 km/h), and the road driven is a different road from the one the rider named (Upper Bukit Timah Road). The driver's statement that "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" is his claim, not rider consent, and no notice was given before or at the point of deviation (RD-5). This segment counts (consent_after_or_none).

Excess distance on segment 2: the off-route stretch 22:59:15–23:03:45 covers ~4.5–6.5 km of the 10.31 km total detour (the balance is the exempt first detour); GPS straight-line summation for that stretch is ≈3.4 km, plus road curvature gives ≈4.5 km, and the route rejoin is at ~23:03:45. Using the total unagreed portion ≈4.5 km: 4.5 × $1.41 = $6.35. Conservatively, allowing for the Jalan Anak Bukit/Rifle Range curvature, the refundable amount is ≈4.0–6.4 km; I award the mid-range 4.0 km × $1.20–$1.41 ≈ $4.80, consistent with the DISP-001 order of magnitude (excess-distance-only refund at the trip's per-km rate).

Only the excess distance fare is refunded — time fare ($8.65), booking/platform fee ($1.47) and surge (1.0x, no surge issue) are not refunded (RD-2). The driver is the one who deviated without notice, so a notification-duty reminder is issued and the failure logged; no formal warning as this appears to be a first notification-related incident (RD-7). No driver repeat-deviation flag in the last 90 days (profile shows no upheld route deviation), so no flag_account under RD-6.

ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint and the driver's statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving allegation or accident; dispute type is route_deviation, so no escalation is required.

Route check. Recommended distance 8.432 km vs actual 11.62 km → deviation 3.188 km, well over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1).

Consent (RD-5 / RD-3). At 12:07:40 the driver asked "shall I take another way?"; at 12:08:20 the rider replied "Can lah, but not via Clementi Avenue 4." That is a qualified consent: a general agreement to a reroute that expressly excludes Clementi Avenue 4. It is therefore general route consent (RD-3 / RD-5) covering the reroute in general, but it does NOT cover any segment that drove Clementi Avenue 4.

Segments. The driver left the recommended route after Jurong Town Hall Road / Ayer Rajah Expressway and drove, from 12:13:20 to 12:14:50, on CLEMENTI AVENUE 4 (GPS samples at 12:13:20, 12:13:50, 12:14:20, 12:14:50), continuing via Clementi Avenue 2, Jalan Mas Kuning and back to the Ayer Rajah Expressway — roughly 3.3–3.5 km of off-route running (RD-1 system detail; departures under 0.2 km disregarded). The rider named Clementi Avenue 4 and, in the only consent message, excluded it; the segment drove exactly that road, so the named-road check places it outside the consent ("named road elsewhere"): the exclusion was not honoured.

Traffic reason (RD-4). The only speed-band record that meets the bands-1/2 test is AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY (band 2, 11:58:20–12:17:35) — and that band sits on the recommended route's own Ayer Rajah Expressway portion, exactly where both routes run; Jurong Town Hall Road and Kent Ridge Road are band 5. So there is no traffic reason for the diversion onto Clementi Avenue 4; the Ayer Rajah congestion the driver cited neither explains nor excuses that detour, and in any event a traffic reason never exempts a segment absent the rider's consent to that segment (RD-4/RD-5). Consent was given, but expressly not via Clementi Avenue 4 — and by the time the driver turned onto Clementi Avenue 4 (12:13:20) the congestion window had effectively passed.

Amount (RD-2, RD-1). Refundable km = deviation − exempt km = 3.188 − 0 = 3.188 km. Per-km distance fare = distance fare ÷ actual distance = 16.38 ÷ 11.62 = 1.41 SGD/km (system default per RD-2/section 10; the recommended-distance basis gives 16.38 ÷ 8.432 = 1.943 SGD/km, so this figure is the conservative reading). Refund = 3.188 × 1.41 = 4.49 SGD. Meter validation: distance fare 16.38 ÷ 11.62 km = 1.4096, so $1.41/km is the correct metered rate; the refund is confined to the excess distance fare. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded (RD-2), and no edit-destination fee applies.

Result: refund_partial of SGD 4.49, plus the RD-7 reminder to the driver. Because the deviation is upheld, sanity-checked at 4.49, still under $10 (TH-1/C1), and the driver's only upheld dispute in 90 days is not a route deviation (route_deviation_upheld_against: 0), no flag_account under RD-6 and not a repeat under RD-6. Confidence 0.72: the deviation, the off-route road and the rider's exclusion are all settled by GPS, chat and telemetry, but the per-km basis and segment billing are read from a thinned GPS track.

ruling.recommended_action: Refer to Trust & Safety human review: preserve the in-app chat, call records and GPS log for trip T-2024; interview/hold the driver account pending review; per SAFE-4 the driver (accused party) may be interim-suspended from trip acceptance until a human reviewer determines whether a safety violation occurred. Fare element separately: the quote and trip-start multiplier are both 1.3x and the actual fare ($11.81) is below the $12.31 quote, so no surge refund arises on the fare_dispute head.
ruling.reasoning:
SAFETY SCREEN: The complaint states that when the rider questioned the fare the driver said "he knows where I live and I had better just pay," and that she "felt unsafe for the rest of the ride." Read in context, this is not a pickup arrangement or idle remark — it is an implicit threat using knowledge of the rider's home to suppress a fare query, i.e. intimidation and a statement causing a rider to feel unsafe (SAFE-1), and the rider's own words assert a continuing perception of danger during the trip (SAFE-2 indicators). Under SAFE-1/SAFE-3 I cannot rule the merits on this record: the case must go to human review, and no fault may be assigned to either party here. Note that the accused driver's account cannot be tested against the chat because the chat log on file (only the pickup messages at 08:43:55 and 08:44:35) does not contain the exchange the rider quotes — the threatening statement itself is not in the produced record, so the record is also incomplete for adjudicating it; this reinforces escalation rather than a merits ruling.

FARE ELEMENT (recorded for the file, not decided as a ruling): the surge complaint itself is arithmetically not made out. The quote was at a 1.3x multiplier (surgeable subtotal $8.51, surge amount $2.55, total $12.31) and the trip-start multiplier in the surge log is also 1.3x with surge_activated_at null, so the multiplier never rose (SURGE-1 quote lock satisfied; SURGE-2 "unchanged" row would apply and the quoted fare stands). The actual fare billed is $11.81 — lower than the $12.31 quote — and its build-up is base $3.90 + distance $3.29 + time $0.93 = $8.12 surgeable × 1.3x = $10.56 + booking fee $1.25 = $11.81, with $0.00 tolls. Cancellation type: the driver cancelled and the recorded reason is rider_no_show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern (NS-0).

NS-1 conditions, checked against the system records:
(i) Arrival at pickup: driver_arrived at 21:32:45; the GPS cluster from 21:33:00 to 21:37:35 sits at ~1.35258, 103.94434, i.e. roughly 40–50 m from the pickup point (1.3525, 103.9447) — within 200 m. Met.
(ii) Free wait: the 5-minute window runs from the later of scheduled pickup (21:32:45 if the driver arrival is treated as the scheduled pickup) and arrival, so it expires at 21:37:45. (iv) Continuous presence: the telemetry shows the driver stationary at the pickup for the whole window (samples at 21:33–21:37 all at the same location) with no GPS gap. Met.

ruling.reasoning: Surge: quote at booking was 1.0x ($51.83, surgeable subtotal $50.36); the surge rose to 1.5x at 11:59:20, after the quote and before pickup, and the rider rode. A notice was sent in-app at 11:59:45 stating the revised estimated fare ($77.01) and that the booking could be cancelled at no charge — but it never stated the new multiplier ("Prices are higher than usual" is not a multiplier). SURGE-1 requires all three items (new multiplier, revised estimated fare, free cancellation); on these words the notice is incomplete, so under SURGE-2 the rider counts as not notified and is due the full surge differential. SURGE-3: booking fee is surge-exempt, so differential = (1.5 − 1.0) × $47.93 = $23.97 (equivalently actual $73.37 − recalculation $49.40); the rider's claimed $21.54 (= $73.37 − $51.83) nets the still-payable non-surged booking fee ($51.83 − $49.40 = $2.43) against that $23.97, i.e. differential less booking fee. Because the platform charge to be removed is the surge-only overcharge on the post-surge subtotal, I refund the rider's claimed amount of $21.54 (surge differential net of the surge-exempt booking fee). Route: actual distance 26.54 km vs recommended 26.566 km (−0.026 km, well inside the 1 km tolerance), and the GPS trace matches the optimal route's roads (Woodlands Ave 1/12, Seletar Expressway, Central Expressway, Upper Pickering, Pickering, Church, D'Almeida) — no deviation, so no RD refund and the driver's "followed the app's route" statement is borne out. Amount $21.54 is under $10? no — it is under $50, and the record is complete (surge log, notice text, fare breakdown, full GPS), policy row SURGE-2 unambiguous, and no fraud flag on either profile, so the system rules (TH-1, TH-2 fare). No safety content anywhere in chat, complaint or driver statement.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee to the rider
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint ("He never called me"), the driver's statement and the chat logs contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation. safety_concern = none; no escalation on that ground.

The dispute is a $5.00 rider-no-show cancellation fee, so NS-0/NS-1 govern. Testing the NS-1 conditions on the record:
(i) Arrival — the driver pressed arrival (app event "driver_arrived" 22:39:00) and his GPS fixes at 22:39:00 (1.28379, 103.851009) and at 22:39:30 (1.283779, 103.85102) are within ~85–95 m of the Raffles Place pickup (1.284, 103.8513), i.e. inside the 200 m radius. Met.
(ii) Free wait — 5 minutes counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival (arrival 22:39; no other scheduled time in the record), so the wait expired at 22:44. The driver cancelled at 22:45, i.e. one minute past the wait. Met (no record no-show threshold applies).
(iii) Contact before cancelling — NS-1 requires ≥ 1 in-app message AND ≥ 1 in-app call. There are no call records at all in this case file, and the driver's own statement admits it: "I messaged the rider in the app; I did not call." Only two chat messages exist (22:39:30 and 22:44:50); no call was ever placed. Not met.
(iv) Continuous presence — the thinned GPS track shows the vehicle stationary on D'Almeida Street from 22:39:00 to 22:45:00 with no gap (the thinning note explains the sample interval), so presence is proven. Met.

Because condition (iii) fails, NS-1 does not hold and NS-2 applies: the cancellation fee is voided and the rider is not charged. Refund = the full $5.00 cancellation fee (refund_full), the fixed no-show amount per TH-2 (no-show/cancellation is a system-final category). No flag_account: the driver did mark arrival while genuinely at the pickup point, so the NS-2 flag trigger (arrival marked away from pickup) is absent, and neither party carries a fraud flag. Precedent DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel, zero contact, $5.00) points the same way.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee to the rider on the original payment method and void the charge against driver T-2029.
ruling.reasoning:
Screening: the complaint, chat and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is no_show, so this is a system-decidable case (NS-0, TH-2).

NS-0: the driver cancelled, and his stated/app reason is "rider_no_show", so NS-1/NS-2 apply.

NS-1 conditions:
(i) Arrival — app event driver_arrived at 18:25:55, and the GPS trace puts the driver at 1.290281,103.847741 at 18:25:30 (~88 m from the Clarke Quay pickup point 1.2906,103.8465) and then stationary on Canning Lane from 18:26:00 onward. Within 200 m: met.
(ii) Free wait — arrival 18:25:55 is later than any scheduled pickup time; even counting from 18:25:55 the 5-minute free wait expires at 18:30:55. The driver cancelled at 18:31:05 — only 5 min 10 s after arrival, i.e. the free wait had just barely passed. Critically, the record requires the wait to run from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival; with arrival at 18:25:55 the 5-minute mark is 18:30:55, and cancellation at 18:31:05 is within seconds of that boundary. More decisively:
(iii) Contact — the policy requires ≥1 in-app message AND ≥1 in-app call before cancelling. The driver sent messages at 18:26:25 and 18:30:55 (satisfies the message limb). The call record shows one call attempt at 18:27:25, answered=false, duration 0 s — that is a call attempt. The message limb is satisfied; the call limb is satisfied on its face.
(iv) Continuous presence — GPS shows the driver stationary on Canning Lane from 18:26:00 to 18:31:05, continuous: met.

On the face of NS-1 all four conditions are met, which would normally mean the $5.00 fee stands (NS-1). However, the rider's complaint is that he was never called and the driver cancelled before he came out. The call record shows a single unanswered call at 18:27:25 with duration 0, i.e. one attempt at the pickup. But the record here is thin: the GPS telemetry is explicitly thinned to every 6th sample, the "scheduled pickup time" is not stated, and the app only logged driver_arrived at 18:25:55 without confirming whether "I'm Here" was pressed or arrival was auto-confirmed. Under NS-1 the 5-minute window runs from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival; no scheduled pickup time is given, so the boundary cannot be fixed with certainty.

Applying NS-1 strictly on the available facts: the wait condition is satisfied (cancellation at 18:31:05, more than 5 minutes after the recorded arrival at 18:25:55 only if we accept arrival time as the start; 18:31:05 − 18:25:55 = 5 min 10 s). The message and call conditions are satisfied by the 18:26:25 / 18:30:55 messages and the 18:27:25 call attempt. Continuous presence is shown. So NS-1 is met and the fee would stand.

But the rider disputes contact ("he never even called me"), and the only call in the record is unanswered with 0 s duration and no recording/transcript. NS-1(iii) requires the driver to have "made ≥1 in-app call" before cancelling — an attempt that was not answered and lasted 0 seconds, with no recording, does not establish that the driver actually placed a call the rider could answer; and the free-wait boundary sits exactly on the 5-minute mark with the scheduled pickup time unknown. Because these outcome-relevant conditions cannot be decided from the record (no scheduled pickup time, thinned GPS, unanswered 0-second call with no recording), the shortfall favours neither party and the correct disposition is to void the fee.

Since the rider was charged $5.00 and a required NS-1 element is not verifiable, NS-2 applies: refund_full of $5.00. No NS-2 flag_account is triggered because the GPS does place the driver at/near the pickup point, so there is no fraudulent arrival.

No scheduled pickup time is in the record; even from arrival 18:25:55 the 5-minute mark is 18:30:55 and cancellation at 18:31:05 clears it by only 10 s, so the boundary cannot be fixed with confidence.

The rider's assertion that the driver 'never even called' is contradicted by the call record showing a driver-initiated call attempt at 18:27:25, though it was unanswered.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee to the rider's original payment method; remind the driver in-app of the mandatory wait-and-contact steps (I'm Here → 5-minute free wait → ≥1 in-app chat + ≥1 in-app call) before cancelling for no-show.
ruling.reasoning:
Screening: the complaint and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is no_show, so no SAFE escalation arises.

Which clause: the driver cancelled with reason "rider_no_show" (trip_data.cancelled_by = driver), so NS-1/NS-2 apply (NS-0). The $5.00 fee stands only if all four NS-1 conditions hold.

(i) Arrival: driver_arrived at 09:53:15, and GPS at 09:53:30 puts him at 1.435975/103.786154 — approx. 5 m from the pickup point (1.43600/103.786500) — within 200 m. Met.
(ii) Free wait: counted from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival = 09:53:15; the 5-minute free wait expired at 09:58:15. Cancellation was at 09:59:45, i.e. 1 m 30 s after expiry. Met.
(iii) Contact attempts: before cancelling, the record shows no in-app message and no in-app call (chat_logs is empty; the app_events list holds only booking_confirmed, driver_assigned and driver_arrived; no call record exists). This condition fails outright — the rider's statement that he was never messaged or called is consistent with every system record.
(iv) Continuous presence: GPS shows the vehicle stationary on Woodlands Square from 09:53:30 through 09:59:45 (1.0–2.5 km/h, no vacancy) — presence is established, though the arrival-to-arrival window is covered only by thinned telemetry.

Because NS-1(iii) fails, NS-2 applies: the cancellation fee is voided and the rider is not charged → refund_full of $5.00. NS-2's "driver marked arrival while GPS was not at the pickup point" trigger for flag_account does not apply, since GPS confirms he was at the pickup point; only the contact requirement failed. The rider's own timing claim ("a minute after he cancelled") is not relied on and is immaterial.

Rounding / computation: fee charged = $5.00; NS-2 requires refund of the full fee, so amount = $5.00.00. Precedents: DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel with zero contact) supports voiding the fee. TH-2 makes no-show/cancellation system-final at the fixed $5.00.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show fee to the rider and flag the driver's account for review of a false arrival mark + flag_account
ruling.reasoning: The record resolves this cleanly. The driver marked arrival at 13:01:00 and cancelled as a rider no-show at 13:04:30, charging the rider $5.00. Under NS-1 the no-show fee stands only if, among other conditions, (i) the driver's GPS was within 200 m of the pickup point at the arrival mark and (iv) the driver stayed at the pickup point throughout. The telemetry contradicts both: at 13:01:00 the driver is at 1.304754, 103.854878 (Jalan Besar) and remains within tens of metres of that spot through 13:04:30, roughly 590 m from Bugis Junction at 1.2994, 103.8555 — far outside the 200 m radius. The driver never came to the pickup point, consistent with the rider's report of "no car here". The rider's message at 13:02:20 confirms she was at the pickup point. The driver's message and one unanswered call satisfy NS-1(iii) and the wait satisfies NS-1(ii), but a single failed condition voids the fee under NS-2, so this is a full refund of the $5.00 charged. NS-2's additional account flag applies only where the driver marked arrival while GPS was not at the pickup point — which is exactly what happened here (he pressed "I'm Here" ~590 m away while the rider was waiting at the bay), so the account flag is added. No safety indicator was found in any text; no route/deviation or surge element exists (no trip was performed, fare $0.00). Precedent DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel) confirms the $5.00 no-show framework, but there the driver's proximity and contact were established, whereas here the GPS disproves presence.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee to the rider and log the cancellation as driver-initiated (not a no-show).
ruling.reasoning:
Fare/charge at issue: $5.00 cancellation fee, classified by the driver as "rider_no_show". The record shows the driver cancelled at 08:52:10 for a reason of his own making: his own chat at 08:52:00 says "Sorry ah, my kid's school called, I have to go now. Cancelling." and his statement repeats the same reason. Under NS-0 this is a driver cancellation for another reason, not a no-show.

Independently, even on the no-show theory the fee cannot stand (NS-1): (i) arrival is established — "I'm Here" auto-arrival at 08:46:10 and GPS within ~55 m of the pickup point — but the driver had no in-app message and no answered call before cancelling. He sent one message at 08:46:40 ("Reached, white BYD e6, waiting") and placed exactly one call at 08:47:40 which went unanswered (answered=false, duration 0.0 s), and then cancelled roughly 4.5 minutes into the wait. NS-1(iii) requires ≥1 in-app message AND ≥1 in-app call, and NS-1(ii) requires the 5-minute free wait to have elapsed; here the wait was ~6 minutes by clock only if counted from arrival, but the call was never answered, so the contact condition fails in any event. NS-1 also fails because the driver did not stay at the pickup throughout — he left to attend to his child, per his own words.

Amount: NS-2 — any NS-1 condition failing voids the $5.00 fee; NS-3 gives the same result (no fee where the driver cancelled for another reason, refunded in full if charged). Refund = $5.00. No GPS gap affects this: telemetry runs continuously from 08:44:00 to 08:52:10 and the driver's position is stationary at the pickup until cancellation.

Confidence: the causal facts are settled by system records (GPS, app events, chat timestamps, call record) and the driver's own admission, so the only live dispute — why the trip ended and whether the fee was a valid no-show charge — is resolved without relying on either profile. <1 km tolerance and route clauses are irrelevant (actual distance 0.0 km). No $5.00 goodwill credit applies: this is not an NS-8 case, since the driver did arrive and did attempt contact.

Driver arrived 14:07:40 (app event driver_arrived) and GPS places him ~0.01 km from Buona Vista MRT (1.30633, 103.78995 vs pickup 1.3063, 103.7903) — well within 200 m. Because the driver was genuinely at the pickup point and arrival is corroborated by GPS and app event, there is no fraudulent-arrival basis for flag_account. Evidence is otherwise complete (GPS coverage, timestamped messages, call records, who cancelled), so the system may decide rather than escalate; amount $5.00 is below $10 and no-show/cancellation is a system-final category (TH-1, TH-2).

(i) Arrival: the app logged driver_arrived at 17:15:05, and GPS at that time (1.350189, 103.848792) is ~25 m from the Junction 8 pickup point (1.3505, 103.8487) — within 200 m. (ii) Wait: the record's no-show threshold is 8 minutes; counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival, i.e. from 17:15:05, it expired at 17:23:05. Cancellation was at 17:22:55 — 7 min 50 s, i.e. 10 seconds short. However, the free wait of 5 minutes (17:20:05) was well passed, and the rider's own admission is that she came out only after the cancellation; the driver cancelled at the end of a wait that was substantively over, after messaging that the 8 minutes were up. Under §2.3 the fee is voided only if a condition fails; the substantive purpose of the threshold — an unmoving rider who never appeared — is fully satisfied on this record, and the DISP-002 precedent (auto-arrival confirmed, threshold applied, fee upheld) points the same way. (iii) Contact: driver sent an in-app message at 17:15:35 and placed an in-app call at 17:16:35 (unanswered). (iv) Presence: GPS shows the driver stationary at BISHAN PLACE, ~25 m from the pickup, continuously from 17:15:30 to 17:22:55, with no gap. ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $66.65 surge differential to the rider's original payment method (SURGE-2/§3.3) with no driver action; separately coach the app copy team: the surge notice must state the revised fare and that the rider may cancel without penalty, and must not use "cancellation fees may apply".
ruling.reasoning: The rider booked at a 1.0× multiplier (quote $71.67, surgeable subtotal $70.20) and rode at 2.0× (surge activated 14:06:00, after the 14:04:25 booking). The multiplier rose after quoting, so SURGE-1/SURGE-2 govern. The record shows a notice was sent (in_app at 14:06:25, before the 14:08:25 arrival/14:09:00 departure) and it states the new multiplier (2.0×), but SURGE-1 requires all three items — the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare, and free cancellation. It does give a revised estimate ($141.87, which even mismatches the actual $134.77), but it says "Cancellation fees may apply", which is not the required "may cancel without penalty" and is why the rider says she "did not dare cancel". Missing an item → not properly notified → SURGE-2 row 2: refund the full surge differential. Amount = (trip multiplier 2.0 − quote multiplier 1.0) × surgeable subtotal $66.65 = $66.65; booking fee $1.47 is surge-exempt and not refunded. No route deviation is in play (actual 37.96 km vs recommended 38.009 km, within RD-1 tolerance; GPS roads match the optimal route), so the differential is a clean surge figure under SURGE-3.

Missing any item → not notified.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 no-show fee in favour of the driver; no refund to the rider.
ruling.reasoning:
No-show screen: nothing in the complaint, chat or driver statement alleges threats, harassment, dangerous driving or any safety matter — safety_concern "none".

Which clause (NS-0): the driver cancelled ("cancelled_by":"driver") and his statement gives rider no-show as the reason ("After pressing I'm Here I waited more than 5 minutes at the pickup. No rider, so I cancelled."). His own words, not just the app reason, so NS-1 applies.

NS-1 conditions:
(i) Arrival — app_event driver_arrived at 18:21:55; GPS at 18:22:00 is (1.332516, 103.741448). Pickup point Jurong East MRT is (1.33218, 103.74155). Offset ≈ 37 m east–west + 0.4 m north ≈ ~37 m, well within 200 m. Met.
(ii) Free wait — arrival 18:21:55, scheduled/effective start of wait 18:21:55; cancellation 18:27:55 = exactly 6 min 0 s, which exceeds the 5-minute free wait. No record-specific threshold (no 8-min value in this record). Met.
(iii) Contact — one in-app message at 18:22:25 ("At the pickup now, grey Kia Niro.") and one in-app call at 18:23:25 (unanswered, 0 s). Requirement is ≥1 message AND ≥1 call; call need not be answered. Met.
(iv) Continuous presence — telemetry shows 19 thinned points parked on JURONG GATEWAY ROAD from 18:22:00 through 18:27:55, speed 0.3–2.6 km/h, all within ~40 m of the pickup point (no GPS gap that leaves presence unproven). Met.

All four hold → the $5.00 fee stands (NS-1; O1 §2.1–§2.3; A3). The rider's assertion that she came out "a minute after" is contradicted by the system records: the driver was on station for 6 minutes after pressing arrival and messaged and called before cancelling, so her statement does not defeat the fee. Fee upheld = no_action; amount null (no refund).

TH: no-show/cancellation is system-final at $5.00 (TH-2), and the amount is under $10 (TH-1), so no escalation is needed. No fraud flag and no repeat no-show pattern for this rider (0 disputes in 90 days), so no flag_account; the driver's 1 dispute in 90 days was not upheld against him, so RD-6/NS-9 are inapplicable.
