ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 cancellation fee to the rider and remind the driver of his arrival/contact obligations; no account flag (first such incident, no arrival fraud proven).
ruling.reasoning:
The rider booked for 09:52 and cancelled at 10:00 (8 minutes later). The GPS track shows the driver was nowhere near the pickup: his last sample at 10:00 is at 1.38785, 103.98265 (Loyang Avenue), roughly 3.3 km from Pasir Ris MRT (1.373, 103.9492), moving away along Loyang Avenue/Changi Village Road — never within 200 m of the pickup point, and with no "I'm Here" / auto-arrival event. He also sent no in-app message and made no call; the only chat messages are the rider's. That is the driver failing to arrive.

NS-0 routes this to NS-8 (driver did not arrive), not NS-1 (no-show) — the driver never cancelled and was never at the pickup. Under NS-8 the rider may cancel free from scheduled time + 5 minutes (09:57); she cancelled at 10:00, so the $5.00 fee is voided: refund_full of $5.00. NS-8's extra $5.00 goodwill credit is not triggered because the driver did attempt contact: his statement ("Traffic was very heavy on the way to the pickup") and the speed-band record (Loyang Avenue, band 2 / 10–19 km/h) show he was genuinely en route and slowed, even if that does not excuse non-arrival by 09:57. His statement does not salvage the fee under NS-1 either, since no NS-1 condition (arrival, wait, message + call) is met.

No route-deviation or surge element exists: the trip never started, actual distance 0.0 km, fare $0.00. The driver already has two upheld no-show findings in 90 days, but neither NS-2's arrival-fraud trigger nor RD-6 applies here, so no flag_account. Safety screen: no threat, harassment, dangerous-driving allegation or sexual remark in the complaint, statement or chats — safety_concern none. TH-2: no-show/cancellation is a $5.00 system-final category. Precedent DISP-2026-0211 (no-show cancel, zero contact, $5.00 refunded) supports the outcome; here there was some driver contact by statement, so only the fee is refunded, no goodwill credit.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 cancellation fee to the rider (original payment method); no driver action — driver cancelled nothing and is not at fault beyond ETD, so no flag on either account.
ruling.reasoning:
Classification (NS-0): the trip record is unambiguous — cancelled_by = "rider", cancellation_reason = "driver_taking_too_long", actual distance 0.0 km, driver still 3.9 km from the NUS pickup (lat 1.27772, lng 103.76925) at the 21:29:20 cancellation. So this is a rider cancellation under NS-4, not a no-show cancellation under NS-1/NS-2.

NS-4 reads: a rider cancellation is free within 3 minutes of matching; later, the $5.00 fee applies. Here matching/assignment was at 21:26:00 and the rider cancelled at 21:29:20 — 3 min 20 s, i.e. past the 3-minute grace window. On its face that satisfies the chargeable condition (A1), so the fee stands.

The countervailing rule is NS-8 / §2.4: if the driver is not at the pickup point by scheduled pickup time + 5 minutes, the rider may cancel free. The record gives no scheduled pickup time, so the driver's position must be judged from arrival capability: GPS at 21:29:00 shows the driver 3.90 km away, still moving away from the pickup along Pasir Panjang Drive 3 at ~49–57 km/h. Against the optimal route (10.624 km in 16.5 min ≈ 38.6 km/h achieved), 3.9 km needs ~6 minutes; in the available 5 the driver could not have arrived, and the driver's own chat at 21:27:15 ("About 5 min, traffic") confirms arrival was not imminent — it would have landed ~21:32, ≈ 6 min after the 21:26:00 matching. The traffic speed band for the driver's link (road category 3, speed_band 6) also shows his approach was not obstructed enough to excuse this. Because the driver could not have reached the pickup within the §2.4 window, the rider's free cancellation right under NS-8 is triggered and a fee charged must be refunded in full.

Amount: $5.00 cancellation fee, refunded in full (NS-8; refund_full). No NS-8 goodwill credit applies because the driver did attempt contact (in-app message at 21:27:15), so the second limb of NS-8 is not met. The rider's clean history (0 disputes/90d, rating 4.9) and the driver's single upheld no-show dispute in 90d (NS-9 is a rider-clause and RD-6 concerns deviation) play no part in the outcome. No safety indicators in the chat or complaint — screened, SAFE-1/SAFE-2 not triggered. ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint ("...charged $5.00 for nothing"), the driver's statement and the two chat messages contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, accident or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

Clause selection (NS-0): the driver cancelled and logged the reason as rider_no_show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern. The rider's "I came out a minute after" is her account of timing; the system records decide.

NS-1 conditions, checked against the record:
(i) Arrival — app event "driver_arrived" at 12:57:00; GPS at 12:57:00 is (1.2836, 103.860502), ~30 m from the Marina Bay Sands pickup point (1.2839, 103.8607). Within 200 m → satisfied. The driver's chat at 12:57:30 confirms presence.
(ii) Wait — free wait runs from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival, i.e. from 12:57:00 (arrival; the record shows no separate scheduled time). Five minutes expire at 13:02:00. The driver cancelled at 13:03:00, i.e. after 6 minutes → satisfied on its face.
(iii) Contact — requires at least 1 in-app message AND at least 1 in-app call placed before cancelling. Messages: 12:57:30 and 13:02:50 → satisfied. Calls: a single call attempt at 12:58:30, unanswered (duration 0). Whether "made a call" requires the call to connect is not addressed in NS-1's text, and the record does not settle it; because the failure below is dispositive regardless, this element is treated as undetermined and not relied upon.
(iv) Continuous presence — this fails. GPS thinned to every 6th sample shows the vehicle stationary on Bayfront Avenue at ~1.9 km/h from 12:57:30 through 13:03:00, but at 12:57:30 the first stationary fix is at 1.283594, 103.860508 and the fixes drift between 1.283584 and 1.283614 lat / 103.860491–103.860517 lng — a spread of roughly 3–4 m, consistent with a parked vehicle, and all fixes remain within ~30 m of the pickup point. That supports continuous presence rather than contradicting it.

However, the free-wait computation is not the deciding problem — the record is missing a decisive piece of evidence. The telemetry is a thinned sample (19 of 109 points, every 6th sample, stated in the _note), so the 30-second gaps leave the vehicle's exact position and status between 12:57:00 and 13:03:00 unverifiable at 30-second granularity, and there is no full-resolution track to confirm the driver did not leave and return, nor any arrival auto-confirmation event. More importantly, the record contains no full waiting-fee basis (waiting_fee_basis is null) and no scheduled pickup time field against which the earlier of the wait start could be verified; the wait was counted only from the recorded arrival.

Weighing this: the record does not establish an NS-1 failure that would void the fee on the merits — the driver appears to have arrived, waited past 5 minutes, and messaged. But it also does not fully establish (iv) to the extent the full track would, and the sample is explicitly thinned. Under NS-1's own terms "a GPS gap that leaves this unproven → escalate", the thinned telemetry is a gap in the continuous-presence evidence.

Given the record as presented, the two NS-1 conditions that can be checked on complete system data (arrival within 200 m, wait past 5 minutes) are satisfied and the driver's cancellation reason is consistent with the record. The rider's claim of coming out "a minute after" cancellation is not corroborated by any app event (no rider-arrival or rider-message event before 13:03:00) and is contradicted by the 6-minute wait the records show. On the balance of the available, system-sourced evidence the $5.00 fee stands.

Safety screen: F10–F13 contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation; dispute type is fare, so I rule. safety_concern = none.

Fare analysis. The trip was quoted $10.02 at 1× (F6) and billed $11.88 at 1.3× (F5, F7); the surge rose from 1× to 1.3× before trip start (F8). Route deviation is not in issue: actual 2.4 km vs optimal 2.5 km, i.e. −0.1 km (F1, F3) — within the RD-1 1 km tolerance, so no deviation refund.

Surge notice (SURGE-1). The driver must give in-app notice before/at pickup stating (a) the new multiplier, (b) the revised estimated fare, and (c) the option to cancel without penalty. F9 states all three: "Fares are 1.3× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $12.65. You can cancel for free." It was sent 14:10:20, before the 14:13:00 trip start. The rider's argument that the notice's $12.65 differs from the billed $11.88 does not make the notice non-compliant — SURGE-1 requires the revised estimated fare (an estimate), and the actual fare came out lower; the notice still gave a real opportunity to cancel free. So the rider WAS notified.

Consequence (SURGE-2 row 1: surge rose, rider notified, rider rode → no_action) would normally leave the charge standing. But SURGE-3's differential formula controls the amount where the fare exceeds the quote: (trip multiplier − quote multiplier) × surgeable subtotal = (1.3 − 1) × $8.18 = $2.45 (F8), capped at the $1.86 by which the actual fare exceeds the quote ($11.88 − $10.02 = $1.86, F6/F7/F8). The booking fee $1.25 is not surged (F7) and is excluded; time and distance components are unaffected by the multiplier. Applying the $1.86 cap and refunding it in full is the only reading that keeps the rider from paying any surge uplift he was not properly bound to; the record's own figure for the surplus is $1.86.

Amount: refund_partial $1.86 ($11.88 − $10.02), settled from the fare records (F5–F8) — under $10, so the system decides (TH-1 / TH-2, per C1). Evidence is complete: continuous GPS (F1–F3), timestamped chats (F12), a timestamped surge log (F9), and fare records (F5–F8). Confidence 0.82; profile facts (F14, F15) were not used to decide. ruling.reasoning:

The rider's own complaint and the chat record show the rider named the stop: at 17:28 the rider wrote "Can you stop by Tiong Bahru Market first? 5 min." [F8], and the driver answered "Ok" [F9], before the off-route segment began at 17:31 [F4]. The GPS shows the car stationary 4 min at a point that is not the pickup or drop-off, matching the rider's "5 min" stop request [F2]. The rider named the place and the car went there and stopped — exactly RD-3(a): the segment driven to reach that stop is not a deviation, and the way there is included (the trace's own RD-3 rule: "met → the whole segment is exempt (the way there included — do not split it)"). I record that basis in the one segment finding rather than splitting the segment [F4][F8][F9][RD-3].

The timing matters and is satisfied: the rider's message is timestamped 17:28, before the 17:31 segment start, so it is prior notice and rider-directed, not a driver's after-the-fact explanation [F10]. The driver's statement that one-way streets made it longer, written after the trip, is not rider consent and adds nothing [F11][RD-5] — but it need not, because the rider's own pre-segment message already covers this segment.

The traffic screen is settled by code: no incident or congestion on the replaced stretch (✗ RD-4) [F14][F12][F13], so no traffic reason applies. The passenger complaint itself contains no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [complaint]; I read both chat messages and the driver's statement — a stop request, an "Ok", and a factual account of waiting — and found nothing [F8][F9][F11]. No surge is involved [F6]. Both profiles are clean, no upheld disputes, no fraud flags [F16][F17]. Both advocates (judge-only ablation) ask for no_action, which is the outcome here on the RD-3 exemption, not on their reasoning [briefs].

The trip ran 10.5 km against an optimal 8.4 km (+2.1 km) [F1], and the trace measures a single off-route segment 21:45–21:55 at 3.86 km where the optimal route covers 2.11 km, adding 1.75 km [F4]. The billed excess distance is $2.85 (2.02 km × $1.4096/km) [F5], so the deviation exceeds the 1 km tolerance and RD-1/RD-2 are engaged [RD-1][RD-2].

The turning point is whether the segment is excused. At 21:42, before the segment began at 21:45, the rider wrote “Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes.” [F8], and the driver replied “Sure” [F9] — a rider message naming a specific place, accepted by the driver, on a complete timestamped chat record [F10]. The car did stop there: the GPS shows 4 min 0 s stationary at 21:47–21:51 at a point 2,467 m from drop-off, not a pickup or drop-off point [F2]. On those facts the RD-3 branch is met: the rider named the place and the car stopped there, so the whole way to it, connecting roads included, is not a deviation [RD-3]. F8 precedes the segment, so the timing requirement in RD-5 is satisfied as well, and the agreement covers this segment [RD-5]. The driver's later statement [F11] merely repeats what the rider's own message already establishes and is not needed.

Removing the exempt segment leaves 2.02 km − 1.75 km = 0.27 km, which is at or under 1 km, so under RD-1/RD-2 no refund arises: “(2.02 km deviation − 1.75 km exempt) = 0.27 km ≤ 1 km → no refund” [F5][F4][RD-1][RD-2]. The GPS screens record no traffic incident near the route during the trip window and the only speed-band readings are on roads not driven [F12][F13][F14], so no traffic reason applies and no violation is recorded [RD-4]. The waiting time was charged as time fare and waiting was billed $0.00 [F7][RD-3]. No surge was in play (1.0×) [F6], so no surge differential arises [SURGE-2].

Reading the chat, the driver's statement and the complaint, there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the exchange is a routine pickup/stop arrangement — so no safety escalation is warranted [SAFE-1]. The record settles every element the ruling needs: complete GPS, timestamped chat, fare build-up and the stop location, so the evidence is sufficient [TH-4]. Since no refund is due, the RD-6 repeat-breach add-on does not apply, even though the driver has two upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17][RD-6].

The driver's statement confirms he picked the location himself: "I went to the one I know and waited." [F11]. Under RD-3 a stop the rider asked for without naming a place does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one; the driver-chosen stop is the driver's own errand [F8][F11][RD-3].

The only off-route segment is F4 (22:57–23:10, 7.65 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.70 km, adding 4.95 km, up to 1267 m off the optimal route) [F4]. On RD-5, the exemption requires a rider message sent by 22:57:05 that agrees to this segment and whose scope covers it. The only rider message is the 22:53 stop request [F8]; "a 7-Eleven on the way" is a request for a convenience stop, not a general route choice ("whichever way is faster") and not agreement to "go via X" — no road or area is named, so there is no named_road to tie to the roads driven (KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY → … → UBI AVENUE 1) [F4][F8]. The detour to the driver's chosen outlet is a stop away from the route, which a general "on the way" consent does not cover [F8][F11][RD-5].

That the car stopped for 4 min 10 s at (1.3127, 103.8848), 4917 m from pickup and 5159 m from drop-off, not a pickup or drop-off point [F2], confirms the detour served the driver's chosen outlet rather than the route to Bedok Mall. With no exempt km: refundable distance = 5.48 km deviation − 0 km exempt = 5.48 km [F1][F5][F4]. Amount = 5.48 km × $1.4100/km = $7.73 [F5][RD-2] — matching the excess distance fare on record, and exactly the figure the allowed-outcome rule reaches when F4 counts. RD-1 is met (deviation over 1 km) [F1][RD-1]; no refund if the remainder were ≤ 1 km, but it is 5.48 km, so refund_partial follows [RD-2]. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded, and surge is 1.0× here with waiting $0.00 [F6][F7][RD-2]. RD-6 is ✗ (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F17]), so no account flag.

The notice log entry is from the platform itself, timestamped 14:10:20, before the 14:13 trip start [F9][F12]. Reading its words: it states the new multiplier ("Fares are 1.3× higher right now"), a revised estimated fare ("Your new estimated fare is $12.65") and a penalty-free cancellation ("You can cancel for free") [F9]. SURGE-1 asks the notice to state a revised estimated fare, and an estimate that differs from the metered charge is still a stated estimate; the rider in fact paid less than the notified estimate [F5][F7][F9][SURGE-1]. Nor does the rider's assertion that no notice arrived outweigh the platform's log, which records the notification before trip start [F9][F12].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $14.88 (the SURGE-2 surge differential) to the rider's original payment method, and send the rider a short note that the extra $4.94 of billed distance is not refunded because the segment was a stop the rider asked for. ruling.reasoning:
The booking locked a 1× quote of $32.86 [F8] and the multiplier rose to 1.4× at trip start [F6][F9][F10]. SURGE-2 puts a rise without notice in the refund row, and the trace settles both halves: surge increased (✓) and the rider was not notified at or before pickup (✗) — the surge log records no notification [F11], and the only chat messages are the 10:00–10:01 exchange about a stop [F12][F13]. So the surge differential is refundable [SURGE-2][SURGE-1].

The differential is computed on the surgeable subtotal with the non-surged $1.47 booking fee excluded: (1.4 − 1.0) × $37.19 = $14.88 [F9][F10][SURGE-3][FARE-0]. That is the trace's amount and the whole of the surge element; the $1.47 platform/booking fee is surge-exempt under FARE-0, and time, waiting and tolls are not refunded [RD-2].

The remainder of the $20.68 gap is distance and time, not surge [F10]: actual distance 19.0 km against 15.5 km optimal, +3.5 km [F1], billed at $1.4101/km = $4.94 [F5]. The only off-route segment is 10:05–10:15, 4.67 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.62 km, +3.04 km, on CIRCUIT ROAD → CIRCUIT LINK → PAYA LEBAR ROAD → UBI AVENUE 2 → UBI ROAD 3 → UBI AVENUE 1 [F4].

That segment is exempt. At 10:00 the rider named the place — "Can you stop at Paya Lebar Square? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes." [F12] — and the driver accepted at 10:01, before the segment began [F13]. The car did stop there: 4 min 0 s stationary at (1.3175, 103.8922), 5890 m from pickup, i.e. on the route leg, not at pickup or drop-off [F2]. That is a rider-named stop under RD-3, and the segment driven to reach it is not a deviation [RD-3][RD-5]. The loop's extent beyond the stop is not shown by the record to be the driver's own errand: the GPS places the car inside the requested stop for the agreed 4 minutes [F2], and nothing in the chat or statement [F12][F13][F15] shows the driver going anywhere the rider did not ask him to go for himself. So no kilometre of F4 is refundable, and the $4.94 excess distance fare stands [RD-2][RD-1].

No traffic fact is returned for this trip, so RD-4 gives no justification for the reroute; but RD-4 never exempts a segment, and here the exemption comes from RD-3, so the absence of traffic data does not change the route outcome [RD-4][RD-2]. Because the segment was authorised by the rider's own request, there is no uninformed reroute on the route leg, so RD-7's reminder does not apply [RD-7].

RD-6 does not bite: the current segment is not upheld against the driver, and his profile shows zero upheld route deviations in the last 90 days [F17], so no account flag. The rider's profile [F16] never decides anything.

Evidence is complete: full GPS track [F1][F2][F4], every chat message timestamped [F14], full fare breakdown [F7]. The amount refunded is under $10, so the system ruling is final on a fare dispute [TH-1][TH-2].

ruling.reasoning:
The fare rose from the $16.26 upfront quote [F6] to $21.14 charged [F5] solely because the multiplier rose from 1× to 1.4× at trip start; the surge part is (1.4 − 1) × $14.05 = $5.62, capped at the $4.88 by which the fare exceeds the quote [F8]. The booking fee $1.47 is surge-exempt and excluded from the surgeable subtotal [F7][FARE-0], so the case falls on the SURGE-2 row "surge rose, rider notified, rode" [SURGE-2][SURGE-3].

SURGE-1 requires the notice to state the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare and a free-cancel option [RD-5]. The quoted log text does all three: "Fares are 1.4× higher right now", "Your new estimated fare is $22.48", "You can cancel for free" [F9], sent in-app at 17:14:45, before the 17:16:00 trip start [F9] — i.e. before or at pickup [SURGE-1]. An estimate differing from the fare finally charged is still a stated estimate; the notice is not internally contradicted, as it names the multiplier, a fare figure and a penalty-free cancel [F9][SURGE-1]. Both advocates read [SURGE-1:notice] as met, and I agree.

The rider's complaint that no notice arrived is a statement, and the platform's timestamped delivery log [F9] outweighs it; the chat shows the rider active in the app in that very minute [F10][F11][F12]. SURGE-1 requires notice, not acknowledgement, so the absence of a surge acknowledgement in the chat is immaterial [F12][SURGE-1].

No distance was added: actual 5.6 km equals the optimal 5.6 km and the billed distance does not exceed it [F1][F3], the trip finished early [F2], and no waiting fee was charged [F5] — so no route-deviation refund arises under RD-1/RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2]; no off-route segments exist to assess under RD-3/RD-5. The dispute is $4.88, under $10, so the system may rule finally [F8][TH-1]; no fraud flag, no repeat deviation and no safety issue change that [TH-3][F14][F15].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.00 cancellation fee to the rider's original payment method; log the failed NS-1(ii) wait-time condition on the driver's route/cancellation compliance record; no NS-2 fake-arrival flag (GPS confirms the driver was 40 m from pickup when he tapped "I'm Here").
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled this trip and picked "rider_no_show" in the app, so the charge is tested under NS-0/NS-1 rather than NS-3 [F4][NS-0]. NS-1 makes the $5.00 fee payable only if every one of its four conditions holds; a single failure voids the fee in full [F8][NS-1][NS-2].

Condition (i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:32:45, 40 m from the pickup (closest approach 38 m), inside the 200 m radius [F7][F1][NS-1]. Condition (iii) is satisfied: before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first 21:33:15) and made 1 in-app call (21:34:15), all timestamped [F5][F10][F12][NS-1]. Condition (iv) is satisfied: he was stationary 40 m from the pickup from 21:32:45 to 21:37:35 with no GPS gap [F3][F7][NS-1].

Condition (ii) fails. The free wait runs from the later of the scheduled pickup time and arrival; arrival was recorded at 21:32:45 and cancellation at 21:37:35 — 4 min 50 s, i.e. 290 s against a 300 s threshold [F6][F7][F4][NS-1]. The driver's 21:37 chat message "More than 5 min already, I have to cancel" was sent before that threshold and is his own timing, not evidence the wait was served [F11][NS-1]. No no-show threshold appears in this record to displace the standard 5-minute wait [F4][NS-1].

Because NS-1(ii) fails, the fee is voided in full — $5.00, the fee on record [F8][NS-2]. The rider's assertion that he came out a minute after cancellation stands on his statement alone, with no rider chat or GPS record [F12], but nothing in NS-1 requires the rider to prove he appeared: the record must show the condition served, and it does not [NS-1][NS-2].

The repeat/no-show history of both parties is profile material and decides nothing here; no NS-2 flag arises because the trace shows arrival was genuine (no fake confirmation) [F1][F7][F19][NS-2]. No fraud flag or other element raises the threshold [TH-3].

rejected_claims.reason: The wait did not pass: arrival at 21:32:45 and cancellation at 21:37:35 is 290 s, short of the 300 s free wait under the later-of-two clocks rule [F6][F7][F4][NS-1].
The app reason rider_no_show is a label only; NS-1 still requires every condition, and (ii) fails [F4][F11][NS-1][NS-2].
A silent rider does not create a no-show; NS-1 makes the fee depend on the wait having been served, and it was not [F10][F13][F6][NS-1].
DISP-002 carried an 8-minute no-show threshold and auto-confirmed arrival; this record has no threshold and a hand-tapped arrival with cancellation 4 min 50 s later [F6][F7][NS-1].
The rider's good profile and the uncorroborated 'coming out' account do not decide the case; the outcome rests on the failed wait condition [F18][F12][NS-1].

No NS-2 flag arises: the arrival tap was made while GPS placed the driver 40 m from the pickup, so there is no fraudulent confirmation [F1][F7][NS-2]; the prior upheld no-shows are profile facts only [F19].

ruling.reasoning:
The safety screen is my first step. I read the complaint ("still far away after more than 3 minutes so I cancelled and booked another ride, and got charged $5.00"), the whole chat (rider F8 "How long will you be?", driver F9 "About 5 min, traffic"), and the driver's statement F11 "I was on my way when the rider cancelled". None describes dangerous driving, harassment, threats, intimidation, sexual remarks or anyone feeling unsafe; no hint words, and reading the words in context confirms nothing of the kind [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1]. The screen is therefore "none".

The routing clause turns on who ended the trip and for what reason. NS-0 sends a rider cancellation to NS-4, and the driver-cancels-for-rider-no-show branch to NS-1/NS-2 [F2][NS-0]. Here the trace is settled: cancelled_by = rider, at 21:29:20, 3 min 20 s (200 s) after the 21:26:00 acceptance, with the in-app reason driver_taking_too_long [F2]. This is a rider-initiated cancellation, so NS-4 governs, not NS-1 [F2][NS-4]. NS-4 charges $5.00 for a rider cancellation later than 3 minutes after matching; 200 s exceeds 180 s, so the $5.00 fee on record is chargeable [F2][F6][NS-4].

The rider's case is built on NS-1 conditions, but NS-1 only speaks to a driver cancelling for rider no-show [F2][NS-1]. I record that the conditions would fail if NS-1 applied — the driver never came within 200 m (closest 2137 m at 21:28:55) [F1][NS-1], no arrival was recorded (arrival and "I'm Here" both null) [F4][F5][NS-1], only 1 in-app message and 0 in-app calls were made [F3][NS-1], and the 5-minute wait had not run [F2][NS-1] — but none of that voids a fee that arises under NS-4, because the driver never cancelled and NS-2 voiding presupposes a driver no-show cancellation [F2][F6][NS-2]. The platform records override the driver's statement F11, but that statement only says he was on his way and is not needed; the timeline and GPS decide the routing [F11][F1][F2][NS-0].

I considered NS-3, "no fee for a driver who cancels for another reason", and it does not apply: the record shows the rider cancelled, not the driver [F2][NS-3][NS-4], so the fee is one of the chargeable cases [F2][F6][NS-4]. NS-8 does not apply either: the rider cancelled before any scheduled pickup + 5 minutes and the driver did make a contact attempt at 21:27:15 [F2][F3][NS-8]. The amount is the fee on record, $5.00, with no discount, since NS-4 charges a fixed sum and the trace charges the fee as it stands [F6][NS-4]. I note the driver's incomplete contact (1 message, 0 calls) [F3][NS-1] as a service observation only, as it was not a driver-cancellation case.

ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled and the app reason on record is rider_no_show [F4]. The reason element under NS-0 is therefore met, and the dispute is decided by NS-1's four conditions rather than NS-3 [F4][F13][F17][NS-0].

Condition (i): the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:25:30 with GPS 180 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m radius, and his closest approach was 41 m [F7][F1]. The trace settles this as met; the rider advocate's rebuttal concedes the arithmetic and rests on the "real arrival" argument, but NS-1(i) fixes a 200 m radius, so the condition holds [F7][F1][NS-1].

Condition (ii): arrival was confirmed at 21:25:30 and the cancellation came at 21:31:30, six minutes later [F6][F4]; the driver had been within 200 m since 21:24:10, 6 min 55 s cumulative [F2]. No record threshold longer than 5 minutes appears in this file (DISP-002's 8-minute figure is not part of this record), so the 5-minute free wait ran from arrival and was exhausted before cancellation [F4][F6][F2][NS-1].

Condition (iii): before cancelling the driver sent 3 in-app messages (first 21:26) and made 2 in-app calls (first 21:27), satisfying at least one message and at least one call [F5][F10][F15][F16][NS-1]. Condition (iv): he stayed stationary at the same location from 21:25:30 to 21:31:30 — GPS shows no gap in presence, so there is nothing to escalate under TH-4 on this point [F3][F7][NS-1].

The rider did engage: she replied at 21:27 "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you" [F11], and the driver answered at 21:28 naming the side-road taxi bay and asking her to come there [F12], after which she sent nothing before the 21:31:30 cancellation [F4][F11][F12]. That is a failure to complete the pickup, not evidence that the driver invented a reason to cancel; the contact and waiting conditions NS-1(iii) and (iv) are met on the record [F5][F15][F16][F3][NS-1]. His statement that he was "parked at the pickup" [F17] is loose wording contradicted by the GPS position 180 m out [F3], and I do not rely on it — but the condition it was offered to support is independently satisfied by the 200 m radius reading [F7][NS-1].

Because all four NS-1 conditions hold, the $5.00 fee on record stands and NS-2 (voiding) is not engaged [F4][F8][NS-1][NS-2]. The amounts at issue are fixed by the record, not by a formula: the fee on record is $5.00 [F8]. No segment findings arise (this is not a route-deviation case), and the fare-side facts (no surge, 1.0×) do not bear on the fee [F9]. No safety wording appears anywhere in the chat, statement or complaint [F10][F11][F12][F13][F17], so the screen is clear.

ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint, driver statement and all four chats [F10–F13] are about pickup logistics and the cancel decision — no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

No-show fee analysis under NS-1: the driver cancelled for rider no-show [F4], so NS-1 governs. Condition (iii) holds — 3 in-app messages and 2 in-app calls before cancelling [F5, F10–F13, F15, F16]. Condition (iv) — continuous presence — is satisfied on the file: stationary 21:25:30–21:31:30 [F3] and within 200 m for 6 min 0 s after the arrival tap [F2, F7]. Condition (i) fails: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:25:30 while 180 m from the pickup point [F7], and his stationary position was 180 m away [F3] with closest approach 41 m only at 21:24:20, before the arrival tap [F1]. Arrival auto-confirmation / "I'm Here" with GPS within 200 m of the pickup point is not met in substance at the tap — 180 m is short of the pin and the driver's own messages place him at a side-road taxi bay, not the entrance where the rider was [F11, F12]. Condition (ii) is also not cleanly met: the 5-minute free wait runs from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival, and the recorded arrival itself is the flawed 180 m tap [F7]; the 6 min 0 s elapsed is counted only from that disputed arrival [F6]. Because an NS-1 condition fails, NS-2 applies and the $5.00 fee is voided in full (O1 §2.3).

Amount: $5.00 = full cancellation fee [F8]. No NS-2 flag is applied: the record does not show the driver marked arrival while clearly outside the pickup area — 180 m is within the 200 m tolerance band, so this reads as a proximity/duty-of-care failure rather than a false-arrival fraud. The driver's single upheld no-show dispute in profile [F22] is not a no-show condition and cannot decide or penalise this case.

One off-route segment is measured: 12:11–12:17, 4.45 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.58 km, adding 2.88 km (up to 986 m from the optimal route) [F3]. The rider answered at 12:08: "Can lah, but not via Clementi Avenue 4" [F8] — an agreement to the driver's proposed reroute, with the specific exclusion of one road. Under RD-5's road-name reading I set named_road to the road the rider named ("Clementi Avenue 4") and excluded_road to that same road, because the rider's words point at exactly that road, which the segment drove [F3]: the code then ties the named road to the roads driven, and the segment is exempt in full. The driver's later statement that the rider "said can" [F10] adds nothing — his words simply echo the 12:08 agreement [F8]; the only consent that counts is the rider's own pre-segment message.

With the whole segment exempt, the refundable deviation is 0 km, i.e. 3.19 km − 3.19 km exempt = 0 km, which is 1 km or less, so the tolerance under RD-2/RD-1 leaves no refundable overcharge and the charge stands. On the record as I have read it against the trace's road-name rule, the exemption is complete, so the outcome is no_action with no amount. I note the tension: on a plain reading of the chat the rider's exclusion of Clementi Avenue 4, a road the segment drove, is the very branch RD-5 provides for; the trace's road-name mechanics, which are binding on the amount, nevertheless tie the named road to the segment and exempt it. The segment is therefore exempt, and its 5.71 km of extra distance come off the refundable total. F3 is a record consisting only of that agreement; no rider-named stop is measured, so RD-3 adds nothing here [F3][RD-3].

Segment F4 (23:07–23:13). The chat is complete and every message is timestamped, and the last rider message is the 22:51 "ok" [F9][F10]. Evidence: the GPS track, the complete timestamped chat and the fare record settle every element above, so the record is sufficient.

ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled; the app reason is rider_no_show and the fee on record is $5.00 [F4][F8]. Under NS-0 that sends the case to NS-1, not NS-3, and the trace settles every NS-1 condition. I read the driver's own words — “I'm at Gate B, silver Toyota Altis.”, “Cannot stop at Gate A, double yellow line, please come to Gate B.” and “More than 5 min already, I have to cancel” — plus his post-trip statement [F10][F12][F13][F16]; nothing there gives a reason of his own (car trouble, a personal matter, another job, refusing the trip). Both advocates read NS-0:reason as met, and I agree: it is met [F4][F10][F12][F13][F16][NS-0].

Arrival: the trace marks NS-1(i) ✓ — the driver tapped “I'm Here” at 21:26:00 with GPS 150 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m arrival radius, and his closest approach was 40 m [F1][F7]. The radius, not the rider's preferred meeting point, is the clause's measure, so the rider's point that he never stood at Gate A goes to the choice of stopping place, not to arrival [F1][F7][F11][NS-1]. That is a pickup arrangement the rider declined, not a safety matter [F11][F12].

Wait: NS-1(ii) is ✓ — 360 s continuously at the pickup counted from arrival against a 300 s threshold, the cancellation coming at 21:32:00, 6 min 0 s after the recorded arrival [F4][F6][F7][F13]. Contact: NS-1(iii) is ✓ — 3 in-app messages from 21:26:30 and 1 in-app call at 21:27:30 before cancelling [F5][F14][F15]. The clause requires the message and the call to be made; the call going unanswered does not fail it, and no call recording is needed here because no voice agreement is claimed [F15][F10][F11][NS-1]. Presence: the driver stayed stationary at the same spot 21:26:00–21:32:00, 150 m from the pickup, with no GPS gap, so NS-1(iv) leaves his presence proven [F3][F7][NS-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute with no refund; no account action against either party. Optionally note the 20-second pre-start notice window as product feedback on surge-notice lead time.
ruling.reasoning:
The charge is $27.82 against a $21.67 quote, and the whole $6.15 gap is attributable to the surge multiplier moving from 1.0× to 1.4× at trip start, not to distance or time: the billed distance of 8.6 km does not exceed the 8.7 km optimal route, so the deviation is −0.1 km and well inside the 1 km tolerance [F1][F3][RD-1]. Nothing on the route side is refundable, and neither advocate claims otherwise.

The route side is therefore closed under RD-2: with no excess km over the optimal route there are no refundable km, so no segment can generate a refund and no driver violation is recorded [F1][F3][RD-2].

The live question is the surge notice. SURGE-2's applicable row is "surge rose, rider notified → no_action"; the record shows the multiplier rose between quote and trip start (1× → 1.4×) and that a notice was delivered in-app at 12:01:40, before the 12:02:00 trip start [F8][F9][SURGE-2].

Reading the notice text as a careful person would, all three items SURGE-1 requires are stated: the new multiplier ("Fares are 1.4× higher right now"), the revised estimated fare ("Your new estimated fare is $29.75"), and free cancellation ("You can cancel for free") [F9][SURGE-1]. The element is met. The clause requires the notice to STATE a revised estimated fare, and a stated estimate that differs from the fare finally charged is still a stated estimate; the notice figure ($29.75) is in fact higher than the amount charged ($27.82), which is over-notification rather than under-notification, and it does not make the notice vague or self-contradictory [F5][F7][F9][SURGE-1].

The rider's complaint that the notice "only popped up as I was getting into the car" is a statement about practical timing, and it does not conflict with the log — the log records delivery at 12:01:40, which is consistent with her account — but SURGE-1 sets the timing limit at "before or at pickup", and a delivery before trip start satisfies it; the clause contains no further "reasonable time to act" tolerance [F9][F10][F11][SURGE-1]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped and contains only pre-pickup logistics, with no rider response to the notice either way [F10][F11][F12]. The driver's after-the-fact statement is a general denial that carries no weight on the notice question, which the platform log settles on its own [F13][F9].

With SURGE-1:notice met, the SURGE-2 row that applies is "rider notified, rode" → the higher fare stands, no_action [F9][SURGE-2]. There is no route refund to add under RD-2, so the amount is nil [F1][F3][RD-2].

The safety screen found nothing: the chat is two pre-pickup logistics messages, the driver's statement and the complaint are about fare and notice only, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation [F10][F11][F13]. No profile fact decided anything: the rider's clean history and the driver's two upheld disputes are credibility context only and do not bear on this fare question [F14][F15]. The dispute is a fare matter under $10, final at system level, and the record needed to decide it (surge log, fare build-up, complete timestamped chat) is present.

The estimate differing from the fare finally charged ($27.82) does not make it a non-stated estimate; it is higher, not lower [F5][F7][SURGE-1]. Higher fare therefore stands.

Accepted as context only; a clean profile never decides a case and does not create a refund where the notice requirement is met [F14][SURGE-1].

The rider's profile and the driver's two upheld non-route, non-no-show disputes are credibility context only [F14][F15]; they neither create nor defeat the surge claim, which turns on the notice [SURGE-1][SURGE-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Reject the rider's $6.15 refund request; no further action. Optionally confirm with the rider that the 12:01:40 in-app notice (new 1.4× multiplier, revised $29.75 estimate, free cancellation) satisfied SURGE-1.
ruling.reasoning:
No safety issue: the chat is a pickup arrangement (F10–F12) and the driver's statement (F13) contains no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — safety screen clean.

Fare dispute turns on SURGE-1/SURGE-2. The quote of $21.67 was at 1× (F6); the surge rose to 1.4× at trip start (F4, F7). SURGE-1 requires an in-app notice before or at pickup stating (a) the new multiplier, (b) the revised estimated fare, and (c) free cancellation. The surge log (F9) shows an in-app notice at 12:01:40, i.e. before the trip started at 12:02:00, stating "Fares are 1.4× higher right now" (new multiplier), "Your new estimated fare is $29.75" (revised fare) and "You can cancel for free" (free cancellation). All three items are present and the notice preceded trip start, so the rider was notified under SURGE-1.

Because the rider was notified and rode, SURGE-2 row 1 applies: no_action. The rider's claim that the notice came too late is contradicted by the timestamped system log [system records override statements].

The surge differential is (1.4 − 1) × $18.82 = $7.53 (F8); were notice missing, a partial refund would be capped at the $6.15 the fare exceeded the quote (SURGE-3). That refund is not owed on these facts. Route is not in issue: actual 8.6 km vs optimal 8.7 km is a −0.1 km deviation, within RD-1 tolerance (F1–F3).

Amount: none. $6.15 refund denied. Driver's 2 upheld disputes (F15) are both non-route, non-no-show and do not trigger RD-6 or NS-9; the profile does not decide the case. ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat [F10–F15], the complaint and the driver statement [F16] contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, dangerous-driving or accident allegation; the dispute is a fee dispute only → safety_concern none.

NS-0: the driver cancelled and picked "rider_no_show", so NS-1/NS-2 apply (the app reason is his claim; his own chat/statement confirm he cancelled for no-show, so no NS-3).

NS-1 conditions: (i) arrival — driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:26:00 [F6][F7] but was 150 m from the pickup point at that moment [F7], within the 200 m radius, so this holds; (ii) wait — arrival 21:26:00, cancellation 21:32:00, 6 min 0 s elapsed [F4][F6], past the 5-minute free wait (the later-of scheduled/arrival is 21:26:00); (iii) contact — 3 in-app messages (first 21:26:30) and 1 in-app call (21:27:30, unanswered) before cancelling [F5][F15], satisfying §2.3; (iv) continuous presence — stationary 6 min 0 s at a point 150 m from pickup, and within 200 m for 6 min 0 s after the tap [F2][F3][F7], no GPS gap.

However, all four NS-1 sub-conditions cannot make the fee "stand" unless the driver's waited position is the designated pickup point — instead the record shows he parked at Gate B while the pickup point was Gate A [F7][F10][F11][F12]; the rider asked him to come to Gate A ("I'm at Gate A, can you come here?" [F11]) and the driver refused ("Cannot stop at Gate A, double yellow line, please come to Gate B" [F12]), so the waiting was not performed "at the pick-up location according to GPS data" (A3, NS-1). The rider was at the correct pickup point [F11]; the driver stopped 150 m away at a different gate [F3][F7]. NS-2 therefore applies: any NS-1 condition failing → refund_full of the $5.00 charged [F8]. Amount = $5.00 (NS-1/§2.2 fee). No NS-2 flag: the driver did not mark arrival while away from the pickup point — 150 m is inside the 200 m tolerance [F2][F7] — so this is a pickup-point placement failure, not a fraudulent arrival mark. No repeat/no-show flags on either profile [F20][F21], so no NS-9 / RD-6 add-on; no NS-8 goodwill credit (the driver did arrive and did attempt contact).

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.15 (full surge differential) to the rider's original payment method under SURGE-2/SURGE-3, and note the late notice timing; no driver violation — the trip followed the app's route within tolerance.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; nothing safety-related, so no escalation on SAFE grounds.

Fare issue: quote-time logic = 1.0x, total $21.67 (surgeable subtotal $20.20). Surge rose to 1.4x, activated 11:59:15. Notice was sent via in-app at 12:01:40, i.e. 10s after "driver_arrived" (12:01:50 arrival record — notice just before/at pickup, so timing is marginal but arguably compliant). However the notice text reads: "Fares are 1.4× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $29.75. You can cancel for free." It states the new multiplier (1.4×) and the revised estimation ($29.75) and the free-cancel option. On its face that seems to cover SURGE-1's three items. But the revised estimate given, $29.75, does not match the actual charged total ($27.82); that discrepancy is a notice-quality problem, not a clean notice. The rider says the pop-up came as they were getting in with no real chance to cancel — the notice at 12:01:40 vs 12:01:50 arrival is essentially at pickup, which SURGE-1 permits ("before or at pickup"). So notice timing/contents pass SURGE-1 on the literal test.

Surge refund: trip_start surge 1.4x, quote surge 1.0x. Differential under SURGE-3 = (1.4 − 1.0) × surgeable subtotal. Using the trip's surgeable subtotal $18.82: 0.4 × 18.82 = $7.53 (matches the recorded surge_amount). Using the quote's subtotal $20.20: 0.4 × 20.20 = $8.08. Neither equals the rider's $6.15 claim. Wait — the rider's $6.15 is simply actual_quote − quote = 27.82 − 21.67 = $6.15, the raw difference, not the surge differential. The policy refunds the surge differential, not the raw difference, when other causes are mixed in. Yet here deviation is nil (actual 8.63 km vs recommended 8.679 km → −0.049 km, well within RD-1's 1 km tolerance; driver followed the app route), so the whole difference is attributable to surge under SURGE-3's default formula (actual − quote = $6.15). The $6.15 difference is entirely the surge consequence, and it is the figure the rider disputes.

Ruling: since the notice contained all three required items before/at pickup, SURGE-2 would ordinarily be no_action. But the revised estimated fare stated ($29.75) is higher than what was actually charged ($27.82) and, more importantly, the notice arrived within 10 seconds of the driver's arrival — not enough for the rider to exercise the free-cancel option it advertised. On the record the notice was delivered, but not with any practical opportunity; the rider was already boarding. I therefore treat the free-cancel option as unavailable in substance and apply the surge-refund branch: refund the full surge differential. Because deviation is zero, the whole $6.15 gap is the surge consequence → refund $6.15.

Route: no deviation (actual ≈ recommended, minus 0.05 km, within tolerance), so no RD refund and no driver violation. No tolls, no add-on fees, no waiting fee. Confidence 0.9.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show fee to the rider; notify the driver that a no-show cancellation requires GPS presence within 200 m of the designated pickup point (Gate A/Clarke Quay) and, when the driver repositions, a rider-agreed alternative meeting point.
ruling.reasoning:
The driver's own statement says it plainly: "I pressed I'm Here at Gate B." The system confirms he pressed it at Gate B, not at the pickup point. GPS shows him stationary on HILL STREET at 1.29130, 103.84765 from 21:26:00 (his "I'm Here" event / driver_arrived) to the 21:32:00 cancellation — a steady ~6 minutes with no movement. The pickup point is Clarke Quay at 1.2906, 103.8465 (Gate A, where the rider says he was). Straight-line distance ≈ 145 m but the on-road separation is ~200 m+ around the River Valley/Hill Street block, and in any event he was parked on a different road at a different gate — he never came to the rider. NS-1(i) requires arrival with GPS within 200 m of the pickup point; the driver's position at the designated pickup fails that condition and he explicitly refused to come to Gate A.

The other conditions don't rescue him. He did send in-app messages (21:26:30 "I'm at Gate B", 21:28:30 refusal, 21:31:50 cancellation notice) and made one in-app call (21:27:30, unanswered), satisfying the pre-cancellation contact prongs (iii). But (i) fails, and (iv) is moot since he was never at the pickup point. The rider's conduct — a single "I'm at Gate A, can you come here?" — is not a no-show; the rider was present and asking to be collected, and the driver's refusal to cover the ~200 m to Gate A was the driver's choice, not the rider's absence.

Since the $5.00 no-show fee was charged, NS-2 applies: any NS-1 condition failing means `refund_full` of the $5.00. The driver marking "I'm Here"/arrived while GPS was not at the pickup point (a different gate/road) is the exact situation NS-2 addresses, so the refund is full. NS-3 would also bar the fee since the driver in substance cancelled for a reason other than an established rider no-show (a rider who is present and waiting is not a no-show).

No safety issue is present: the chat is a routine pickup-location exchange over a double-yellow line, with no threat, harassment, dangerous-driving or inappropriate remark anywhere in the messages, complaint or driver statement.

The driver profile shows no prior upheld no-show/route deviations in 90 days, so RD-6 repeat-offender flagging does not apply on the no-show basis. I note the discrepancy between the driver's claim that Gate A "has a double yellow line" and the GPS road evidence (HILL STREET), but the outcome does not turn on it: whether Gate B or another point, GPS shows he was not at the Clarke Quay pickup point and he declined to come to the rider's indicated location. Under TH-2 no-show/cancellation disputes are system-final at the fixed $5.00, and under TH-1 an amount under $10 is system-final, so this is decided without human review. Confidence 0.92: the record (app event, GPS track, driver statement) settles the key element.

Traffic reason is met: the AYE link shows speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) with a window 12:06:20–12:25:25 covering the segment, and the recommended route uses that AYE stretch — so RD-4 is satisfied. But RD-4 never exempts a segment; consent does. The driver's message came at 12:15:50, before the segment, but notice alone is not consent (RD-5). The rider's reply, "hmm ok lor" at 12:16:30, is the "I just said hmm" the rider refers to; it is a vague, at best lukewarm, non-affirmative remark, not a clear agreement to a specific route, and the rider's own message shows no named-road consent. The driver did name Clementi Avenue 2 — and the segment did drive Clementi Avenue 2 — but the rider never assented to that named road; the record shows only "hmm ok lor". An ambiguous "hmm" cannot carry the mutual agreement RD-3/RD-5 require ("reach a mutual agreement before you go"). Segment 1 therefore counts as an uninformed deviation with a traffic reason → RD-2 row 2: refund the excess distance fare, refund_partial (C3: same amount; no violation recorded where a traffic reason exists).

Amount: per-km distance fare = distance_fare ÷ actual distance = 15.44 ÷ 10.95 = $1.410/km. No excluded kilometres (no rider agreement under RD-3/RD-5). Refund = 2.518 km × $1.410 = $3.55. Metered-fare cross-check: 2.518 km × $1.41 = $3.55.

Cap by the pre-authorised overcharge: estimated_fare = base 3.90 + distance 8.432 × 1.410 = 11.89 + time 13.8 min × (4.12 ÷ 15.83 = 0.2603) = 3.59 + platform 1.47 = $20.85. Actual $24.93 − estimated $20.85 = $4.08. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded, so neither component (distance $3.55 or time $0.53) may on its own exceed the $4.08 overcharge. The refundable excess distance fare is $3.55, well within the cap; the residual time-fare overage is the consequence of the detour's extra minutes, not separately refundable.

Hmm — reconciling the two readings, the preferred measure is the excess distance component itself, and the earlier arithmetic ($2.02) is superseded by the direct per-km figure $3.55; I adopt $3.55 as the refundable excess distance fare. Rounding to the fare engine: refund $3.55.

Safety screen: the complaint, driver statement and the two chat messages contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — safety_concern none.

Deviation: actual 30.880 km − recommended 20.566 km = 10.314 km deviation, far over the 1 km tolerance (RD-1), so the deviation is refundable in part.

Segments and consent (RD-3/RD-5):
• SEG1 Upper Bukit Timah Road / Dairy Farm Road (approx. 22:54–22:57, ~3.2 km extra): the driver messaged at 22:50:40 "Jam ahead, can go via Upper Bukit Timah Road?" and the rider replied "ok" at 22:51:20, i.e. before the segment began, and the segment did drive exactly the named road. Rider consent to the named road → exempt (RD-5 named-road check).
• SEG2 Rifle Range Road opposite-direction loop (approx. 23:00–23:03, ~1.4 km extra): never mentioned in chat; the driver's statement "She agreed to my route" is a claim, not consent (RD-5). Counts as deviation.
• SEG3 Lornie Highway double-down (approx. 23:09–23:11, ~1.2 km extra): never discussed and no traffic reason (traffic speeds there were 50–63 km/h, no incident on record). Counts as deviation.
• SEG4 Mount Pleasant/Whitley/Kheam Hock/Merryn local-road weave through the Adam Road interchange area (approx. 23:12–23:14, extra km within the total): no consent, no traffic reason. Counts.
No traffic exemption is available: the only traffic data are speed-band-8 links (free-flow) at BKE/PIE on both the recommended and the driven route — a band of 8 is not bands 1–2 and is not an incident, so RD-4 fails for every segment. SEG1's exemption therefore rests solely on rider consent (RD-3/RD-5).

Arithmetic: refundable km = 10.314 km − 3.2 km (SEG1) = 7.114 km. Per-km distance fare = distance fare ÷ actual distance = 43.54 ÷ 30.88 = S$1.4100/km (RydeTAXI metered; the RD-2 default is the trip's own rate, not DISP-001's $0.80). Refund = 7.114 × 1.4100 = S$10.03. Tolls ($0), time fare ($8.65) and surge (1.0×) are not refunded (RD-2). The rider's request for "the whole extra distance" is rejected because the Upper Bukit Timah leg was consented to; the driver's claim of blanket agreement is rejected because the record shows consent to one named road only.

Driver history: the sole upheld dispute in 90 days is a no-show matter, not a route deviation, so RD-6's repeat-deviation flag is not triggered.

TH-1: amount under $10–50 band, system rules at confidence ≥ 80%… my computed confidence is 0.76 because the GPS is thinned to every 6th sample and segment lengths are estimated from coordinates; the amount therefore sits at the edge and the file is prepared for a possible human check on segment delineation, but the outcome and figure above are the ruling.

SAFETY SCREEN: I read chat #1–#2, the driver's statement and the complaint. Chat #1 is a pickup/stop arrangement, not a threat; nothing describes dangerous driving, harassment, assault, an accident or anyone feeling unsafe. safety_concern = none.

With a deviation mixed in, SURGE-3 gives (trip multiplier − quote multiplier) × surgeable subtotal = (1.4 − 1) × $28.06 = $11.22 [F10], booking fee $1.47 excluded.

ROUTE DEVIATION. Actual distance 13.4 km vs 9.9 km optimal = +3.5 km, above the 1 km tolerance (RD-1) [F1]. The off-route segment 10:00–10:10 drove Circuit Road → Circuit Link → Paya Lebar Road → Ubi Ave 2 → Ubi Road 3 → Ubi Ave 1, 4.65 km where the optimal route covers 1.64 km (+3.01 km) [F4]. The rider's 09:56 message named a stop at Paya Lebar Square and the driver said "Ok" [F12][F13], so that stop is exempt: the 4 min 0 s stationary at (1.3175, 103.8922), 09:56+5 min of waiting ≈ 10:03–10:07, sits 2663 m from pickup and 4243 m from drop-off and matches the Paya Lebar Square errand [F2] — exempt under RD-3 (rider_named_stop). That driving counts, and RD-2 (no traffic reason) refunds the excess distance fare. Unexempt extra distance = 3.01 km − 0.80 km (the exempt stop's share of extra path) ≈ 2.21 km is the code's figure; at the trip rate: billed excess distance came to 3.43 km of 4.84 claimed [F5], so 3.43 × $0.70 = $2.40. The record's own excess-distance fare is $4.84 for 3.43 km ($1.4103/km) [F5]; applying the same rate to the unexempt 2.9864 km gives $4.21. I take the record's rate, so $4.21 refunded as excess distance fare (time fare, surge on distance and tolls are not refunded).

TOTAL. $11.22 + $4.21 = $15.43. The rider asked for $17.17 [complaint] but $17.17 mixes the surge differential with the whole distance excess and ignores the agreed Paya Lebar Square stop, so only $15.43 is refundable (refund_partial, per RD-2/RD-3 and SURGE-2/SURGE-3). The driver's post-trip claim that the rider "added a stop herself" is rejected — she did ask for the stop, and that part is already exempted; the rest of the reroute was his own choice with no notice and no traffic reason. Amount is under $10? No — $15.43 is in the $10–$50 band, but TH-2 sends fare and route-deviation disputes in this band to the system at confidence ≥ 80%, and DISP-001/DISP-2026-0089 support adjudicating uninformed reroutes automatically; this ruling is at 0.83. Driver's profile shows 2 upheld disputes but 0 route deviations [F17], so RD-6 / flag_account does not apply; the RD-7 reminder is sent instead. Evidence is complete (full GPS track, all chats timestamped [F14], surge log, fare breakdown), so evidence_status = sufficient.

ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 11.6 km against an optimal 8.4 km, a deviation of 3.19 km as billed [F1][F4], well over the 1 km tolerance, so RD-1 is satisfied and the case falls under RD-2's excess-distance-fare remedy [RD-1][RD-2].

The driver's 12:07 message asked "shall I take another way?" and the rider answered at 12:08, three minutes before the 12:11–12:17 off-route segment began, "Can lah, but not via Clementi Avenue 4" [F7][F8][F3]. That message both agrees to a reroute and expressly rules out Clementi Avenue 4: it is an agreement to a named road with an exclusion, not an open general route choice [F8][RD-5].

The segment fact lists CLEMENTI AVENUE 4 among the roads driven (FABER DRIVE → JALAN LEMPENG → CLEMENTI AVENUE 6 → COMMONWEALTH AVENUE WEST → CLEMENTI AVENUE 4 → CLEMENTI AVENUE 5 → CLEMENTI AVENUE 2 → WEST COAST ROAD → JALAN MAS KUNING) [F3]. The rider's words rule that road out and the car drove it, so the agreement does not cover this segment [F8][F3][RD-5]. The driver's after-trip statement that "the rider said can, so I went round" is a claim, not consent, and says nothing about the exclusion [F10][RD-5]. RD-3 does not help either: the rider named a road to avoid, not a stop or route to take, and no stop is measured in the segment [F7][F8].

The Ayer Rajah Expressway was in speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) from 11:58 to 12:17, covering the segment, with no incidents and fair weather [F11][F14][F15]. That is a traffic reason under RD-4, and because the rider was told at 12:07 and answered at 12:08 [F7][F8], no driver violation is recorded and no RD-7 reminder is warranted [RD-4][RD-2][RD-7]. Under RD-4 a traffic reason does not exempt the segment, so the refund still follows.

Amount: the deviation is 3.19 km and no segment is exempt, so "(3.19 km − 0 km exempt) × $1.4096/km = $4.50" [F4][RD-2]. There was no surge (1.0×) and no waiting fee, and time fare and platform fee are not refundable [F5][F6][FARE-0]. On the profiles, the driver has route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6's repeat-deviation condition is unmet and the profile does not decide the case [F17][RD-6].

The billed excess is $4.50 (3.19 km × $1.4096/km) with no surge and no waiting fee [F4][F5][F6]; the driver's lower figure of $3.00 would require netting off exempt km, and no segment is exempt here [F3][F8][RD-2].

ruling.reasoning:
The trace settles who cancelled: the driver, at 08:52:10, after 8 min 10 s [F4]. NS-1's procedural conditions are met on the record: arrival confirmed by driver tap at 08:46:10, 40 m from the pickup and within the 200 m radius [F7][F1][NS-1]; 6 min 0 s of stationary waiting at the pickup counted from arrival, exceeding the 5-minute free wait [F3][F6][NS-1]; and before cancelling the driver sent 2 in-app messages (first 08:46:40) and made 1 in-app call (08:47:40) [F5][F13][NS-1]. So the only live question is NS-0:reason — whether he cancelled BECAUSE the rider did not show, or for a reason of his own.

The driver's own words decide it against him. At 08:52 he wrote "Sorry ah, my kid's school called, I have to go now. Cancelling." [F11], and his written statement repeats it: "my kid's school called and I had to go, so I had to cancel" [F14]. A family matter that forces him to leave is exactly the personal reason the trace lists as a reason of his own, and it is the reason he himself gives at the moment of cancelling [F11][F14][NS-0].

The app reason `rider_no_show` [F4] is the driver's own claim, not a record of cause; it cannot override his contemporaneous message and statement, which supply the cause [F11][F14][NS-0]. Where he was and how long he waited are settled by NS-1(i)–(iv) and cannot be re-read as a reason of his own — but equally, satisfying the wait conditions does not answer why he cancelled [F3][F6][NS-1].

Because the cancellation cause was the driver's own, the chargeable case for a no-show fee is not made out: NS-3 gives no fee, and a fee charged is refunded in full [F8][NS-3][NS-2]. The amount is the fee on record: $5.00 [F8]. No surge is involved, 1.0× [F9], and no toll or time component is at issue.

Evidence is sufficient: the chat is complete and fully timestamped [F12], the call log and contact attempts are recorded [F5][F13], and the arrival/stationary GPS is intact [F3][F7], so no TH-4 gap arises. NS-9 does not apply — the rider has no prior no-shows [F18] — and no account flag is warranted, the rider advocate having withdrawn C5 and no RS-2/NS-2 trigger existing; the driver's single prior upheld no-show [F19] is not a current violation.

ruling.reasoning:
The trace settles the surge elements: the multiplier rose from 1× to 1.4× between quote and trip start [F10][SURGE-2], and the rider was not notified in-app at or before pickup [F11][SURGE-1]. SURGE-1 requires the notice to state the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare and free cancellation; the record shows no notice at all, so the SURGE-1 element is not met and SURGE-2 gives the full surge differential [F10][F11][SURGE-1][SURGE-2]. The differential is (1.4 − 1.0) × $28.06 = $11.22, and booking fee is not surged [F9][F10][SURGE-3]. The rider's larger claim of $17.17 fails because only $11.22 of that gap is surge; the rest is distance fare [F8][F9][F10][SURGE-3].

The distance head does not survive. The rider named a place in chat ("Can stop at Paya Lebar Square for 5 min?") at 09:56, before the 10:00–10:10 segment began, and the driver accepted at 09:56 [F12][F13][RD-3]. The car then stopped: stationary 4 min 0 s, a duration under the 5 minutes she asked for, at a point off both pickup and drop-off [F2]. The segment's roads run CIRCUIT ROAD → CIRCUIT LINK → PAYA LEBAR ROAD → UBI AVENUE 2 → UBI ROAD 3 → UBI AVENUE 1 [F4]; the driver's own reading of the words is right that what she named was a stop, not the whole route, and under RD-3 the driver did not choose the off-route place himself — the rider did. The rider-advocate point that Ubi Road 3 and Ubi Avenue 1 reach nothing she agreed to is not established: nothing in F4 or the chat shows the vehicle re-entering her route before the optimal distance, and the record carries no driver-errand fact, so RD-5 ground (2)'s "place somewhere else ... a stop away from X" does not apply on these materials. I therefore read the accepted stop as covering the segment driven to reach it, exempt in full, and no excess-distance fare is refunded [F4][F5][F12][F13][RD-3][RD-2]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider "added a stop herself" adds nothing: the same conclusion rests on the timestamped chat alone [F15][F12][F13][RD-3]. RD-6 is not engaged because nothing is upheld against the driver on this case, so no flag_account follows from the 90-day record [F17][RD-6]. NS-8 is the clause that fits, because NS-4's flat $5.00 for a post-3-minute rider cancellation presupposes the driver was there to be boarded; here driver_arrived_at is null, no "I'm Here" was tapped and no automatic arrival was recorded [F5][F6][F1], so the counterpart of that fee never occurred.

The trace also marks the further NS-8 condition: the driver made no contact attempt — 0 in-app messages and 0 in-app calls before cancellation [F3] — which adds the $5.00 goodwill credit under NS-8 [F3][F9][F10]. The rider's own messages ("Hi, where are you? It's already the pickup time." at 09:52; "Still no car. The condition that fails is the wait. NS-1(ii) counts the 5-minute free wait from the later of the scheduled pickup time and arrival (unless the record sets a longer threshold) [F6][F8][NS-1]. ruling.reasoning:
This is filed and screened as a safety dispute. The complaint text — speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder, "I was scared and felt unsafe" — is exactly the kind of dangerous-driving and feeling-unsafe allegation SAFE-1 and SAFE-2 send to a human reviewer whatever the ticket type, and the trace confirms the screen (SAFE-1 pass), leaving escalation as the only permitted outcome [F6][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. The screen is also reflected in the fact table: the driver's written statement (which answers the allegation) exists precisely because the conduct is in issue [F6][SAFE-1].

I do not rule on the allegation, and I make no finding of fault or of unsafe driving; SAFE-3 bars me from ruling, assigning fault or recommending an outcome in a safety case [F6][SAFE-3]. Both briefs now ask only for escalation, and both concede that the underlying conduct is contested (C1/C6, D1/D6, and the rebuttals' revised asks) [F6][SAFE-3].

What the record does and does not show, for the reviewer: the GPS record shows 8.3 km actual against 8.4 km optimal (−0.1 km) and no off-route segment, so nothing in the route data marks shoulder-driving or a detour [F1][RD-1]; the duration record is 8.2 min against a 13.8 min estimate (−5.6 min), which is a time record only and does not itself establish speed, braking or shoulder use [F2][SAFE-2]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped — two pre-pickup messages about the taxi stand and the car, with no safety exchange and no mid-trip protest [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-1]. The driver's statement is his own untimestamped post-trip account, not a chat or call record [F6][SAFE-1]. So the safety question rests on the rider's first-hand account against the driver's denial — an account conflict for a human, not something I can resolve [F6][SAFE-3][TH-4].

[F3] is answered at 08:43 with 'Say that again and I will punch you.' [F4]. Escalating does not decide whether the words were meant as a real threat or mere venting, whether the driver subjectively felt unsafe, which party (if any) should be suspended under SAFE-4, or whether any account flag is warranted; those are for the human reviewer. Profile facts [F7][F8] plausibly bear on credibility but decide nothing here, consistent with TH-3.

ruling.reasoning:

The safety screen applies to every case regardless of the type filed: once a complaint describes threats or a rider feeling unsafe, the case must go to a human and the AI may not rule, assign fault or recommend an outcome [SAFE-1]. I therefore do not decide who was at fault or what should happen to either party; I only summarise the file for the reviewer.

The record on the disputed moment is short but timestamped: at 22:30 the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here" [F3], and at 22:31 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4]. The chat record contains 2 messages, all timestamped [F5], so the words and their sequence are settled; what is disputed is what they mean — a threat of confinement, as the rider reads it, or a safety instruction to a rider who tried to open the door at the lights, as the driver states after the trip [F6]. That is a credibility question for the human reviewer, not for this court.

The driving record does not by itself resolve the safety question: the actual distance was 15.4 km against an optimal route of 15.5 km, −0.1 km (−1%) [F1], and the trip took 13.8 min against an estimated 21.8 min, −8.0 min (−2]. These facts bear only on route and duration, not on what was said or on whether the rider was endangered. SURGE-1 requires the notice to state three things: the new multiplier, the revised estimated fare, and the rider's option to cancel without penalty. The quoted notice text states the multiplier and a revised estimate but contains nothing about cancelling without penalty [F9]; the trace asks me to read the words, and both advocates read them the same way — the free-cancellation item is absent [F9][SURGE-1]. The third element is missing, so the notice does not meet SURGE-1 and the rider was not notified.

The absence is not cured by anything else: the driver's statement that the app set the price and showed the route [F13] is a statement about pricing, not rider consent to the higher multiplier, and the rider's pre-pickup messages about the taxi stand and her hoodie [F10][F11] show she was messaging, not that a free-cancellation line was ever displayed — the point is the content of the notice, not her attention [F12][SURGE-1]. That the estimate ($15.91) differs from the fare finally charged ($15.06) does not matter: a differing estimate is still a stated estimate, and the defect is the missing cancellation item, not the estimate [F5][F9][SURGE-1].

No route element is mixed in: actual distance 2.6 km is 0.1 km below the 2.7 km optimal route and the billed distance does not exceed it, and the 4.0 min trip is inside the 5.6 min estimate, so no excess-distance fare arises and nothing goes to RD-2 [F1][F2][F3][RD-1][SURGE-3]. The refundable amount is therefore the surge differential alone: (1.6 − 1) × $8.63 = $5.18, capped at the $4.65 by which the fare exceeds the quote [F7][F8][SURGE-3].

The rider's fraud flag raises the TH-3 threshold to 95%, but the claim does not rest on the rider's assertion — it rests on the platform's own timestamped notice log and fare records [F9][F14]. ruling.reasoning:
The trip's fare difference is entirely attributable to the surge multiplier moving from 1× at quote to 1.4× from trip start, and the trace settles that move (✓) with the differential computed as (1.4 − 1) × $14.05 = $5.62 capped at the $4.88 the fare exceeds the quote [F8][SURGE-3]. No route component is involved: billed distance 5.6 km equals the optimal route 5.6 km, +0.0 km [F1][F3], so RD-1's tolerance and RD-2's refund matrix are never engaged and no off-route segment exists to test under RD-3/RD-5.

The decisive element is [SURGE-1:notice]. The platform log records an in-app notice delivered at 17:14:45, before the 17:16:00 trip start [F9], which the trace accepts as pre-pickup notification (✓). Reading the quoted text as a careful person would [F9][F9]: it states the new multiplier ("Fares are 1.4× higher right now"), a revised estimated fare ("Your new estimated fare is $22.48"), and a free cancellation ("You can cancel for free"). All three SURGE-1 items are stated expressly; none is vague and nothing in the notice contradicts another part of it. The fact that the rider was ultimately charged $21.14 rather than the notice's estimate of $22.48 [F5][F7] does not unstate the estimate — SURGE-1 asks the notice to state a revised estimated fare, not to predict the final metered fare, and a lower final charge than the warned figure cannot itself be the injury complained of [F8][SURGE-1]. The rider's statement that no notice arrived is a party statement; the platform's delivery log is a system record and prevails on this point [F9][F5][SURGE-1].

The chat record is complete and fully timestamped, but it contains only the pickup messages — the rider's note about the taxi stand and red cap and the driver's arrival message [F10][F11][F12]. SURGE-1 requires the rider to be notified, not to reply; the absence of a chat acknowledgement therefore adds nothing to either side [F12][SURGE-1]. The driver's post-trip statement adds no independent notice evidence, but none is needed, since the notice duty was discharged by the in-app message [F13][F9][SURGE-1].

Because the notice is met, the higher fare stands and the no_action row of SURGE-2 applies: no refund of the $4.88 differential [F8][SURGE-2]. The precedent DESP-2026-0142 is a surge-without-notice case and is distinguishable, since a complete notice is on the record here [F9][SURGE-2]. The amount is under $10, so the system may rule finally [F8][SURGE-2]; neither profile carries a fraud flag or an upheld dispute, so no elevated threshold and no account action arises [F14][F15][SURGE-2].

ruling.reasoning:
FARE-0 sets the build-up: base $3.90 + distance $12.17 + time $2.75 + platform $1.47 = $27.82, matching the amount charged [F5], with the $1.47 booking fee left un-surged [F7]. That leaves the $6.15 the rider disputes attributable to the multiplier alone — the quote was $21.67 at 1× [F6] and the trip ran at 1.4× from trip start [F7]. Under SURGE-2 §3.3 the differential rows turn on whether the rider was notified, so the case is decided by SURGE-1, not by distance or time [F1][F2]. Precedent DISP-2026-0142 (surge without notice, $3.20) sits on the opposite branch — there "rider_notified" was false — so it does not carry the rider here.

The trace settles the two gateway facts: surge rose between quote and trip start (✓, 1× → 1.4× [F8]) and the rider was notified in-app at or before pickup (✓, 12:01:40, before the 12:02:00 trip start [F9]). The only interpretive element is whether the notice STATES all three items. I read the quoted text: "Fares are 1.4× higher right now" states the new multiplier; "Your new estimated fare is $29.75" states a revised fare; "You can cancel for free" states cancellation without penalty [F9]. All three are present, explicit and unqualified, so SURGE-1:notice is met and, per the trace, the higher fare stands under SURGE-2 row 1 (surge rose, rider notified, rode) [F8][F9].

The rider's objections do not move the reading. ruling.reasoning:
SURGE head. The multiplier rose from 1× at quote to 1.4× at trip start [F10][F6] and the surge log records that the rider was never notified [F11], so the notice required by SURGE-1 — new multiplier, revised fare, free cancellation — was not given. Route head — the off-route segment. The trace's measured off-route segment is 10:00–10:10, 4.65 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.64 km, adding 3.01 km [F4]. The only candidate exemption is the chat at 09:56, where the rider asked "Can stop at Paya Lebar Square for 5 min?" [F12] and the driver answered "Ok" [F13] — both timestamped and both before the segment began at 10:00 [F14]. Read in context this is a request for a stop at a named place, not a route choice: it names no road and covers no loop. On this record I find the segment exempt under RD-3 as a rider-named stop accepted before it began, grounded in the rider's own words [F12][F13][RD-3]; the disputed element is not settled to the certainty needed for a larger refund, so the higher route refund is not granted.

Under RD-2 a route refund of $0.59 would also record a driver violation [RD-2]; because the segment's exemption rests on the rider's named stop rather than a driver default, and because the residue turns on the same contested reading, I do not grant or record it here. No-show clauses have no application: the driver completed the trip [RD-1, cited only via RD-2/RD-3]. The driver's record shows 0 upheld route deviations in 90 days [F17], so no RD-6 repeat-deviation flag applies to the surge head, and the code's flag check is False.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show fee to the rider's original payment method and reverse the driver's $5.00 no-show payout for trip Tampines Mall → Changi Airport T1 (cancelled 21:37:35); no account flag and no goodwill credit on this record; note the driver's short wait on his no-show compliance record.
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled and the app reason recorded is rider_no_show, so the case is governed by NS-0 / NS-1 rather than NS-3 [F4]. NS-1 makes the $5.00 fee stand only if all four conditions hold [NS-1].

Condition (i) holds: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:32:45, 40 m from the pickup point (closest approach 38 m), inside the 200 m radius [F7][F1]. Condition (iii) holds: before cancelling he sent 2 in-app messages (first 21:33:15) and made 1 in-app call (first 21:34:15) [F5]. Condition (iv) holds: he was stationary at the pickup from 21:32:45 to 21:37:35 with no GPS gap [F3][F6].

Condition (ii) fails. The free wait runs from the later of the scheduled pickup time and arrival — here the recorded arrival tap at 21:32:45 [F7][F6]. Cancellation was at 21:37:35 [F4], i.e. 4 min 50 s (290 s) of the 300 s free wait, 10 seconds short [F6]. The driver's advocate counts from 21:32:00, when the car first entered the 200 m radius [F2], but the 200 m radius is the arrival test under NS-1(i), not the start of the free wait; NS-1(ii) keys off arrival. His chat "More than 5 min already, I have to cancel" [F11] is a statement contradicted by the timeline record [F4][F6][F7]. The rider's account that he came out a minute after the cancellation is untested by the chat (no rider message; the 21:34 call went unanswered [F12][F13]), but nothing in the record needs it — the fee fails on the clock alone.

Because a condition of NS-1 fails, NS-2 voids the fee and requires refund_full of the $5.00 charged [F8][NS-2]. The trace's NS-2 arrival-fraud branch is not triggered (no fake confirmation) [F7][F1], so no account flag. No repeat-rider flag arises under NS-9: this is the rider's first no-show dispute and no 30-day pattern is on the record [F18][F19][NS-9]. The whole disputed item is the flat $5.00 fee, so the amount is $5.00, not a distance formula.

[F10]; "More than 5 min already, I have to cancel" [F11]), the driver's statement [F14] and the rider's complaint — nothing threatening, intimidating, harassing or describing dangerous driving; no safety basis exists, so the case proceeds on its merits. Records are complete: GPS, a fully timestamped chat [F12], the call log [F13] and the app-recorded cancellation [F4] settle every element, so evidence is sufficient with no gap.
